title: WOW!
text:
I used to own a pair of Sennheiser noise cancellation headphones but they were getting old and falling apart. I like the BOSE but they are way too spendy (which is why I think they are so heavily marketed). The Jabras are very comfortable to wear and even without the noise cancelling feature, they block a lot of sound. When I turn them on, background noise dissappears and the music from my palm pilot gets a bit louder (I suspect there's some amplifying circuity built in). This is a very handy feature becasue with my old headphones, I had to crank the volume on my device and it was never enough. I like how the headphones can still be used to listen to music even when noise cancellation is off (and the battery is removed). I also like the removable audio cord (you can wear the headset without listening to music and not have dangling wires). It comes with two sized cables, lots of adapters, and a nice sturdy case. The headphones seem to be well constructed and are lightweight.

Only negative is when I turned off the music, I could hear a radio station playing lightly in the left earpiece. But it's not a factor when music is playing or when I remove the audio cable (I guess it's like an antenna).

title: Does the trick and more
text:
I bought these because I was taking my wife and daughter on a long trip from Honolulu to Washington D.C. and wanted to add as much comfort as I could to the flights. Actually, I first bought a pair of sale-priced Maxell NC-II headphones to see what the noise-cancellation was like and whether it was worth it. Yep, it did seem like it would make a difference. There were three of us, so I needed two more. Researching the different models available, I became very curious how much better the more expensive models were, so what I did was buy another sale-priced Maxell, and then succumbed to my curiosity for the third. I figured it might be nice to have a better headphone for home use too. My research pointed at three price levels for noise-canceling headphones, with the Bose at the top, a variety around the $100 price range, and the lower price range with the Maxell and a Sony I found in the stores. The Sony was definitely out of the question because they were not the cup design that covered the complete ear. I wanted to spend money on the lower range of the mid-priced models, and I narrowed it down to either these Jabra C820S or the Logitech Noise Canceling model. The Logitech were cheaper than the Jabra by an amount significant enough that I was close to buying them instead. Reviewers seemed mostly pleased with the Logitech's sound quality. The raves were about equal to the Jabra on that issue. There was one factor that made me go for the more expensive Jabra. Many of the reviewers for the Logitech model complained that the Logitech model could easily break at the swivel joint, and some complained that they even arrived in the package already broken, so why risk that, I thought.

I'm very happy with the Jabras. They do the trick quite nicely. The noise cancellation is noticeably better than the Maxells. I let my daughter use the Jabras on the plane and she fell asleep with them easily. The detachable cord is a significant factor to consider. Fall asleep on the plane, roll over in the wrong way, and you could be putting a strong tug on that cord. Even more so, I used the Jabras while I was on a treadmill at the hotel, and many times my swinging hand came down and knocked the cord right out of its connection to the phones. For what we wanted in the airplane situation, the Maxells worked fine for me and my wife, despite not having detachable cords, but I doubt I'll ever be using them at home. The Jabras have good enough fidelity when the noise canceling feature is on that they also make nice phones for personal stereophonics. With the noise canceling off, the fidelity drops significantly, but you know, so what? If you want to listen to music, you're better off with the outside noises canceled anyway. A true audiophile might complain about a slight hiss from the noise cancellation feature, but it's not noticeable for me.

The case the Jabras come with is nice and sturdy. It's a little nuts in the way it can completely zip apart. I can't think of why they designed it that way. If you zip it completely apart, its a little tedious putting the zipper back together, but if you're conscious of what you're doing, you'll remember not to unzip the whole way. The truth is, though, the Maxells fold up nicer into a smaller ball which I prefer--makes it fast to put them away when you're through with them. The Jabras, though, are definitely a much better headphone. Now I've got one decent set of headphones connected to my computer, and two sets of Maxells in storage waiting to accompany them on our next trip.

Note: At the time I bought these, the Logitechs were everywhere selling cheaper. Right now they're significantly more expensive than the Jabras on Amazon. There are such huge differences in list prices and street prices on these things and prices fluctuate often. Buyer beware.

title: Good headphones
text:
Above average sound and build quality.
Bought these based on reviews that said they were almost as good as the Bose equivalent models (but cheaper). Sound quality is very good. With the noise cancelling on the sound quality reduces slightly along with an increase in bass and volume. There is a low level hissing sound with Noise Cancelling turned on, however it's not too annoying and wouldn't be noticeable in a noisy environment such as a plane anyway.
The Noise Cancelling is very effective at reducing constant noise like jet engines. Other sounds are reduced but not entirely (takes the edge of them). As these are "over ear" headphones (like earmuffs) they passively reduce outside noise anyway. Your ears can get warm as they are fully enclosed within the headphones muffs, but are comfortable.
Comes in handy tuff zip case with enough room for an iPod Classic and USB cable. Various adapters are included as standard with the headphones.

title: Can't wear for long
text:
The over-the-ear loop is great and the are secure when exercising. However, the buds themselves are a hard plastic with no "cushion". After wearing them for a short time, my ear canals were pretty sore. I am disappointed with these overall.

My wife bought a different set of Skullcandy earbuds- same over the ear loop BUT the buds are covered in a soft vinyl/plastic material with just enough give to cushion your ear canal. She has no trouble wearing hers for extended periods. If you look in the picture of these, you can see the black band around the silver speaker. That black plastic band is rigid plastic and unforgiving on your ears.

If these had some kind of cushion around the buds, I'd rate them 5 out of 5 stars. As they are, 1 star. I wish that I'd known how uncomfortable they are.

title: What is with the left bud?!
text:
This is the second pair of Skullcandy Chops I've owned. My brother was given a pair as a gift, but he has a different set of headphones he loves, so he gave me the unused Chops, knowing my original iPod earbuds were falling apart. I liked the over the ear hangers, but the hard rubber rim around the actual speakers hurt the inside of your ear after extended use. God help you if you fall asleep with them on. Sound quality is poor. When the pair my brother gave me broke (couldn't get sound out of left speaker, loud crackling out of the right speaker after about a month's use) I had to use my original iPod earbuds and realized just how poor the sound quality was with the Chops.

My husband bought me a red and black pair for Christmas this past year. They cost $25. What a waste of money! The left speaker went out just like the first pair's did, only this time it happened within two weeks. Now I'm back to using the falling apart iPod earbuds until I can afford a nicer pair of hanging earbuds. Thanks for being all hype with low quality, Skullcandy!

title: Great sound, but with some quirks
text:
I will be the first to admit I am not a bona fide "audiophile" so so this review will not focus on any technical jargon or specifications, besides those are listed on the skullcandy website. First, These were bought as a replacement to my Sennheiser CX200 earphones that were left in a hotel room. As the package came, the first thing I noticed was not the earphones but the cool ballistic mylon case. It is round, with one side being mesh and the other being nylon, akin to the nylon cases that Oakley sells. the case zips closed, with a small mesh pocket to hold spare ear gels. The earphones also come with two other sets of silicone gels (large and small) and if you look closely they actually have small skulls on the gels themselves.

The earphones themselves look and feel durable. The color is not a pitch black but more of a carbon gray, and the crosshatching on the earbud helps to place and remove the earphones, providing the wearer does not have sausage-fingers. Once fitted, these are less comfortable than the CX200 Sennheisers. The body of the Titans are a bit wider, and that may cause light contact on some wearers ears, as it does mine. That aside, these are still worlds more comfortable than the stock ipod earphones.

The sound on the Titans is superb. I don't have selective enough hearing to tell a noticeable difference between these and my previous pair, but compared to the ipod headphones the bass is deeper and richer, yet the midrange and highs are still very complete. I certainly "hear" subtle musical parts of a song that aren't heard with a basic set of earphones through the entire range of sound. Most of my music selection is made up of 80's and electronic, however I can see where some listeners of hip hop would love this pair for the potential to boom bass. (Maybe different brands of headphones are better for different genres of music, but Im not going to blow out my budget to find out.)

Overall, the Titans get four stars because of the less than perfect fit. Also a cord keeper on the volume bar to help wrangle up some of that extra cord between the earphones and the music player would be nice. As I have not had these long enough to a review durability, my rating may change in the future. Still, a great package and a great pair of headphones, just be cautious for wearers with smaller ear canals.

title: Good construction, mediocre sound.
text:
I bough these headphones after my Creative EP-630 broke. These seemed to be much more durable, and got good reviews in terms of sound. Here are my thoughts:

Sound: Compared to the EP-630's, these are actually pretty bad. The sound is just not that clean and clear. It always feels like there is a little bit of interference, almost like white noise in the background. The bass is nice and strong, but the rest of the range is mediocre. Not as bad as the Marshmallow earbuds, but nowhere near as good as the Creative EP-630.

Construction: This is one thing I really liked about these. The buds themselves seem to be metal, and look pretty good, and feel solid. Everything is made in a simple style, but high quality. The chord seems to be rather strong, and does not tangle easily at all. I think these will definitely outlast my previous earbuds. The silicone tips fit pretty well: not too soft or too rigid.

Price: The construction of the earbuds fits the price. A lot of higher end models are not made as well as these are. The sound definitely does not. EP-630's, which are in the same range offer much better sound quality. Or you could go for the Sennheiser CX-300 (basically the same as EP-630, but they are the ones who actually own that design).

Overall, I think I will stick with these for now, despite the not-so-good sound. However, I would not consider buying them again in the future. Unless you just want something very robust, there are other better alternatives out there.

It always feels like there is a little bit of interference, almost like white noise in the background. The bass is nice and strong, but the rest of the range is mediocre. Not as bad as the Marshmallow earbuds, but nowhere near as good as the Creative EP-630.

Construction: This is one thing I really liked about these. The buds themselves seem to be metal, and look pretty good, and feel solid. Everything is made in a simple style, but high quality. The chord seems to be rather strong, and does not tangle easily at all. I think these will definitely outlast my previous earbuds. The silicone tips fit pretty well: not too soft or too rigid.

Price: The construction of the earbuds fits the price. A lot of higher end models are not made as well as these are. The sound definitely does not. EP-630's, which are in the same range offer much better sound quality. Or you could go for the Sennheiser CX-300 (basically the same as EP-630, but they are the ones who actually own that design).

Overall, I think I will stick with these for now, despite the not-so-good sound. However, I would not consider buying them again in the future. Unless you just want something very robust, there are other better alternatives out there.

title: I found a new best headphone in the sub-$50 range
text: For a long time I considered the Skullcandy Ink'd Buds the best headphones around for under $50, but when my pair broke on me a few months back (after three years of abuse), I decided to step up to these because the difference was only $10. I wasn't sure if they would be worth the money (the versions Skullcandy sells that fall between these and the Ink'd Buds have majorly disappointed in the past), but they are more than worth it. These quite literally blow my $130 Shure phones right out of the water, and are a considerable improvement on the already excellent Ink'd Buds. With the Ink'd Buds you always need a good break-in period (usually 20+ hours) before the highs loosen up and the sound becomes really enjoyable. These sounded smooth and rich right out of the packaging, and have only improved in the month since I got them. The bass is strong and solid but never overpowering, the highs are rich and clear, and the soundstage has excellent depth. The buds are comfortable, even though I got the plastic rather than foam tips, and the construction is rock solid. A coating on the cord cuts down some of the incident noise that all buds have on contact, and the inline volume control is excellent. Sometimes I wish for a little more sensitivity at the low end of the volume control (these phones are sensitive, and therefore I usually keep them at a very low volume so I don't blow out my hearing), but they sound great throughout the range regardless. If you're currently in the market for a new pair of headphones (and don't want to spend over $100), these should definitely be on your shortlist.

title: Surprisingly good
text:
I've had these for about 6 months. I did a lot of research online before buying these and was hesitant when I actually picked them up at the store--the packaging seemed kind of cheap and I was skeptical. I bought them anyway and was surprised by how well made they felt. They are gratifyingly heavy for their size and the polymer cap that fits into your ear seems durable and is very comfortable.

When I put them on, I was surprised by the sound quality and amount of noise reduction. The sound quality still amazes me. These have really good base and rich, full sound. I've had several pairs of headphones and these blow all of them away in quality. They are definitely competitive with headphones over twice the price. I didn't see any advertisement about noise reduction, but as soon as you put them in, the world becomes muffled, and once you turn on the music to a reasonable volume, nearly all outside noise is drowned out. It feels like walking around in a movie, where the scene volume is muted and the soundtrack is all that is heard. They don't amplify the sound of you breathing, either, as covering your ears would do.

The one thing it does amplify is the sound of the cord moving--it is an awful noise that becomes infuriating quickly. Any thumping at all on the cord is greatly amplified. The noise isn't as noticeable when I take them out running, especially if I wear the cord under clothes. It is most obnoxious when sitting still or walking and the cord is accidentally thumped. As annoying as I find this noise, it doesn't even come close to outweighing the pros of these headphones.

I have taken them out jogging and biking, and they are great in the wind, since most of the ear bud is in your ear canal. My old ear bud headphones forced me to crank the volume to the max to hear over the sound of wind. Not so with these. I've accidentally tugged the cord hard a few times while jogging and as a result, the sound sometimes begins to cut out if the cord is bent in just the wrong way. I am sure this would be the case with most headphones, however, so I do not fault them for it. All in all, I love these and would buy them again immediately even if they broke tomorrow. For $50, I don't think these can be beaten.

Pros:
-Outstanding sound quality
-Very good noise reduction
-Comfortable fit

Cons:
-The sound of the cord moving around is loud and annoying

UPDATE!
After accidentally yanking the cord, the metal housing of the earbud snapped apart at the seam. I was able to snap it back together, but it didn't hold very consistently and it came apart a few more times. They still worked perfectly and I'll still keep them as a backup, but it was time to buy a new pair. The first lasted well over a year, if not two years. True to my word, I bought another pair of Titans. Here's what you get with newest version:
-Fancy packaging, and now says 'Hi-definition noise isolating ear buds'
-Different cord--this time it's braided aluminum (according to the package) and has a clear plastic sheath. It looks cooler, but functionally seems just like the last version. Relatively loud thumping sounds are still transmitted through the cord when it is bumped sharply.
-Black silicone earbud fittings instead of clear. There are 3 sizes. There is a significant difference in sound quality depending on the fit--definitely try out the different sizes to make sure you've got the right one.
-Still comes with a nice case.

Bottom line: I'm still very happy with these.

I called another time about using the headset to move to the next selection (which can't be done on an iPhone). Both times Jabra tech answered the call immediately and provided excellent help.

title: Good sound, but not for those of us with large...
text:
...heads. Yes, that roundish thing that caps off my body does me in yet again. But I'm stuck with it so what can I do?

I picked this up at a certain big box electronics store (fact is, they're about the ONLY big box electronics store these days). The Halo paired easily with my iPod Touch, T-Mobile G1 and Sony Walkman NWZ-A829. Its sound quality was quite good, both via Bluetooth and via the corded option, although the only way I could achieve this given the size of my noggin was to use both hands to press both earpieces against my ears to get them to position correctly for the best sound. Obviously personally looking akin to something out of Edvard Munch's painting 'The Scream' really isn't a workable solution for me or anyone else with a head close to my own's physical size. Which is a shame because Jabra otherwise has created a really nice, minimalist slick-looking LITTLE headset (a fitting irony in that last bit of description) that for the bulk of the population probably won't have any fitment issues. But as I lamented earlier I'm stuck with the head I've got so alas, this particular Halo sadly isn't ever again going to find itself around my scalp.

Other observations: Its rechargeable design is a definite plus. Its volume and track advance controls are rather touchy and seem to me to have a bit of a learning curve. The hinges for collapsing the earpiece sections during storage seem rather cheapish and fragile to me; I'd tend to question how long they would last with repeated folding actions, and although the obvious workaround is to leave then unfolded and ready for use most of the time...except that the only way to shut them off is to fold them closed.

title: Good, but hot
text:
As many others have said, the sound is great and the fit, though a bit tight for my big head, is comfortable. The main problem is that it does make my head sweaty. Granted, I'm a bit hot-blooded and sweat easily, but the warmth of these headphones worries me because I live in Japan and walk/take the train to work. Once it starts getting hot here, I'm worried my headphones will be exceedingly uncomfortable.

That being said, there aren't too many options and I tried the Motorola ones on. They were super uncomfortable, right from the get go.

I've had a few range problems as well, with the sound cutting out when the iPhone was in my pants pocket, although that seemed to go away or lessen with time. Weird.

One cool thing: the battery ran out yesterday and I pulled out the extra cord that came with the headphones and was able to use them without the Bluetooth functioning. Meaning, if you're on a long flight or can't recharge for a while, if you carry this cord with you you'll still be able to use the headphones.

By the way, I recommend Poddities ([...]) as a convenient way to carry your iPhone around your neck, especially helpful for commuters who walk/ride to work.

title: Great sound, but slips....
text:
This headset sounds superb. Whether it's music or a caller, the sound is crisp and exceptional. Pairing was easy and I paired my iPhone and another cell phone. The headset connects with both at the same time seamlessly. And when I use one phone, after I finish, I can get a call on the other. Haven't experienced getting a call on the other while using the one yet.

My only complaint is that the headset slips on my head. Almost lost it a few times when I tilted my head. Otherwise, it's comfortable enough. I can still hear the outside world which is what I want when driving (though I may be violating some traffic law having both ears blocked). The control button works just fine. And I have not had trouble with the volume slider. Not a problem at all for me. I like the tone to confirm a change.

The hinges seem solid enough. I have not found them to be a problem once I figured out how they work. To turn off you don't pull and bend, you just bend. To turn on you slide them in to each other.

The material lining the headset was comfortable enough, though it got a little warm at times....but not a big issue.

Overall this headset is great. Great sound, easy to use. Now if I had a thicker head of hair maybe that would solve my slipping issue. :)

You can't go wrong with this headset.

title: Great headphones for some purposes
text:
I don't like writing negative reviews - it makes me feel like I didn't research the product carefully enough. I did like several aspects of this product, but the negatives outweighed the positives for me, so I had to return it.

Here is what I was looking for in a headset:

1. Sufficient volume so that I can hear (I do have a hearing loss and wear hearing aids, so I need some gain!)

This criterion was met, no problem. Its volume is great. I'm not sure that I completely mastered the "touch" volume control in the short time I had it, but it appeared to work. You drag your finger along the front edge of the right ear-piece, and the volume goes up or down. I did NOT have the problem some reviewers have mentioned, that the volume is too high no matter what. If I drag my finger down on the volume control, it gets whisper quiet. But one person's whisper is another person's shout, so there you go.

2. No ear buds (because I wear hearing aids, and there's no place for an ear bud to go)

This criterion was met. The ear pieces definitely do NOT extend into the ear.

3. Compatibility with my Nokia E71x telephone.

This criterion was partially met. I had no problem pairing the Halo with my phone, but its connection would drop mysteriously. I sometimes could not get the connection to re-establish itself without rebooting the phone, which is not fun. This compares negatively to my Sony DR-BT30Q bluetooth headset, which I am currently replacing. The connection between the Sony and my phone was consistent, except when the battery in the Sony was in its death throws. After recharging the Sony battery, it would be fine.

Another compatibility issue was that I was not able to control the phone from the multi-use button on the Halo. I don't do that a lot with my Sony, but the few remote controls that I use (voice dial, answer), work fine.

4. Great sound while listening to audio books

This criterion was met. The sound was great while listening to audio books. I didn't actually use it to listen to music, but that probably would have been OK too. I didn't attempt to use the headset to control the sound playback, so I have no comment on that aspect, which seems to be of great interest to some reviewers.

5. Great sound while communicating on the telephone.

This was the biggest negative for me. The sound during telephone conversations was very bad - for me, and for the people with whom I was talking. It sounded like "being in a tunnel". Volume was fine, but it was just just very hard to understand. This compares very negatively to my experience with the Sony, which had excellent sound (coming and going) during telephone conversations.

6. Comfort while wearing the headset for long periods of time

This was fine. Comfort (and sound quality too, unless you're a sound engineer) is very subjective. I found this headset to be comfortable for a pretty long haul.

7. Ability to use it while exercising

I'm not too sure about this one. The headset worked fine during my exercise session: stayed put, great sound, comfortable. I don't wear my hearing aids during exercise, and the Halo put out enough sound for me to hear the audio book I was listening to.

The problem is that I sweat pretty profusely. I don't know if my perspiration could damage the set, but I do know that it was pretty darn wet - on the ear pieces and also under the "hair-band". The instructions say that limited use in light rain is OK, but that they are NOT waterproof, so one should take care. My perspiration might qualify as more-than-light rain.

8. Ability to use it while charging the battery.

This criterion was met nicely. You can charge the battery with a USB cable (though the one provided is too short to wear the headphone and charge at the same time - one would have to buy a longer cable from a third party. It's a standard mini-mini USB cable). Or you can charge the battery with a "travel" charger that plugs into the wall. Its wire is long enough to wear the headset and charge at the same time, if you're somewhere near an outlet.

You might ask, why am I replacing my Sony headset, if it's so great? That's what my wife asked me! Two reasons:

1) Its two ear pieces are connected with a retractable wire that goes behind the neck. That's fine (and actually gives me clearance to mop my bald pate during the aforementioned perspiration attacks), but my cat knocked the Sony off of my dresser some months ago, and now the retracto-mechanism is balky.

2) The Sony attaches to my ears with some plastic-coated spring-action wires. I find it difficult to attach the ear pieces rapidly, and they are not comfortable for long use.

A less important reason is that I think the Sony looks dorky, as compared to the Jabra Halo, which I felt looked real cool. How these things "look" is pretty subjective, however. And it's not a very important criterion compared to the other ones above.

I have ordered a Nokia BH-503 as a replacement for the Jabra Halo and will try it out. If it doesn't work out I'm going to try the more upscale Nokia BH-905.

title: Well, the 2nd one works great......
text:
O.K., I have a HTC Fuze, and I wanted a Bluetooth stereo headset to listen to my music player, and to take calls. So I went out and bought this one, because I hate ear buds, and I liked the design of it. Well the when I got home, and started syncing it up and using it, it acted really touchy and wierd. It wouldn't stay synced up to my phone and trying to adjust it to fit my head it would turn off and unsync. And it kept saying the battery was dead and shutting off.(I did get to work for a couple of hours,though.) So I took it back a couple of days later after playing with it. Making sure it was the headphones, and not me or my phone.

So now I got my second pair and they WORK GREAT!!! You can't beat the sound quality( I listen to drum and bass, old school rap, heavy metal.) And no matter what type of music it is, all of the channels are clear. And even if you have the volume turned all the way up there's no distortion of the bass. They also seem to hng my head pretty well, after fine tuning the sliders. Going between calls and your music it effortlessly, it pauses the music so you can take the call, and when you end the call goes right back and unpauses the music. Clarity on a call is once agaian awsome, can hear the person on the other side crisp and clear. And it has dual microphone so you can be heard without effort. You can sync up different devices at once with it too.

Now the bad,(which isn't much.)First it the volume control/ song skip buttons(or lack there of?)they're touch sensitive, meaning that there it really no physical buttons, you kinda touch/tap the area marked on the side of the right earphone. And the volume up, shares the same area for the song skip,(tap it once to increase the volume and double tap to skip the song.)this doubles for the decrease/song back area. Which can be a steep learning curve. I kinda of got it down, but there is plenty of times that I'll turn it all the way up trying to skip a song. Or I will be trying to turn it up only to toggle back and forth between turning it up and down. Some time I get no response from tapping it twice. So I end up pausing then unpausing the song(it the only physical button-the send/end call button.) Then double tapping, and that seems to do the trick. Once I turn off the headset( by closing them at the hinges,) and reopening them to turn on the headset my phone only reconizes that they're handfree bluetooth and not handsfree stereo bluetooth. So I have to manually go into my settings, and turn that on. They are also lined with crushed velvet on the inside, which can get a little hot. But I work in a building with no air conditioning in the summer, and the boilers makes feel like summer in the winter. And I must say that to some people this also might be a deal breaker, but I have worn many over the ear headphones,or ear protection in some really hot enviroments, and these really don't get all that hot.

In my opinion this is a great bluethooth stereo headset. There are some minor issues, but if you can get past the volume/song skip issue, and the crushed velvet making you hot, you will come to like this headset.

And I must say that to some people this also might be a deal breaker, but I have worn many over the ear headphones,or ear protection in some really hot enviroments, and these really don't get all that hot.

In my opinion this is a great bluethooth stereo headset. There are some minor issues, but if you can get past the volume/song skip issue, and the crushed velvet making you hot, you will come to like this headset.

title: Pretty things don't always perform as expected!!
text:
From the moment I first discovered these online I was in love with this sleek and stylish dream of a perfect headset. Unfortunately actually using them proved much more like a nightmare. While this headset is very visually stunning the performance leaves much to be desired. First and foremost, the headset does have a 30 foot range as advertised, but when you put it in your pocket (as I'm assuming that's where most people plan on putting their phones when they wish to utilize the features of a HANDS-FREE device) it constantly cuts in and out. I usually listen to calming music on my walk to and from school, but the constant blips make it even more frustrating than listening to the homeless people beg for change on the subway. It's a constant reminder of the very disc-man portable CD players that you had to stand stalk still with to use. My experience from the "noise canceling" microphone actually was the opposite, meaning the lovely people on the other end of my phone call could hear my cat breathing from the other side of the apartment!! Whoever wrote this description needs to get their hearing checked. Also IPHONE USERS BEWARE this device is not fully functionally with your iPhones!! The nifty volume control does work, but the track forward/back function is absent, it did however work with my Mac and is pretty nifty. As for the fit, the headset was constantly slipping off of my ears and onto my temples, which wouldn't be a problem if I could hear out of my temples. It would stay put on my head only when I was sitting still at home, but if I was trying to walk or turn my neck ever so slightly the headset would ride my silky smooth hair right off my head. The hinges that turned the device on/off felt very flimsy and kept bending the wrong direction!! YIKES!! Finally the battery life was not all it was cracked up to be, partially because the device would often stay on even when folded. Expect 6 hours period, not 6 hours of actual listening time. If I unplugged this device at 9 they would be dead by 3, only listening to music for the 20 min commute to and from campus. I encountered a stranger on the subway that had recently purchased and returned the Halo just the day before. He asked my humble opinion and completely agreed with almost every complaint.

In conclusion these are beautiful headphones and I received numerous compliments from friends, professors and complete strangers. Unfortunately I listen to music with my ears not my eyes and this experience was painful at best. I've said this about people for years and now I can easily apply it to this headset, when things are good to look at they don't have to perform as well because they're carried by their looks. Perhaps if these were made to function better I would repurchase them in the future, but for the time being I'm going to research a different model. :(

title: Took them right back for a refund
text:
Let me start be stating that the audio quality was acceptable, both for calls and music, but overall, the design is seriously lacking in the following respects:

1. The power switch is integrated into the headband hinge -a snap open, fold-and-slide affair that feels rather insubstantial and twice collapsed (inadvertently shutting down the radio) while in the process of taking the unit off my head.

2. Beyond the power switch functionality, the folding configuration provides no significant space savings. It's not as though collapsing these headphones will make them any less bulky in a laptop bag or purse.

3. The earpieces do not pivot or swivel at all -basically, if your head isn't a perfect fit (and mine isn't), they don't sit right on your ears and constanly slide off.

4. The software-based, touch sensitive volume control is a profoundly unreliable, counterintuitive gimmick. A hardware dial or rocker switch would have been much better.

5. The headband and earpieces are lined with some kind of synthetic velour that traps lint and fuzz admirably, but doesn't add to the comfort. And finally,

6. You can't control the tracks on an iPod Touch or iPhone 3G/3Gs with it. I know that's not Jabra's fault -that is a problem with Apple's current version of A2DP, so I don't consider it a knock on this product per se. I just mention it for the benefit of anyone planning to use these with one of those devices.

If you're really in love with the aesthetics of this unit, consider the Jaybird Sportsband. They're $10 cheaper, and they have basically the same features, but the earpieces adjust to the shape of your cabeza and you get real, tactile controls.

title: Very buy worthy
text: This is my third stereo bluetooth headset, and it's definitely the best. The fit is comfortable and can be worn for many hours at a time, and the sound is "full/bassy" but sacrifices a bit of mid/high tonal crispness (being a bit picky here considering the price). Charging it took bit of trial and error. It has to be locked open to charge, BUT if it has gone into sleep/standby mode then you have to unlock and relock it to charge. The locking mechanism is clever and looks like it should last, but only time will tell. For me personally, having the optional 3.5mm plug was a huge and pleasant surprise because I can plug into my silent guitar for practicing - a couple years ago I had looked long and hard for this feature (wireless with wired option) but didn't find anything. With regards to previous reviewers' complaints about it being loud even at minimum settings, I'm willing to bet almost anything that they just have to turn down the volume of the music source (iphone or otherwise). When I first used it with my phone, I thought they were right about it being too loud at min, but then I turned down the volume on the media player program, and problem solved.

title: Pleasantly surprised and happy with the product
text:
I was (admittedly) apprehensive about buying the Halo after reading the reviews here and on Cnet but have been pleasantly surprised by the product. I've been using them for a good part of the day to listen to music and take conference calls from my PC...it fits my head just fine without any issue (I must have the Jabra "standard" head shape!). Sound is okay for work listening and the folks on the other end of my VoIP calls have reported normal voice quality.

***UPDATED*** I'm now a few weeks on of daily use and continue to be happy with the Halo!

PROS
* The touch volume slider is convenient and reasonably sensitive - not a selling point but it works.
* Sound quality - not too bassy or trebl-y. These do a reasonable job of blocking out ambient "office noise"
* Voice quality - I've used these on Skype and my mobile and folks on the other end still report good quality

CONS
* The inner headphone lining does tend to grab a bit of fuzz (a minor annoyance)

title: Great set of stero headphones
text:
I bought my Jabra Halo's at Best Buy in case I wanted to easily return them. Turns out that the product is a keeper and I wish I would have purchased them at Amazon for about 23.00 less.

I purchased my Halo's to pair up with my Droid Eris to listen to music and as a phone headset. Sound from the Halo's is very good but using it as a phone head set the sound is awesome! You can answer and end calls with the button on the right side of the head set as well as access your music files just by pushing the button.

Inital bluetook pairing was quick and painless as well as re-connecting the head set. My bluetooth range is only about 10 foot which works ok for me. They say range is about 30 foot. I don't know if it is my Droid or the Halo or both that is limiting me to 10 foot.

I've had my Halo's for about 2 months and have not had any issues with the folding hinges, but I always feel like it is going to break or I am going to break one of them. So far so good on that.

The owners manual is weak on instructions. To charge the Halo's the right side must be in the locked position (not folded) and I have to press the button on the headset to start charging. I purchased a mini USB to micro USB adapter so that I can charge my Droid and the Halo's with my car charger. The longest I've worn them listening to music (Pandora) is about 3 hours and the battery held up well.

In summary after two months of daily use I would highly recommend the product.

title: Really nice stereo headphones
text:
I just got a imac and wanted bluetooth stereo headphones or headset to use with my imac and my ipad.
Do not care about cell phone use, just wanted a nice stereo wireless set for music and movies.
This Jabra Halo set is PERFECT!!! Most everyone else was suggesting the motorola S9 set. So I tried that first.
One word for the motorola S9...AWFUL!!! Had a terrible time pairing to my iMac. But worse, the S9 is heavy, bulky
and really unconfortable to wear. They drove me nutz. Could not stand that heavy tight wrap-around behind the head
on the S9. If you laid back in a chair, the S9 poked into my neck and really was so unconfortable...PERIOD.
So I returned them and got the Jabra Halo BT650s. About the only other option in wireless headsets for stereo and music use.
Well.. the halo set is soooo light weight. Like draping a scarf over your head. You don't feel it at all.
No... I guess I would not run or exercise with them because of the fit is not pressure tight (a good thing).
BUT... if you want a bluetooth great sound stereo headset, that easily paired to my iMac first try (unlike the motorola S9),
then this is the set to get.
I can not believe how good they feel on the head/ears. You could wear these all day and never have an issue.
Where the S9 gave me neck cramps after a few minutes. Like having popcorn stuck in your teeth, the motorola S9 drove me crazy.
The Jabra is like a draped scarf draped over your head. So nice!!!
And the sound is NOT too loud. Easily adjustable. Also, if using on a imac, in the iMac bluetooth settings you can further
adjust the volume there too, if needed.
Like I said, I do not use them for a cell phone or running/jogging. But for pc/mac use they are the only solution.
Great sound. Great fit. Great pairing. Great job Jabra...!

title: Product is too fragile
text:
I bought this in January to replace wired headsets for my iPhone, and it worked very well. I read all the reviews about flimsy hinges and the indicator lights not working as described, and yes - they are correct. However, even though the indicator lights do not do what the manual says, I had no trouble charging or pairing it to the iPhone. It stayed paired for weeks at a time, and only once in a while did I need to have the iPhone "forget" it and start over. The hinges thing is bad - I eventually stopped closing the left hinge, but the right hinge has to be closed to turn it off. If you are extremely careful about pulling the hinge out before folding, it might last a little longer.

The call quality on phone calls was excellent and worked flawlessly from audio to call. Volume control was a little iffy because you can't see your right ear to know exactly where you are going to touch it - you might accidentally do something you didn't intend. But generally I had little trouble with volume.

I loved this headset - really - and I was as gentle as I could be with it. But eventually the right hinge lost a piece of plastic, even though it continued to work. The headset also loosened a little, so that it became harder to keep it over my ears. Then, last week, it stopped sending a bluetooth signal (which you can see as the blue indicator light). I imagine the connector wire is probably damaged, and I'm looking for my warranty info now. I won't be surprised if they say I damaged it, since that piece of plastic broke off, so I'm not hopeful they'll repair or replace it.

I give it 3 stars - I loved it and want to give it 5 but hey, it costs too much, especially for only 8 months of service. That being said, don't buy it - it's too fragile.

title: Jabra Bluetooth Stereo Headset
text:
I bought this headset to use with my Samsung Epic Android phone. It appears to be the same as one sold by my carrier Sprint. The instructions are very inadequate and at first I thought mine was defective. However, after reading what other people had written on the net about the device I finally figured out how to get it opened and turned on and charged. To open/turn on the headset you pull the arms out and push them in at the hinge point. To close it you simply "bend" them closed. This makes a snapping sound that might cause you to think you have broken them. Not so, they are fine.
The "touch controls" on the right side are a bit difficult at first but they do work. The sound is very good. I do feel like they do not clamp as tightly to my head as I might like since I sometimes use them at the gym. Considering the Amazon price I think they are a good deal. They come from the supplier in a very plain box which makes me wonder how much we otherwise pay for the fancy box that would be used at a regular store ?

title: Exactly what I wanted
text:
I've been looking for wireless, bluetooth headphones and these one of the limited selection that I found that looks good.

So after extensive reviewing, I thought these were the perfect ones for me. I wanted something that would fit snug and comfortably over my head so I can lay down and listen to music without something on the back of my head, wirelessly.

I just picked up the new iPod Touch gen.4 and paired it to my new headset. I read reviews where the music control does not work but I guess Apple has updated their software and with the new iPod they do work!! It's great! Volume control is easy. Pausing songs was easy to control from the button on the side. Changing songs took some getting used to but doesn't work every time but it's a good option to have ontop of changing the song from your device. Controls were made well, I love the minimalistic look.

I have other bluetooth devices at home (laptop, Blackberry...etc) and seems like every 30 seconds the headset would stutter while I listened to my iPod. Seems like the other devices are interfering with the music and trying to pair. After the first few songs the "stuttering" went away.

Anyway, the headphones are exactly as they look. There should be no surprises if you did your research. The snap on and off is cool and not as easy to turn on/off as I thought. You have to actually open them up and snap them into place.

The standard micro USB charger is loose. You have to really have to make sure you plug it in and not move it around or else the charger will come out. This was using my Blackberry charger which also works. I haven't tried to use the charger that came with it because I didn't want to use up my limited plugs. Works fine and charges fast.

Anyway, if I find something else, I'll write another review but this is what I found after 20 mins of playing with it. I'm really happy with it. I think the sound is good enough for me. It doesn't cancel out all noise but I like to be able to hear a bit of the outside world in case someone needs to get my attention. Great device and I got it for $55 here on Amazon.com which is a great deal compared to the $129.99 original price.

text:
I've shopped around and tried out SOOOO many different stereo bluetooth devices. Most notably have been devices by Motorola and Plantronics. The specific model numbers elude me at the moment. The Motorola was nice, but cumbersome and the battery died after a few months. It had a band that went behind the head and was inflexible making it very uncomfortable to wear while leaning my head against anything such as the headrest in the car, or a pillow in bed. The Plantronics faired better, but the noise canceling wasn't very good.

I did it once by accident, and haven't been able to figure it out since.

Overall, the noise canceling is good, and the quality of the sound it produces is very good as well. The only reason I'm not ranking this more than 3 stars is because of how difficult it was to figure out, and the fact that I STILL can't get certain functions to work. Overall, I like this better than other products of this kind.

title: Good overall, but painfully tight for big heads
text:
These look really slick and I wish they had fit me. They fit my wife fine and they seem to be intended to keep all the pressure on your head and little to none on your ears. This works well for someone with an average to small sized head, but on my big head they were painfully tight over my ears even when extended all the way. They were particularly painful while wearing glasses.

Regarding the touch interface, it worked decently well for controlling the volume, but I could almost never get it to change tracks. Play/pause is controlled by a conventional button which worked well.

I liked the battery indicator on the inside of the head band. The mechanism for locking out the hinges was odd and felt fragile. The inside of the band is lined with a felt like material which picks up lint easily. Dandruff suffers and heavy hair gel users need not apply.

My house is in a densely packed subdivision with neighbors close on either side and we all use a lot of wireless tech, so I have a higher than normal amount of interference to contend with. These did ok with the interference, but not great. They suffered some minor interruptions (skipping and crackling) in the heaviest interference areas, but were generally usable with my iPhone 4.

Speaking of which, the iPhone 4 shows a battery meter for the headphones when they are on. Really slick. I wish all the blue tooth headphones would do that.

title: Could not get it to work
text: I received my first Jabra HALO from DB Roth. It didn't work (I charged it with: 1. the hinges folded, 2. the hinges opened (like they would be if placed on one's head), 3. with hinges fully extended, each for two hours and did each of these charging iterations with 1. the earpieces extended and 2. the earpieces not extended for a total of 9 different charging iterations of two hours each). The charge indicator never indicated (it flashed on and off green on the LED charge indicator light, but never was solid green as the indicated in the instructions...after each charging iteration, I tried to turn the unit on and pair it with at least one Bluetooth device after each charging iteration). It never indicated that it was on, and never tried to pair with any of several Bluetooth devices automatically as indicated in the instructions. I tried automatic pairing with: 1. hinges opened, 2. hinges closed, each with ear pieces fully extended and with earpieces extended and closed. I never figured out how to turn it on and the Bluetooth indicator LED never indicated anything. I also tried to turn it on using the call button as indicated for manual paring in the instructions (note that the call button, the hinges, the volume control and the earpiece extensions are the only things that you can change on this headset so it is pretty easy to try all variations...none worked). During this process I depressed the call button for longer than 4 seconds numerous times, as well as less than 4 seconds numerous times and it did not try to pair with anything nor did it indicate that it was on at all. The Bluetooth light never indicated anyting (ever). I called Jabra Tech Support and they tried to help me by running me through several iterations of the process described in the instructions, but nothing that they told me to do worked (and I had already tried everything that was suggested (see above). The Tech Support representative concluded that the unit was defective and said to send it back to the seller (DB Roth). DB Roth replaced it with another unit promptly (I have to pay for shipping). The replacement unit acted the same exact way and I sent that back as well (had to pay for shipping again!). I even tried to use the hardwired input (mini USB with mini RCA jack plug in)and it would not work. I would really like to see how the HALO works and hear how it sounds, but I gave up trying to make either unit work and was tired of spending about $20 in shipping and numerous hours trying to get this thing to work. Life is too short for that. I am sure that, when the HALO works, it is a good Bluetooth headset, but I could not get it to work and I suspect that this seller is selling defective product...Conclusion: Avoid this seller and this product! Subsequently, I purchased the MOTO ROKR S305 (4 sets) and they all work great, sound great and fit my head more comfortably than the HALO. The MOTO ROKR costs considerably less than the HALO as well. I cannot comment on the ROKR vs. the HALO with regard to sound quality or utility with my iPhone as I could not get the HALO to work. To me, the choice here is a "no brainer"...MOTO ROKR all the way!

title: Audio aficionados really need this item
text:
After some intermittent problems with my bluetooth adapter (see other review) I bound the unit to my computer and my Android phone. It exceeded my expectations. First, the audio is great and you can control the next/previous with the headset. The mic is excellent and works quite well in windy conditions. The bass and high notes are clear and crisp, volume goes to dead quiet to beyond anyone's comfort level. From a sound quality standpoint, I would ask for nothing more. After over 30 charges, the battery still lasts more than 8 hours. I have only had it run down once, this was on the third day after a charge. No indication, just would not stay bound to a device for more than 15 seconds or so.

Here are the issues I have with this unit.
The inner foam rubs off. It doesn't effect the quality of the device but it definitely looks like I have had it for years. I use it every day (listen at work) and the foam is very cheap. The next/previous function is by tapping the + or - on the headset. There should be a raise/recessed area so that this location can be easily found. If not, then you will have your volume go too high for comfort. (next function).

Last, While you can see if you are connected via bluetooth, (blue light flashing) there needs to be some indication of battery level while the unit is open. The battery seems to last as long as I need, but it would be good to know this with some positive feedback from the headset.

title: They'll break in a year or less
text: I got my Halo at a Best Buy about a year ago. The headset has the upper piece that sits on top of the head and two lower pieces with the earphones that are connected to the upper piece by joints that have to be put together with a 'click'. Problem is, these joints are made of plastic and if they don't connect, the headset does not work. I use my headset every day. I like them. They have good sound. The joints have worn out, though, and my headset will not stay together anymore. A piece of plastic on one side cracked two months ago and recently fell off. It's winter now, too, so if I can finally manage to gingerly get the pieces together, after I put my hat on, they come apart. Most of the time you don't even know they've separated until you try to make a phone call or listen to music and realize the headset is not working. What a waste of a Benjamin for a headset to function properly for less than a year. They won't work with the PS3, either.

title: Jabra Halo: The most underrated wireless headphone set!
text:
This won't be long, but to the point. I only tend to write reviews when I feel strongly one way or another (good or bad), and by the amount of stars for this item, I think you can foreshadow what this will be.

Previously I was using the Sony DR-BT101 wireless headphones, which are good but not fantastic like the Jabra Halo. The Halo seems to just fit better (albeit not recommended for overly large heads...might be an issue), it has a much smaller profile which I think many people would prefer from a wireless headphone set, and the aesthetics and options are plentiful being just enough to satisfy even the savvy tech connoisseur. But one of the major differences between this set and others (I mean this is after all the main reason for them) is the sound coming out of them. I'm a bit of an audiophile, and while these are certainly not the absolute best sound I've ever heard, they are definitely the best sound I've heard from sub-$60 headphones, and better ANY wireless headset that doesn't have Bose written on it. The highs and mids are comfortably set, and the bass is most certainly classified as surprisingly good. I can't see anyone not satisfied with this pair at least sound wise.

The only con I can think of is their folding mechanism seems to be a little weak, and a person might think that with some stress on the joints when folding that they will break. This doesn't seem to be the case for me, but I wonder how it will be later on. My recommendation is not necessarily to come at them with kid gloves, but just take care to pay attention to what you're doing and I'm sure all will be fine. In any case this "con" certainly is outweighed by the "pros" listed above, so much that I don't even pay attention anymore.

Lets just say that I was pleasantly surprised at the quality of the Jabra Halo wireless headphones. Now back to some music...

title: Good sound, good looks, great price!
text:
I've heard good things about Jabra's products, so I took a chance on the HALO after losing my beloved Logitech Freepulse on a trip. I wanted to find something with a mic as well to use with my phone. These work exceptionally well and look pretty good too! The sound is rich, from some seriously booming bass to nice highs on cymbals. title: Voodoo required
text:
I bought this headset to pair with my Lenovo laptop. I work for a virtual company, so the bulk of our communications are on Skype and GoToMeeting. The headset "mostly" works. It can go days with no problems, but then it will indiscriminately disconnect and I just about have to kill a brindled calf in the pale moonlight to get it connected again. I'm not sure if it's a Bluetooth issue or a Jabra issue, but whatever the issue is, there is no hard and fast procedure for getting it to connect again. Sometimes it's just a matter of going through the re-connect procedure on the laptop, other times I have to fold the headset up, unfold it, then go through the re-connect process, still other times it requires a full restart of the computer to re-establish a connection. You can imagine this being a problem during an online meeting.

I have paired my Droid with out any reliability issues on this machine, so I'm fairly certain that my BT adapter is solid.

It's extremely frustrating when it doesn't work, so likely I'll be searching for a decent wireless USB solution. I was just hoping not to have to put another dongle on my computer.

title: Buyer beware....
text:
I usually don't leave reviews unless I can remain positive for the most part but I really feel like I need to voice my opinion about this product. I am one of those people who think they can read all the negative reviews and then think it will be better for me because I am really good with this stuff. I was dead wrong.

I have wanted a pair of these for a very long time now but after only a week with these things I have had nothing but problems,

-Half the 'felt' from the headband is already falling off. It's all over my head every night and very annoying and makes the product look terribly cheap.

-The cheesy fold to power off/ power on is a complete joke and the hinges feel extremely fragile to me and likely to last less than a few months at most. This means there is no way to wear them around your neck if out and about with no other way to hold them and wish to have them turned off. And it also means you have to fold them in order to charge with out interfering with your backup bluetooth headset. I found this to be a very annoying problem becuase I wanted to avoid hinging them as much as possible because of the cheap hinge feel.

-The charging indicator works nothing like advised in the manual. You plug it in and the battery blinks red for 2 hours and then just turns off. It never turns to green like it is supposed to and unless it does it wont turn on. The first charge took over 4 hours, 2 hours blinking red and then turned green after another 2 hours of no indication light at all. The second charge I had it plugged in for 5 hours, it blinked red for the first 2 hours and then did nothing for the next 3 hours and when I went to use them the battery was still dead!

-Terrible, uncomfortable fit that will have your ears throbbing within the hour and a design that in no way attempts to stay flat against your ears or stay even remotely positioned on your head in an active environment.

-Constant clicking and static sounds heard during silent periods between songs/during pause time.

-It is not possible to initiate voice commands with the headset. Long pressing the center button only puts it in pairing mode to pair with multiple devices at the same time. Seriously a bluetooth hands free headset that cannot initiate voice commands so I can make a call?

-Jabras customer support declined to respond to my emails or call me despite their *STOP DO NOT RETURN TO STORE* labeling. I gave them a fair chance to support their product and they declined.

+On the bright side when they did work the phone calls were crystal clear and music sounded amazing with deep rich lows and crisp vibrant highs with plenty of volume even when working in noisy environments with power tools. No call complaints what so ever.

+Volume controls worked very well, precise and consistent for me. EVEN with my work gloves on.

Promptly returned. BUYER BEWARE.

The JayBird Sportsband is a far superior product in almost every way. [[ASIN:B003TO52A2 JayBird Sportsband Bluetooth Headphones (Midnight Black)]]

title: Excellent music audio, average phone audio
text:
I've owned many Bluetooth headsets, mainly because I'm very hard on them. I have several hours of commuter train rides each working day and any Bluetooth headset I buy will get constant usage. I bought a Jabra Halo about three months ago and so far, I'm extremely happy with this product.

There are several thing I really like about the Halo:

1) They fit my head very well, snug but comfy. The problem is, not everyone has my head's dimensions but for me, they're perfect.
2) Audio quality for music is excellent...much better than the Plantronics/Altec-Lansing Backbeat headphones I was previously using. Specifically, the bass response is much better and the mid range sounds have much more punch.
3) These headphones are able to connect to more than one device at a time, two at a time to be precise. Hence, I can switch from my iPhone, laptop or iPad without explicitly disconnecting from one unit and reattaching to another. This is an extremely convenient and helpful feature.
4) The Jabra Halo connects much more quickly and with less fuss than any other Bluetooth headset I've owned. Other Bluetooth headsets seemed to connect sometimes but not others, and invariably, I end up fiddling with them, turning them off and on, turning the Bluetooth functions on the source device off and on...etc...etc to get a stable connection. The Halo connects just about every time on the first shot to all my devices.
5) The quality of materials is high and feels substantial.

About the only thing I don't think is truly excellent about the Jabra Halo is the phone functions. While the headset works decently with my iPhone, it's not as amazing as it's stereo audio performance for music. The Halo works but it's preyty average where the phone calls are concerned. Hence, I give the Jabra Halo only four stars but that's much more out of consideration of the needs of others than my own.

Indeed, I like this product so much that I just ordered a second set, which I'll keep on my shelf in case my first unit fails. As I said, I use my Bluetooth headphones heavily and eventually, they will die...no reason to think that day is coming soon however, when it does arrive, I'm going to want another set of these headphones. Jabra might discontinue them and replace them with something worse and hence, my second set are an insurance policy against future screwups on the company's part. For right now, these are the best Bluetooth headphones I've found...and I've had a few.

title: Nice idea, poor implementation
text:
This is a headphone that has a nice sound and a good design concept, but it's impaired by cheap materials and poor execution of the concept. I would not recommend buying this unit.

I have two grievances with it:
1. The plastics used in its construction are inadequate for the loads placed upon the hinges in normal operation. I like the folding aspect of the headset: it's why I originally selected it. However, it depends upon the strength of the plastic to stay "locked" in the "on" or operational position. After a month of use, the plastic is cracking and broken away so the unit does not stay locked open. It still works, kindof... see the next note.
2. It has developed an internal short. I'm not sure where, but it results in my having to fiddle with it for the first five or ten minutes of use to get it to stay on. This is unacceptable. It's for this reason that I don't recommend it.

In fairness when it works, it works well. The unit does have a microphone and I do use it with my iphone 3GS as a headset. It's amazing to me that the microphone which is up in the speakers is able to pick up my voice even when the ambient noise is very high.

title: Just OK
text:
I bought these to listen to music on my BlackBerry Torch 9800. I wanted headphones (earbuds hurt my ears) that folded, so I can carry them with me. I also was looking for something that could connect to my phone and my laptop at the same time.

Pros:
1)They fit my head perfectly, but I have a small head.
2)The sound quality is good, and the controls on the side work well. I would like it if the volume controls were actual buttons, though.

Cons:
1) The most frustrating problem is that after a few minutes of being connected the signal will begin to drop in and out, and the only way to correct it is to turn them off and then on again. Sometimes pausing the music and restarting it will work, but this is not often.
2)They fold, but not very small. They still take up a lot of room in my purse.
3)Pairing them with my laptop (Dell C620 with Windows 7) was a complete nighmare, and even after the initial pairing it still takes some effort to get them to connect. The headphone mounted controls do not work when connected to the laptop. Having them connected to the phone and the laptop at the same time is an ordeal. I have to turn off the bluetooth on the phone so that they can connect to the laptop first, and then turn it back on so they can connect with the phone. If they see the phone first they won't connect to the laptop.
4)The port where the micro usb plugs in is very loose, so it is no unusual for the power cable to fall out while it is charging. I don't see how you could use the wired music option because of this. It would never stay plugged in as you moved around.
5)The power cable and usb->micro usb calbes included in the box are 6" long, which makes them pretty much useless. I use the cables from one of my BlackBerrys.
6)They came as a "white box" and it states in the included pamphlet that they are not covered by the manufacturer's warranty.

When everything is working they are great, but a lot of the time everything isn't working. If I could do it again I don't think I would buy them.

title: Design Flaws Destroy its Value
text:
The Jabra HALO is a very nice looking set of headphones. The sound quality is fine (I'm not picky though), but there are a number of design flaws that really make it a no-buy for me.

1. The only way to turn the headphones on and off is by folding in their right side. The power mechanism is built into the hinge. For someone who does a lot of on-and-off listening, it's really annoying to not be able to just turn the headphones off.

2. The folding arms are weak. After about a month of regular use, small cracks started to form around the hinges where the headphones fold. Now, after about three months, shards of plastic are constantly splitting off, and the hinges no longer stay open on their own. I have to carefully put the headphones on, and then the pressure from resting against my head keeps them in place. A moving part like this should have been designed to withstand much more wear and tear.

3. The touch-sensitive area on the right earpiece that does volume and next/previous track is terrible. It is sluggish and slow to respond. You'll also find that you accidentally change the volume a lot of the time when you're trying to reach the play/pause button, or trying to change tracks. Using a touch sensor here is pure gimmick, I would definitely prefer physical buttons.

4. If you have glasses, you'll be miserable. The headphones, although sleek, are really uncomfortable to wear for more than a few minutes if you're wearing glasses.

If these headphones cost $10.00, I wouldn't mind just buying a new pair every couple of months, but at over $50.00 I can't recommend them.

A moving part like this should have been designed to withstand much more wear and tear.

You'll also find that you accidentally change the volume a lot of the time when you're trying to reach the play/pause button, or trying to change tracks. Using a touch sensor here is pure gimmick, I would definitely prefer physical buttons.

4. If you have glasses, you'll be miserable. The headphones, although sleek, are really uncomfortable to wear for more than a few minutes if you're wearing glasses.

If these headphones cost $10.00, I wouldn't mind just buying a new pair every couple of months, but at over $50.00 I can't recommend them.

title: "was" a great product
text:
I bought that product with my brother's referral. loved the form, the sleek design and exceptional sound quality for its price range. Quite natural yet rich sound, not that kind of "we boosted the bass so that our crappy headset sounds like something to you"... HOWEVER, like every item in use, my beloved halo also wore out. first started with the velvet like coating on the inner part of the neck piece. Luckily the surface beneath it was even better (still somehow velvet like) so I just scratched off the worn part (photo available). I was still happy...

And the device kept non intentionally folding in at instances like mom was giving a tight hug or I was stretching inside the car to grab a hold of something. was still ok, I was clicking it back. no worries...

So if you're a headset-around-my-neck maniac like me, I strongly discourage you from buying this product. But if you're just an occasional music listener and looking for killer price-performance stereo headset for your mobile, that's still the one...

title: Surprisingly good!
text:
I bought these headphones out of sheer desperation while in Target, so I could listen to music on my iPhone while shopping (too many distractions, I am not what one would call a "people person"), and was shocked at more than a few features:

1. Comfort. I have always been skeptical of ear bud headphones, because all others hurt my ears after a short time. These, however, fit perfectly right out of the box. They do come with different size ear pieces (small, medium, large). The over-the-ear construction is flexible enough to allow for some movement, unlike the ear buds that come with the iPhone/iPod, so they are about a thousand times more comfortable - a huge plus in my book.

2. Sound quality. I own a great number of Bose/higher end equipment, and while these headphones definitely aren't on that level of sound, they are incredibly good! Great bass, crystal clear high tones, and no distortion at all at high volumes. I was pleasantly shocked, to say the least. They are also pretty good at blocking noise, although these are not noise-reduction headphones.

3. Ease of use. As stated, I bought these at Target, tore them out of the box in the parking lot, and wore them into the next store - they stayed in place, and when I needed to I could simply pop out the ear buds and leave the earpieces just over my ears. The length of the cord is also just right for an iPhone or iPod - not so long it gets caught on things, and not too short where you feel restricted in movement.

Overall, for $30, these were a great buy! I'm very impressed.

title: Great little headphones...especially for working out!
text:
I bought these specifically to use while working out and I could not be happier! I am a fan of good sound quality and was worried these "cheap" headphones would not suffice. I own the Bose QC2's, the Shure E4c earbuds, and an older pair of Sony MDR-CD580's so I know what good headphones/earbuds are supposed to sound like. Now obviously these don't sound as good as the Shure E4c's but at 1/10th the price (literally) these sound phenomenal. The Shure's don't sound 10 times as good (diminishing return on investment with them...but on a side note...the Shure's are simply stunning). They need a snug/airtight fit in your ear canal to ensure good sound quality so be patient and try the different ear pieces they come with until you find one you like. Also, they sound better once you start to workout...I think the sweat helps them make a better seal haha.

The cord is a good length...not too short getting pulled out and not w/feet of extra cord laying around. I have a "SanDisk Sansa Clip+ 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)" and these headphones work great with it.

The "earhook" design holds them in place. ALSO, I was worried that the in-ear design of the earbud would amplify noises like a pair of earplugs...like hearing every thud of your footsteps as you walk...our worse yet it you run. But, much to my delight, these headphones work great with running and that is not an issue.

You can't go wrong with these!

****Update 6/28/2011****

I have been using these for a while and I am even happier with them now than I was when I got them. They sound great and STAY ON YOUR EARS...this can be an issue with headphones while you are working out. I have noticed they have a slight "bass-heavy" bias...which typically I am not a fan of but these pull it off/can get away with it. The way you experience the bass effects from in-ear headphones is different than when listening to a big stereo. The bass is in your ear rather than being felt by your whole body like when a dedicated stereo/subwoofer is playing. The slight increase in perceived bass these headphones provide seems to work great - regular old cheap compressed mp3's still sound great.

Also, these have stood up to many workouts thus far...the rubber ear pieces don't absorb sweat like a cloth covering would. Also, no amount of sweat has affected these. I would think the moisture would damage the internals of the speaker but these have not been affected at all. Just make sure the ear piece size you pick (it comes w/several sizes) fit your ear canals fully. All ear-bud style headphones need to fit snugly to sound good.

title: EXCELLENT VALUE
text:
A few days ago I received my new Philips SH8100/28 ear hook in-ear headphones. I spent quite a long time researching these and other lower-priced headphones before making this purchase. As so many other reviewers say, "I'm not an audiophile," but so far, I am quite pleased with these headphones. I learned that many in-ear "cans" require a break-in period, maybe 100 hours. If so, these can only get even better.

PROS: Very good price, considering the quality and performance--balanced range of sound, not super heavy in the bass, nice, clear midrange and treble sounds. These phones are quite comfortable. I had them in for a couple hours straight on the first day, and I've never even worn in-ear phones before! They stayed in place very securely, even when I was heading down a trail on a very warm day hike!

The ear hooks even allow me to semi-remove the phones to talk with other people, while the headphones stay in place hooked on my ears. I was concerned about whether the hooks would interfere with the ear temples on my sunglasses, but not a problem at all.

As for the cable itself, it is a perfect length, and is well-fastened and supported where the wires enter the headphones. Also, I have NOT noticed any noise transmitted to my ears when the cable rubs on my shirt, something I've heard can be a problem with headphones from other companies.

CONS: My only complaints: (1) No storage pouch or case (a Zip Lock baggy does the trick). (2) Providing a clip to hold the cable on my shirt would be nice. (Maybe I can use an old tie clip or alligator clip). (3) As mentioned by others, the cable is VERY tangle-prone, until I straighten it out and put the phones on. A nuisance, but not a deal breaker.

Anyway, so far, after a few uses, these Philips phones are proving to be a wise choice.
