title: Perfect for small ears and exercising
text:
I purchased these headphones specifically after reading another reviewer who called out the fact that these buds are ideal for small ears. Those of us with tiny ears have a hard time finding earbuds that fit properly. Over-the-ear headphones are great but not that great for exercising, hence earbuds make a better option, theoretically. Unfortunately most earbuds just fall out of my tiny ears.

In an effort to get a better fit than the standard Apple iPod ear buds, I purchased a set of expensive SHURE earbuds. Unfortunately, the SHURE buds were just too tight in my ear canal, regardless of the type of bud cover I used (and SHURE provided several fit options). The SHURE bud cover materials were too stiff and simply not small enough, so I ended up going back to the old Apple earbuds as 30 minutes with the SHURE buds left my ears aching. This is most unfortunate because the SHURE earbuds had phenomenal sound quality.

I recently discovered this pair of Philips buds and the above-mentioned review after throwing in the towel while running stairs one afternoon --as my Apple buds kept falling out, every dozen steps. The Philips buds utilize an over-the-ear wrap that is extremely flexible and ultra lightweight, so it fits perfectly on each ear, regardless of your ear shape. What's more, the cables are super thin, so they don't drag down the buds. The less-than robust cables certainly call durability into question, but I'll have to see how they hold up over time before commenting further. Whatever the case, the wrap is fantastic. Additionally, the look of these buds is very slick, and their overall size and shape makes for a discreet package.

The next great feature is the bud itself, which comes with three different sizes of soft, super-pliable bud covers. I used the smallest size cover and they fit perfectly. What's more, the bud covers don't completely filter outside noise like the SHURE buds --which can be great in some instances (e.g., noisy buses and trains). The Philips buds offer a nice compromise in this regard, offering the ability to have excessive noise dampened, yet still enabling you to hear your surroundings enough to get by.

The next great benefit of these buds is the quality of sound. I am very impressed at the overall frequency response and reproduction of sound. From Jack Johnson to the Pet Shop Boys, the highs are accurate and the bass is encompassing (tested with my iPod's EQ turned off). I am very pleased with the sound quality, especially at this price range. It's not as perfect as the SHURE buds, but it's darned close.

I want to mention that I received the buds from Amazon new and instantly noticed that the left bud had greater bass response than the right. After testing to confirm that the buds weren't performing correctly, I used the simple exchange procedure online and a new pair showed up at my doorstep the very next day. The UPS driver even handed over a delivery label for my defective pair, which he delivered back to Amazon. The Amazon exchange procedure is fantastic and painless, with new product delivered overnight.

Yes, this technical issue with the first pair also calls their durability into question, but again, I am willing to wait until I've had them for a while before issuing further judgement --especially at this price point.

The fact remains that these buds fit my almost impossible to fit tiny ears while staying put through intense exercise and offering excellent sound. I'm willing to risk durability when all these other conditions have been met.

title: Don't stay put
text:
I am in the market for some headphones to use for running. Like many others, I find the supplied Apple earbuds to be uncomfortable and prone to falling out with physical activity (such as running). Additionally, I have a set of Sure earbuds but I don't want to run with them because I won't be able to hear anything except my own heavy breathing.

After reading many reviews on several products I opted for these. The moment I put them on I realized they weren't going to work well. In order for earbuds like these to function well (produce good highs and lows) they need to create a seal with your ear canal. They don't. On the few occasions I was able to get them into a good position and create the seal, the sounds were actually quite good. However, the moment I started walking around they came loose. The earhook potion keeps the bud from falling out completely but without that perfect seal, the sound is not good.

I think I have relatively medium to medium-large ears and for me, these did not work. YMMV.

title: Crapped Out
text:
Searching high and low, and having tried any number of earphones to use during runs and workouts without much satisfaction, I was happy to read such positive reviews of these Philips headphones. Using them, however, was another matter.

First of all, I imagine that you have to have fairly small ears for these to fit comfortably. My ears are what I would characterize as average, and I could not get these to stay put without constant adjustment. I tried all three sets of the included plugs, but none solved the problem. The first time I used them, on a treadmill at the gym, I was continuously pressing these speakers back into my ears, else all I got was a tinny playback with no base.

And the second time I used them, the left speaker died completely. Needless to say, I was not happy. They're now on their way back to Amazon for a refund.

My experience may have been an anomaly, but my advice is to avoid these unless you have very small ears and don't intend to sweat or use them during a workout.

title: Earbuds that stay on, and in
text:
I bought a pair of these because my Skullcandy earbuds always kept falling out. When I work out, I sweat a lot, enough that even my sweatband can't always keep it at bay, so I wanted to try earbuds that hooked over the ear as a means of preventing fallout.

As a pleasant surprise, they definitely do work well! I don't know if I have small ears, per se, but they're not that large so that those with more diminutive ears don't have issues, which was a point that another commenter made (in that they fit smaller ears well).

I wouldn't classify myself as an audiophile, but I would say the audio quality is acceptable. I had a pair of Sony earbuds for a long time (can't remember the model) that I had before these, and I have found that Sony products have equal or better sound, but Sony doesn't seem to have earclip models that are viewed favorably by the majority.

UPDATE: I bought these back in October and they were doing just fine until recently when my cats destroyed them. They destroyed the earbuds that came before these too. Obviously my cats approve of my earbud choices and chew on them to show just how much they do. I'm pleased enough with this pair to order another, even though the price went up. Hopefully I can keep my cats away from pair #2. Note to self: keep all things with wires in a drawer when not around.

title: Great execution; that Skullcandy never ceases to deliver.
text: (immediate thoughts on day one of usage) The other reviews are correct; these things pound! You can feel the vibrations from the woofer (hasn't annoyed me yet). I have owned nearly a dozen Skullcandy products and this is the best pair of headphones concerning sound delivery. The woofer can be turned on or remain off at the slide of a switch on the left earpiece. The earpiece speaker cover snaps in and out for easy access to the battery port; very creative and you don't notice any added weight or feel lopsided. The ear pads are super comfortable and you do not feel like your head is in a vice while they are on. They fold-up nice, come with the standard travel sack, and the detachable cord that now comes standard on most of their headphone products. The only area I immediately see for improvement is the fashionability of these phones; you can chose black or white…not quite what you are accustomed to expect from Skullcandy, but hey, fashion isn't the top priority when its time to jam out. I'll dub these the 'ace of bass.'

title: Skull Candy Delivers...and it's Delicious
text:
I did a few months of research for headphones for my budget under $200. These are hands down the best bang for your buck and for your ear drums. They fit comfortably over my big ears and the head band is nicely padded as well. The bass drivers are amazing and produce face massaging bass! I bought these to listen to while at work as a web developer and for online school work. On average I'll have them on my skull for 10 hours per day.

I have only had to change the battery one time since I got them for Christmas...and I've listened to them heavily! If I'm going to spend the majority of my waking hours with Headphones on, #1 they better be comfortable and #2 they better be quality. The build is mostly hard plastic but that does not detract from the sound at all. My cube farm neighbor just bought the Beats Studio headphones for three times as much $$ as the Crushers and they I hear sound leaks all day long! Crushers leak very little and the volume has to be up quite a bit.

The sound quality of the bass is really amazing for the price you pay. Perks of the headphones is the detachable cord and the long battery life of the bass driver. My neighbor that has the Beats Studio requires two batteries and they require to be changed twice as much. Crushers battery power is turned off when you unplug them or when you turn the bass adjuster all the way down so you don't have to worry about dead batteries in the morning if you forget to turn them off.

The other day I forgot my Crushers at home and my day wasn't the same...I had to use ear buds...gak. I am thrilled with these every day and consider them part of the family. Ha. Go try them out at a Best Buy near you side by side with the other way more expensive competitors...you won't be disappointed. My ONLY gripe with these is that I haven't been able to find a hard case that will fit these. I sent them an email and they said they do not know of any manufactures that make Hard cases to fit and they won't be making any for the next foreseeable future. At any rate...Make your face and hears happy...GO BUY THEM!

title: Great cans for your average young adult
text:
Alright. I picked these up for $100 at Best Buy. I went around testing all the available models they had and these stood out with the price point and sound. (They easily beat all of the Beat's in sound quality, AND comfort)

Comfort was a big deal to me, I spend a lot of time studying and playing games with my friends, so lasting comfort was a must, especially with me wearing glasses. These feel great. I can get into a study/game session for 6 or more hours and sometimes forget they're even on. They don't seal great, which is fine with me because I want to be able to hear how loud I'm talking while gaming or if someone calls me.
One small problem is that the headband isn't the softest and can begin to make the top of your head sore. Simply elongate the headphones, and move the pads to have your ears support them more, taking some weight off of the band. Problem solved!

Comfort - 9.5/10 even with my glasses on

Admittedly I'm somewhat of a basshead. I love electronic music and alternative rock. These things are super versatile. I usually keep the bass adjuster around 25%, and that works great for subtle rumbling and great sounding bass. Whenever I'm in the mood, I can turn the bass all the way up and enjoy my music for a bit. Also sounds great for movies and games, being around or inside a tank in Battlefield is an experience not like any other headphone has offered me

Sound - 9/10, pair these up with an EQ and they will sound great.

While they don't feel too expensive, I'm not worried because Skullcandy headphones come with a lifetime warranty, so I'm covered! Definitely stylish enough for me to wear around college and get compliments!

I didn't really have a lot of respect for Skullcandy years ago around 2009, but I was Wowed by the new Crushers, completely blew away the old trashy Skullcrushers.
Skullcandy is stepping their game up, and I'm quite impressed with them.

title: Hands down, the MOST bass you can get out of headphones.
text: I've owned and used several pair of headphones over 25 years and use each pair for different reasons. For super clear hi fidelity listening, I whip out my Bose Quiet Comforts or V-Moda Crossfade headphones. When wanting to travel light or do activities outdoors, I'll use my Beats Powersports or Rockford Fosgate Punch Plugs. (by the way, if I keep a pair of headphones for longer than a few weeks, they are good headphones. otherwise I sell or return them) I bought the Skullcandy Crusher's after demo'ing them in Best Buy. I immediately had to have them after feeling the bass response. I used to have a pair of cheap headphones that had this effect, but they eventually broke and I found out no headphone manufacturer was doing this "trick" any more. Having a driver vibrate the headphones in time to bass frequencies fools your brain into thinking it is hearing massive bass. In car audio competitions, they used to sell vibration "amps" that mount under each seat to fool people into feeling/hearing the bass much harder than the speakers are actually playing. The same thing is happening inside these Crusher headphones. The main reason people keep buying higher and higher end headphones these days is to upgrade the bass response. It is very tough to get massive bass from smaller speakers. Skullcandy has figured out a way to "cheat" and the results are incredible. I'm surprised more companies aren't doing this same trick. I never thought I would say that headphones can have too much bass, but these can hit a ridiculous levels. It isn't ever uncomfortable or too distorted, but you can make these headphones have an over-powering bass response to where songs sound almost comical. These were made for dub-step. Most users I know will play with the novelty of turning the bass slider to max when they first get them, but eventually you will want to hear all of the song and not just the bass end by keeping the slider at 1/2 to 3/4 settings. The mids and highs are very acceptable too. No distortion unless you are blowing up the bass slider to max. The sound you get out of these headphones is worth FAR more than $99. I can't imagine the amount of bass these will have once the speakers reach their prime "break-in" period. To keep this review simple... if you want the most bass you can get from headphones and don't want to spend $500+ to do it, buy these now. The only reason I didn't give this product a 5 star rating was that after an hour or so of listening, it felt like it was crushing my head. They seem a little tight, but that might get better over time. If you have a small/medium head, they might be fine for you. One of the other great features of these headphones are the auto-on/off circuit for the bass driver. Stopping your music or unplugging the cord will turn off the battery powered amplifier circuit. This insures you get the max battery life. I never liked headphones that had a manual on/off switch because you'd always forget. Also, considering what is packed into these headphones, they are rather light. They don't dent your hair like other heavier headphones. If you have a specific question on these, message me. I'd be glad to answer back.

title: Too Big!
text:
I will tell you ahead of time, I am not an expert on sound so I cannot give a well educated summary of the sound.
I will say that they sound to me is good. Everything is clear without static, there is a lot of bass if you like that (I mean I can feel the vibration substantially on the sides of my face and if I put my hand on the cups while the music is playing there is substantial vibration, at high volume). The volume is sufficiently loud. When plugged into my macbook pro I cannot turn them up too high for comfort.

Here's the problem: They are too big for my head! I have a somewhat small distance between the top of my head and my ears. If I put the cups where I normally prefer to wear my headphones the band is a good inch above my head on the smallest setting. I can give you two pieces of information for my relative size: I wear a size 7 hat loosely, and I currently own a pair of Skullcandy PLYR 2 gaming headphones that fit perfectly on the smallest setting. This is not an unusual problem for me, I often have this problem with headphones, but I was expecting them to be fine since my other Skullcandy headphones fit well.

title: Ridiculously good for the price
text:
I have listened to a lot of headphones in this price range to have at the office, and these are some of the very best at anything close to the price. In particular, Beats can't touch the sound from these until their top end model at more than 3x the price. The construction isn't super robust which must be where they cut some corners to get this sound quality.

The ear cushions are very comfortable, not leather at this price, but still very nice. A lot of headphones make me feel like they are clamped on my head creating way too much pressure to be comfortable for long listening sessions. I don't have that issue with these. They give a nice seal that keeps the music in and the outside sounds out, but I don't feel like they're clamped on, just a very nice fit.

My main comparison headphones are my regular office headphones, Beyerdynamic DT770's and my home phones, a pair of Sennheiser HD-600's. The Crushers can't touch my Sennheisers, but they're not far off the Beyerdynamics at less than half the price. If you're in the market for headphones, especially closed headphones, you should definitely give these a listen. One last note, my evaluation of the sound is based on having the bass boost at minimum.

title: Bass to Bust your Brain and Adequate Sound Quality for a lower tier price
text:
The Bass Booster is for when you show your friends how much of a douche you truly are (half the reason I bought them), or you just really really feel like self inflicting a migraine headache. the sound quality is alright, about worth what you would pay for them, maybe the quality of some other brands costing $99+ but nothing special, The booster only hits at the top most bass frequencies, so its no Hanz Zimmer theater experience. What is special is how they fit (at least my head) snug as a glove. My best headset is my desk headphones $200 Turtle Beach with Dolby 7.1. Haven't found much better audio inside of the sub $300 mark, the problem is that I cannot use the Turtle Beaches around the house because they're quite large and loose on my head (much stiffer when new), but these Crushers suit me quite well for every day use away from the desk with an Adequate level of quality.

Side note that I owned a pair of the SkullCrushers in 11' and if I remember correctly they had a much better Bass frequency, didn't give spontaneous migraine headaches, and fit about the same as the Crushers with much more storing flexibility. Although they did lack in sound quality as these feel a bit crisper and more lively. I would still recommend the SkullCrushers to people who want to experience a ripe sub woofing right into their ear canals as opposed to the cerebral jack hammering the new Crushers give out.

title: Pretty good with some caveats
text:
I bought these in 2018 and I'm just getting around to writing a review because I have to replace the cord. I am upset that Skullcandy doesn't sell just the cords because they are detachable and the rest of the headset is perfectly fine. They look brand new. I love these headphones. The sound quality is amazing and the noise cancellation is OK but could be better. I always look for "over-the-ear" headphones because ones that sit on top of my ears cause ear pain and headaches. These are OK in terms of comfort but they tend to cause ear pain after a while and I find myself taking them off.

The only beef I have is what I mentioned before - the CORD!!! It has been an issue from the get-go. Some people might say to go wireless but I am "old school" and I like the wired headphones for the sound quality. Plus, I don't have to worry about charging them - just plug and go. However, the cord for this headset is very short! I had to buy a headphone extension cord because I was constantly unplugging the cord accidentally, putting extra pressure on the end. Eventually, this lead to the problem I have now - a non-working cord. I found a replacement on this website but it's not OEM and the color won't match. I don't care, though, as long as it keeps these "bad boys" working for a few more years and I don't have to buy wireless headphones!

title: Bass Amplifier cuts out unless volume is extremely high
text: I really had high hopes for these headphones. When the bass amplifier is on, they sound great. The bass amplifier has an auto-shut off that turns itself off when there is no audio, or at least that is the theory. The problem is that the auto-shut off circuitry is not nearly sensitive enough which means it shuts itself off at all but the highest volume levels. In order to keep it from shutting off, you have to keep the volume at a level that is not comfortable at all for listening. To make matters worse, their customer support is absolutely horrible. I tried to send them a message using their website, but it complained about me not passing their 'captcha' test, the problem is, there was no captcha test on the page, and yes, I disabled all ad-blockers. Then I sent them a private FB message as well as posted on their FB page (which got deleted). No answers at all. Then I tried their live chat option, sat at queue position #1 for 45 minutes and then was told to contact the seller on Amazon. Bottom line, stay away from these unless you want to listen to your music extremely loud just to have the bass kick in.

title: Excellent build quality
text:
As the selling point of these suggest, these are in fact great when it comes to bass, they're not lying. However, the real selling point of these should be how well they're built. These headphones are the longest I've ever had a pair without them breaking. The only con in terms of build quality is the adhesive on the ear cushions started to decay, but some glue fixed that no problem. The big con, which isn't a con of the headphones themselves really, but because all these aux wires are made in China, they all fall apart absurdly fast. I go through 1 aux wire about every month or two, unless I get really lucky and get a decently made one (by China standards) that'll last a few months. I'm not being overly rough with them, I just use the headphones A LOT and the quality of the cables suck so, very easy to destroy them.

Now, over all audio quality. I'm picky about my audio quality. Picky enough where I can't stand not having an equalizer I can tweak to my liking, but I don't think it's quite fair to call myself an audiophile. That said, the over all audio quality seems fine to me. I did have a headset that was cheap, but supposed professionals were claiming they had really good audio quality despite the price. Comparing the two, I can tell a difference in audio, but not so much in quality. I couldn't tell you which ones sound better over all, I think it comes down more to preference unless you're doing super high end professional work where it's an absolute must to have sensitive headphones to pick apart audio at the seems. The main thing I seek in audio is heavy bass and these deliver, the non-bass audio sounds perfectly good too so over all I'm very happy.

I like these headphones enough that I ponied up for one of the expensive wireless upgraded versions of them, but if you're on somewhat of a low budget and these are available, I'd recommend them. Maybe I'm just lucky, but they should last a good while.

title: VERY good sound for reasonable money!
text: These earbuds have great sound quality, if worn properly. Pay no attention to those who say that they have no bass or that they sound tinny or have too much treble. They, most likely, are having trouble getting a good seal in their ears with the medium sized gel tips that came on the earbuds. They may have missed the little package that has the larger or smaller gels in it. If you don't hear good bass, try the larger gels, if they hurt, try a smaller gel. These earbuds have great sound with punchy bass and balanced mids and high tones. If you like more bass than you get with a correct fitting to your ears, try playing with your phone's music player equalizer settings. I haven't had a problem with them falling out of my ears (possibly another fitment issue for some) but I don't do a lot of bouncing around, either. Any trouble keeping them in the ear could be cured with a set of Comply Sport T200 foam tips if you know the correct size of tip you need (find the correct size gel and you have the right size foam tip.) These earbuds don't have complete sound isolation, meaning that depending on your music volume, you can still hear most things that go on around you, which can be good or bad depending on your particular situation. The isolation foam tips by Comply can fix this, also. The button will pause/play your music, answer/hang up a call, and can select the previous or next track when using the Smart Key app available in your app store for Iphone or Android phones. There is no volume control on the earbuds, but there IS one on your phone or music player, so what's the big deal? These are great earbuds for the price. I am a musician and audiophile. You can pay a LOT more and not get better sound than with these Sony MDREX 110AP earbuds. Better sound CAN be had, but I don't have that kind of money! Believe me when I say that these will do the trick!

title: A Great Pair of Inexpensive Headphones
text:
I normally don’t like in-ear headphones, but I’ve grown to really like these. I originally bought them because I’d forgotten to pack my standard headphones for a plane trip and these looked like they’d block out a decent amount of plane noise without breaking the bank. The microphone and multifunction button was a plus, keeping me from having to turn on my phones screen to pause or change songs (saving battery). It’s also nice because I can seamlessly switch between listening to music and calling people or answering calls (single button press when phone is ringing to answer phone).

The sound quality is great and they fit in my ear very well. After two or more years of use, they still perform great and have excellent bass response. The rubber is even still very pliable and seals into my ear nicely without ever falling out. The build quality appears to be very good and they look brand new even after two years of moderate use. I’m sure I’ll accidentally lose them before they break.

title: Still my favorite after 6 years and dozens of earbuds.
text:
These are still my favorite earbuds after all these years.
I've owned every model of this line, MDEX58, MDRX61, MDRX100, and MDRX110 is the current generation model of the "$30 MSRP" Sony earbud.
They sound spectacular. No other earbud that I've tried under $100 comes close to providing the highs that these do. The sound quality is relatively flat from the lowest bass to the highest highs. They aren't bass enhanced, but they do provide adequate deep, mid, and high bass as well as even mids and highs. If anything they are a bit too generous on the very high end which can be unforgiving to over compression in music files.
I've bought a good 40 or so pair of earbuds and I always come back to these. Nothing else does as good of a job.

title: Best headphones I've ever used... again!!!
text:
I owned the original M50s already. Gave them to my brother after he had a fire in his bedroom. The ear cups may be getting a little worn/cracked but they still sound as amazing as the day I got them, and that's how good the M50xs sound too. Comparing the two, I certainly like the multiple removable cords, and the ear cups feel even softer and more comfortable than before. Very high quality! The dark green color is also gorgeous!

The sound... really just can't be beat for the money (or by most pairs 2x more expensive). If all you care about is bass, then you may disagree, but the M50xs still have plenty of bass. Want more? Use an eq, but you'll be taking away from everything else. Albums are mixed the way they are because that's how the bands/producers/engineers want them to sound. That's what these headphones deliver. You hear every instrument as intended (and I do mean EVERY instrument, you'll hear things that you've never noticed in a song you've listened to 100 times). Nothing is lost. Pure sound. I love them!

title: Good, but HM5 pads are a MUST!!!
text:
Negatives:
- A tad overpriced.
- Sound spectrum is too "V shaped" too much bass and treble, not enough mids.
- ZERO soundstage, sound is aggressively blasted into your skull, it's exhausting.

- Excellent build quality.

- Can go extremely loud with no distortion whatsoever.
- 3 included cables are a nice touch, and very useful.
- Limited Edition colors are gorgeous.
- HM5 pads fit perfect, and make these infinitely more comfortable, while adding a bit of "sorely needed" soundstage.

These are great, high quality, headphones, but to me adding HM5 pads is a MUST. If you own these, or are considering purchasing them, get some HM5 pads along with them, you will not regret it. After adding the HM5 pads, I Love them, and can wear them for 8+ hours straight, no problem. I purchased the Limited-Edition "Dark Green", which has dark brown pleather and pale metallic gold accents, I purchased Brown pleather HM5 pads, they go perfectly together, and match my gold FiiO X1 in its brown leather Ignis case. The headphones with the larger HM5 pads, 4-foot cable, connected to the Fiio X1 (in its leather Ignis case), all fit perfectly in the included bag.

title: No Artificial Colors or Flavors
text:
What do I mean by the title? Unlike some other high profile and popular headphones, one with a big B (Bose) and the other with a little b (beats), the M50x's are natural. No modifications for extra bass or treble. That only robs you of hearing things you should be by drowning them out from boosting other things. These give you the pure, unaltered sound as the artist intended. That means a lot to me because as a home theater enthusiast, I want to see and hear things as they were meant to be. I want accuracy in my audio and video devices and these deliver the audio in spades. It reminds me of TV displays in stores. The brightness and contrast are cranked up to get your attention but upon closer inspection, it's not at all realistic. Details are lost, people look sunburned, blacks look grey and it doesn't reflect real life. That's what Bose and Beats are to me. Dial back the settings and you get every detail, accurate colors, levels of shadow and an overall realistic picture. That's the AT M50x's.
When searching for my first pair of expensive headphones (I had never spent more than $50) the M50x's consistently came up as the best or one of the best in the under $200 category. $200 was all I was willing to spend. What always caught my attention was the unaltered clarity these provide and so far, I have been very pleased by how well they deliver on that promise. When listening to music, I can clearly focus in on every instrument, every cymbal, every word, chorus and solo. It's a joy to hear my music so clearly and well defined. If other headphones I've used were good, solid standard definition, these are definitely high definition. If you really listen to your music, these headphones are going to help you do that and will make it a much more enjoyable experience. I've used them for movies as well and they really deliver a convincing movie experience. Dialogue is easy to understand, sound effects pack all the right punches, surrounds come through, putting you in the moment and theres nice thumps and booms substituting for subwoofer action. If there's a need to keep the noise down or your going portable, you can have a great movie watching experience with these.
Speaking of portability, this isn't your practical, walking around town or going to the gym set. They're big but perfect for home, long trips or any other stationary listening. Sure, you could take them out but it's a pretty big set to have on when you're on the move. I'll use my on-ear Noontec Zoro HD's (which I highly recommend) for that.
Build quality is excellent. There's plenty of plastic here but this is a very solid feeling set. The leather on the head band and earpads is soft, comfortable and has an expensive look and feel. The earpads completely cover my ears and form a nice seal, keeping the sound in, preventing excess leaking and keeping outside sounds out. I'm not one of those 8 hour a day wearers but for the duration of a movie, I didn't notice any discomfort. Felt or suede earpads can always be purchased and swapped out if need be. They're also very versatile by how many ways they can contort and collapse for storage. I also like the matching and locking removable cord and spare cords packed in the box. Also packed in was a soft leather pouch in a matching chocolate brown to my set. I bought a hard case to use instead but I could see using it for a short trip or days use elsewhere. I went with the limited edition dark green and brown and they really look nice. The green is a dark forest green, almost black in low light and the brown is a darker chocolate brown, with champagne gold accents on the ear cups and hinges. Aesthetically, this is a very good looking and feeling combination. Like they're more expensive than their price point.
I chose the combo from Beach Camera as you get the free case and mini amp for the same price. Shipping was next day and reasonable and packaged well.
Overall, I'm very satisfied with this purchase. I read a lot and watched a lot of videos before making the decision to buy these. It only took a few listens to know that I made the right choice. I know there are other brands of good sounding and well built headphones in the same price range but this combination of high marks by professional and casual reviewers, numerous appearances on top 5 lists, good brand reputation, warranty, build quality, and physical attractiveness made these the set for me. When I give a 5/5 review, it's not for perfection or best available product, it's for a performance and value combination. These meet that combination easily. Highly recommended for music listeners.
Note: I've since added dbrand skins and Brainwavz earpads to mine for that custom look and feel. Definitely recommended for M50x owners.

title: Fantastic. The whole package
text:
I've been using these headphones for a few days and let me tell you, they are fantastic. I am not an 'expert' on headphones, but I can say that the sound quality blows away any other headphones I've had. Whilst these are billed as studio headphones and are very detailed in mids highs and lows, they have a somewhat warm sound which makes them very enjoyable for simply listening to music. I was concerned that these were going to be geared more towards studio work than casual listening, but these will do both quite well. There is plenty of bass, dubstep and electronic music sounds great. The dark green edition looks fantastic. The green parts appear dark grey unless in direct sunlight, then they appear an olive color. They are also very comfortable. The band fits a bit snug, just enough so that they won't fall off or slide when bending over, but not so much as to cause discomfort. The extra cables are also very nice to have. Keep in mind that these are closed-back headphones.

Overall I think that these are quite possibly the best all-around studio headphones for under $200. You would be remiss to not give these ample consideration if you are looking for a pair of great sounding headphones at this price point.

text:

Once again, nothing against Grado's. But, for what I want, these headphones more than fit the bill.

title: Beats Wish They Sounded This Good
text:
I came to this headphone after having used and loved a pair of Shure SRH-440 for the last few years. Those headphones impressed me with their flat-tuned response, nice sound stage, comfort and durability. After my 440s were stolen from my desk where I work (word of advice: don't leave your headphones out over a weekend for the cleaning crew to steal), I decided to step up and go with the ATH-M50x. I've only had them for 1 day, but they are outstanding right out of the box. They have a more curved eq response overall than the SRH-440s with more defined bass, but certainly not to an obscene degree and not at the expense of any higher frequencies. The sound stage is rich and wide - much moreso than the SRH-440. They are reasonably light and fit comfortably over the ears with very good outside ambient noise isolation. They are a little tight at first, but I know from prior experience that they will loosen up over time a little.

Having previously spent over 10 years working in the consumer electronics industry, I can confirm that these are among the best and definitely a nicer-sounding set of over-the-ears than Beats. These outperform Beats and most other headphones in a similar price range on pretty much every level and, at least to my adult eyes, look classier too. Easily the best pair of over-the-ear headphones I have ever owned!

title: Superb
text:
Headphone sound is a very personal thing. How do you tell whether the AT's are the best for the price? Youtube! Lots of videos on independent tests and a user blind test. Electronics articles. AT's are rated among the top choices by almost all audio writers and professionals. So, I took the plunge, looking to upgrade from MMElectronics open headphones to a closed system to block out extraneous noise. Frankly, the MME's have very good sound for a reasonable price ($40) and I will continue to use them when outdoors or using an iPhone. But the AT's are an order of magnitude above these entry level phones.

The M50x sound quality is superb. Clear sound over all frequencies. Perhaps a bit bright in the HF's, but most of us like brightness. The bass is full but not booming. These aren't Beat Studios with their bass attenuation.

Overall, I don't think you could ask for a set of headphones in this range that will do any better. They reproduce what is recorded very accurately.

My favorite test is Faltemeyer's "Axel F". About 50 seconds in, there are small clicks that have a tendency to get lost with less responsive headphones. The AT's provided clear definition.

title: Excellent for the money, but over-hyped and need a 3rd-party cable
text:
I bought these as an inexpensive alternative to the ATH-MR7 headphones, which I bought a few months ago. As much as I love the MR7s, I'm not sure I'd want to ride the New York subway with them on. In addition to being much less expensive, the ATH-M50x has a much more flexible design that allows them to be folded into a more compact form for travel. That said, they use a non-standard locking 2.5mm headphone jack that requires use of the proprietary cords that come with the headphones. Designed as a studio monitor, these phones were not intended for use with a smart phone and the supplied cords lack even a microphone, let alone controls. Suitable replacement cords are available from third parties, however, so that is not a significant issue.

My quibble with these cans, however, is in sound quality. Although I would agree that the sound is exceptional for the price, There are other headphones in the price range that are nearly as good, and with a frequency response that is more to my taste. The high end of these is much better than most of the competition, but it's not in the same league as the ATH-MR7s. I find the bass response of the ATH-M50x, however, to be excessive and boomy - not something I was expecting from a studio monitor. Don't get me wrong - these are excellent headphones, but not nearly as exceptional as all the reviews would lead you to believe.

title: Love bass heavy headphones? Get these!
text:
If you are looking for BASS HEAVY headphones on the cheap (let's say, for the gym, running, school), get these!

I was looking for a replacement for my bass-heavy Sony MDR-W014 for a very long time. I run every day to HOUSE music (shout-out to Miss Monique for knowing how to DJ like a bawse) . I noticed that when I fire my EQ on my Android devices (OPO, Pixel XL) the ability of many headphones to shoot out bass is weak. Some can't even handle any EQ other than flat. Shame.

Decided to give these a try and I am super happy. I don't understand how they managed to kick so much bass out of these. My EQ is back to where I like it: bass is all the way up.

One caveat though: I noticed that I need to crank the volume all the way up (as opposed to the Sony, which managed about 60% volume). And at about 70% volume, increasing the volume will do nothing. Not sure if this is my phone's dac limitation or the Jib themselves.

My next job: find an even bass-heavier (if that's possible) model from Skullcandy (know any?).

Summery: GET THESE IF YOU LOVE BASS.

title: Average headphones, but strange shape...
text:
Decent headphones. Sound, build quality, price are all all acceptable. Sound quality isn't impressive, but what can you expect at this price? They feel far more solid than Apple headphones which are known for falling to pieces, and I know from experience with Gumy that the headphones will last.

Here's the issue:

Bought these to replace Gumy headphones I lost; apparently this is a different design than the ones I had previously, even though it looks similar. I always have to buy these type of earbuds because the kind that actually go into the ear canal never stay in my ears. While these definitely stay in, they have a bit of a strange design, with somewhat of a horizontal egg shaped face rather than a standard circle. The result for me was they're a bit uncomfortable and don't fit as closely to my ear canal as I'd like. This issue brought what otherwise would have been a 4 star review (remember, this is considering the price) to a 3. Really wish they fit like my old Gumy headphones. With this fit, I'm really compelled to go just go buy new headphones and keep these around as spares. Every time I take them out, it's a bit of a relief to my ears...

title: Always like Gumy's!
text:
Been using Gumy head phones for several years, always like a good pair of Gumys.
Only have a few small complaints.

For the most part Gumys are VERY comfortable, they're light and thin and easy to stick in your pocket, they don't pull on your ears or cause major discomfort like a lot of other small earbuds do.
However, after extended use (over an hour -say a full length movie, or using it for music while working on your next exam) it does seem to cause a bit of discomfort in my ears. BUT!! That may just be the shape of my ear, and it doesn't apply to everyone. ;)

I purchased this specific earbud (coconut white) because I LOVE coconuts and thought a creamy white would be an awesome color to have next! But I was disappointed in the color, it actually looks dirty and cheap, like something my grandma would have picked up at the Dollar Store.

The only other small complaint I would have is that if you use these headphones often (like I do), they slowly start to short out right below one of the earbuds. I generally find that these earbuds last me anywhere from 3-6 months at a time.
Sadly though, it's not just Gumy's, because I have tried different brands, and they all have done the same. (Even Apple's earbuds, though they lasted closer to 9 months, but I still had the same problem with the shortage right below the earbud itself.)

I still choose Gumy though because of the comfort compared to other brands, and the colors. I mean really... who doesn't love a bright colored pair of headphones? ;)

title: Best economical headphone
text: I picked up a pair of these JVC Gumy Earbuds in Coconut White in a local store for $6.88 on sale. They are about the same size/form-factor as the original Apple earbuds with the exception of they are actually slightly better form fitting to the ear canal. I hardly know they are there. I wear them in the office and they pretty much block out all the distracting ambient noises and conversations, and I can listen at a low volume. The sound is excellent on low volume with plenty of head room to go much louder. They are not "tinny", but rather warm and full sounding and the base response is quite nice. Others have said that the chords transfer noise to the earbuds, but it is only noticeable when the music is turned off. The chord is not as pretty as Apple's single, round chord (it is two affixed side-by-side chords typical of cheaper headphones), but the chord seems tough enough. In fact I forgot them in a shirt pocket and they went through both the washer and dryer, and while the cord was twisted in places, the headphones still work perfectly! For the price I paid I plan on picking up another set as a backup.

title: Excellent earbud in the low price category
text: I purchased all of these and compared them with each other: [[ASIN:B004Y3A3ZQ JVC HA-F150W Gumy Headphones, White]], [[ASIN:B003EM8008 Panasonic RPHJE120K In-Ear Headphone, Black]], [[ASIN:B007FRYDWM JBL Tempo High-Performance Earbud Headphones (Black)]], [[ASIN:B0054L4AD8 AKG K311 In-Ear Headphones (Arctic Blue)]]. All sounded good for inexpensive earbuds, however the JBL and AKG were standouts, with Panasonic next and JVC last. JBL and AKG sounded very realistic with good, crisp treble and audible/realistic but not overpowering bass. JVC treble was harsh. All were comfortable in my medium size ears. AKG and JVC stayed in well while jogging, as did JBL when worn with the removable foam covers. I'd rate the AKG and JBL as tied for best sound. The AKG at about half the JBL price is the winner. I plan to use the AKG, JBL, and Panasonic but will give the JVC's to my daughter! Note that I have heard that these earbuds are often copied by cheap counterfeits from China so buy from a reputable seller like Amazon (some Amazon marketplace or ebay sellers may not be!). Also, individual hearing and sound tastes vary so your review may not be the same as mine. Good luck with your earbud search, hope this review helps!

title: $20 sound for $5
text:
Compared to other headphones in the economical price range, you really Can't beat these. The sound is very clear, crisp, clean, and yes it has bass, but don't expect it to rattle your skull or anything. These are also pretty loud. I usually listen to my music loud because I don't spend much on headphones so I don't have speakers attached to my ears or anything but with these I was pleasantly surprised when I had to turn down the volume.

Nothing really bad I can say about these yet. I've owned some Skull Candy's and they suck (usually defective right out the box) which is terrible since they're much more expensive than the Gumy's and yet these cheap little headphones surpasses them by far. I guess if you have about $10 you can get these or the Sony MDRE828LP/SLV Lightweight Earbuds which have better bass, but are double the price.

I recommend these for anyone wanting a new pair, replacement, for iPods, MP3 players, laptops, etc. Joggers will love the fact they don't fall out of your ears.

title: These earbuds survived nearly 5 years of constant torture!
text:
I've been working for nearly ten years at a factory, and have been using an iPod for about 7 of those. My original earbuds wore out within the first two years of use, and I was looking for some cheap replacements that weren't crap. I found a package of these at Wal-Mart or something, and I've used them ever since.

Last night, after five years of nearly daily use, one of the earbuds stopped working due to the cord catching on something and snapping off. A year ago, the left-side earbud was damaged by a piece of work equipment and cracked a bit, but continued working perfectly even with a chunk missing and the gummy bit partially ripped off. With the gummy bit damaged, earwax easily built up over time inside it, and even with my best efforts, still collected in the inner workings of it. The man section of the cord was cut in multiple spots, and part of the rubber rubbed away through constant friction on my clothes/me. It dealt with extremely hot summers and swam in sweat for hours on end, day in day out, sometimes would get caught on things and yanked out, all sorts of damaging instances.

Throughout that whole five years, they never stopped working properly. Not even losing sound for an instant in any of the above cases. It took getting ripped off the cord itself for the earbud to stop working. These are top-quality products. What I'm saying is, there is no better earbud for your money. Thirty dollars for official iPod earbuds when these are what amounts to The Little Earbuds That Could for at most 10 dollars a pair, to pick the former is sheer LUNACY. The Apple ones didn't even last two years.

BUY THESE EARBUDS IF YOU NEED EARBUDS. It's foolish to pay more for crappier ones than these!

title: BETTER THAN APPLE (no, really :-)
text:
Yes! They are just like iPhone earbuds--but better!

I hate hate HATE the new earbuds, with the rubber condoms that go in your ear. They never fit and they make me feel violated. I missed these and was debating on buying *yet another* set of iPhone earbuds. I am so glad I found these. They are white (just like Apple) and they look, feel, fit, and sound EXACTLY like Apple. But these have a tiny bit more printing on them. Other than that they are virtually identical. They are a bit gummier (2% gummy, not squishy or gooey). They are not "hard plastic" but more "firm plastic." The sound is incredible, possibly even better than the Apple ones I am always paying too much for.

BY THE WAY: There are no volume controls on the cord. Some earbuds come with those. Just so you know this is not what you are getting. They fit your iPod/iPhone, and even my Samsung Galaxy S3 just fine. There is a term for that kind of jack but I don't know (or care) what it is. All I care about is that they work and they are durable. Given that they are built almost identically to Apple's earbuds I am assuming that they will last as long (which is never long enough). Bottom line: for the price these are a steal.

title: Quality Drop
text:
I've purchased over a dozen of these headphones, and they've always been great.

However, I recently purchased a set of 3 and all were bad (soft washed-out sound with little bass).

Curious as to why the sound quality was so much worse I opened up one of the earbuds and compared it to my aging pair. Sure enough the copper ring around the driver was almost non-existent. It folded in half just picking it up, while the ring from my existing pair was much thicker and took a substantial amount of force to bend. Plus it was much more difficult to open my older pair because it had a much sturdier construction.

It's possible that they've improved and I was sent a set of 3 from a very old batch. Regardless, don't buy them from Online Daily Deals (they apparently have a bad/old batch).

title: So far, SOLID wireless headphones from V-Moda
text:
This won't be a full review yet because I just got my pair a couple of days ago from V-Moda, but so far they are awesome.

Coming from using the M100 religiously, they sound equal to actually significantly better in some areas.

The M100 is great for bass while keeping everything else crystal clear. The Crossfade Wireless seems to improve on the mid clarity while tightening up the bass and keepin it punchy.
This goes for wired and wireless and I honestly can barely tell a difference in sound quality between wired and wireless.

The construction is very much like the M100 and I used my XL ear pads on the wireless. I opted for the gunmetal version and although mines has a blue tint to them I still really like them, they just seem different that I expected.

The pairing was easy enough and I know for my iPhone 6, that the notifications screen shows the battery percentage while the main screen shows a new battery bar by the phones battery bar that shows how much juice the Crossfade Wireless has left in it. I have used them wirelessly for around 5 hours so far and it shows about 60% battery left.

The controls feel good and seem sturdy and reliable. They work a lot like the three button remotes on apple headphones.

I really like that there is a wired mode that immediately shuts down wireless mode as soon as you plug it into a 3.5mm jack. This turns off the battery and allows for unlimited listening in wired mode whereas some wireless headphones always need the battery to be used.

My only issue comes from the M100. Cliqfold and the lack of it. The M100 came with an awesome feature called cliqfold that allowed the headphones to fold up really nice and compact. That feature seems to have been omitted here and I don't see a logical reason why just yet. They are still very portable so I didn't feel it enough to dock a star for.

Overall they are great wireless headphones from a company that initially never seemed like they would make wireless headphones. I feel a lot of time went into tuning and although my experience with wireless Bluetooth headphones is limited, I know these are the best I've heard. These are easy to recommend and I'll keep updating my review as I have more time with them.

UPDATE 1:
Forgot to mention that comfort for the Crossfade Wireless is similar to the M100. With the stock earcups comfort is good but after a few hours it is not great. I recommend the XL Earcups if you experience a good deal of discomfort after long term use. I do have a big head so try out the standard cups first but for me the XL earcups add a lot more comfort.

title: Incredible sound and comfort
text: These V-moda headphones are unique in design, comfort and sound. First of all, out of the box, it comes with a case and velcroed into the case is a wire to connect the headphones to the device in case of low power or if you wanted to save battery time. It comes also with a charger cable and, of course the headphones. The packaging is unique with clips and sturdy cardboard. (I am not sure why there has to be such quality with an outer box that will probably be discarded.) There are instruction manuals and warranty guides. The instructions are clear and pairing with your device extremely easy. Once paired, the sound is crisp and clear. The bass is well realized. Clarity is perfect for jazz, classical, or pop. Interestingly, there is no discernible difference between wireless mode and using the wire. I have used the headphones to watch several movies and having them on my ears remained comfortable for several hours. Controls are easy to reach and quite intuitive unlike many headphones. These are the most expensive headphones I own and I can tell by the quality and the sound. I love them.

title: Freedom of cordless beats out the need for EQ
text:
I own a lot of headphones. I am somewhat of a headphone junkie. I own several pairs of V-MODA headphones including the older wired pair of the over the ear Crossfades. They are excellent headphones but they are not my first choice for everyday use. I have been using my Audio technica ATM-M50's as my daily headphones for probably over a year now. Sometimes I switch it up to get a different sound signature but the M50's are just so well balanced that I have a difficult time finding something that can compete in this proce range.

But...enter wireless headphones. I have a few sets including a nice pair of senheiser active noise cancelling ones but I haven't found a great set that was free of soem issue (the Senheisers volume is too low for me). When I was offered as et of these I jumped at the chance because I have had good luck with V-MODA.

Design and comfort - Like the older Crossfades I have, these are some of the most comfortable headphones I own. I can wear these for hours. The design is beautiful and you don;t feel silly wearing them like I do with my M50's. having no crod flying around makes these very easy to use while cutting the lawn, on a train or just lounging around the house.

Pairing - I had no issues pairing this to my Iphone 5S. Following the included instaruction, I was up and running within a minute or so.

Battery life - This is one area that I am hoping I will see improvements. The first 2 charges have not lasted very long. I have gotten about 6 hours per charge so far and I believe these are supposed to last more like 12. I know some batteries improve with a few uses so I am hoping that is the case here. Or it is possible that the rated battery life is based on lower volumes or something. I tend to listen loud so maybe that is killing my battery.

Sound - These headphones were a bit disappointing at first. Coming off the M50's and having my ears trained to hear those, I found these headphones a bit flat and a bit too bass heavy at first. I tend to listen to music with no EQ with my M50's but I find I need to EQ these headphones a bit. I have been playing around with various settings (on Spotify) and find that a treble boost seems to take away some of the "muddy" lowe end sound. It is not perfect but it helps a lot. I think these are just designed to push the bass a bit more since people think that equals quality. As far as soundstage, I find these to be very up front with little soundstage. Great for heavy rock music that I listen to. However, I do get some separation at times wich makes them feel a bit more full. But not a wide soundsatage by any means. If you are listebing to orchestra type music, I would try these before you buy to make sure they work well for that environment.

Cord vs Cordless - the great news so far is that I haven't heard any difference between the two with quality of the music. Running cordless, these are LOUD headphones with my 5S. I am running them at about 75% volume which is in line with my M50's. I find they run the same with the cord. I have had no dropped sound running wireless. These just work well.

Overall these are going to be with me for the near term. I love the fact that I am no longer restricted by a cord to get great sound. I can live with the need to EQ to deal with the low end issue (although this does not work with amazon music) . These are definitley worth considering if you are in the market for quality cordless headphones

title: I'm in love with these headphones. Comfortable for hours, amazing sound quality, beautifully made.
text:
I'm in love with these headphones. I'm a huge headphone nerd and have probably a dozen pairs of varying styles and brands -- I have an old pair of M100 Crossfades that've served me well, and the new wireless option caught my attention.

V-MODA over-the-hear Crossfades are a huge win: they look beautiful, with quality craftsmanship and design, and sound even better. The slick design is comfortable for hours of wear - usually 6-8/day for me - without any issues. They aren't isolating or active sound-blocking, but the enclosed memory foam earcup keeps sound from leaking and lets me enjoy my music without having to crank it up.

Bass kicks without drowning out mids; trebels are tight and sound great without being flat or tinny. The sound quality between wired and Bluetooth is essentially the exact same - a relief, given some BT headphones are kind of lossy.

The wired/wireless dual option is so convenient: the included cable is thoughtfully and well-designed, too, making it prepared for any and all uses without fraying or falling apart. The cable also has controls for volume built-in, which is handy when your phone or iPod is in your bag/pocket. The battery life is at least ten hours over BlueTooth, and it's a godsend when I'm working or at the gym. Pairing is quick and painless, taking just a second.

title: A quality experience from arrival to the day that they will eventually be taken off my head.
text:
This is my first foray into the world of V-Moda and from the first moment I took them out of the box my inner voice said, "What took you so long" referencing my reluctance to take the plunge to try them.

My first impression was how light they are. One would expect these things to weigh a ton (which I think was my original resistance) but they are actually light and feel very balanced. They, in a word are awe-inspiring just to look at in the package. V-Moda seems to pride themselves on the presentation and getting the message across that "We don't just look good, we act good" which is regards to their warranty and service dialogues.

My nephew (a gamer) made almost identical noises as he did when he saw the most recent Star Wars trailer when he saw the empty V-Moda box on the table. A reaction that also let me know that the V-Moda marketing works! But let's take a listen.

The headset is comfortable with a soft by firm squeeze to my head. Pairing was a cinch (iPhone6) and sound was pretty remarkable just listening to mp3's on my phone. It did take me a while to figure out that there is no identifiable microphone (because it's built in) and everyone seemed to hear me fine (nephew interrupted this review to tell me that he would get the sides customized at the V-Moda site but I'll explain that in a minute. The other part of his intrusion was to say HE would purchase the optional external mic that sits in front of your mouth. He said it is more comfortable for him to know where his voice is being sent??). I mention this only to make you aware there are accessories!

The thing the impresses me almost as much as the sound is the comfort of these after wearing them the entire time of writhing this review which is after nearly an hour of TV and Music. I am impressed that it will sync with two devices over bluetooth, like a phone or a laptop (meaning you don't have to unlink one to link to the other).

Sound quality didn't change from wired to wireless (which shocks me) but there was a noticeable drain on battery (nothing you wouldn't expect) so it's good to know that they can be wired without loosing your connection. The sides can be customized very easily through their website, and V-Moda doesn't spare the sense of excitement in that process either. You can make your ear coverings the color of your favorite light saber and have your favorite Empire engraved onto it for around $50 dollars.

The V-Moda, for me, sets high standards that they stand behind with a sense of fearless pride. From their "50% off Immortal Program" to their use of "vegan leather" and cross-fade technology their message is clear - if there was a top, we are over it!

V-Moda seems to pride themselves on the presentation and getting the message across that "We don't just look good, we act good" which is regards to their warranty and service dialogues.

My nephew (a gamer) made almost identical noises as he did when he saw the most recent Star Wars trailer when he saw the empty V-Moda box on the table. A reaction that also let me know that the V-Moda marketing works! But let's take a listen.

The headset is comfortable with a soft by firm squeeze to my head. Pairing was a cinch (iPhone6) and sound was pretty remarkable just listening to mp3's on my phone. It did take me a while to figure out that there is no identifiable microphone (because it's built in) and everyone seemed to hear me fine (nephew interrupted this review to tell me that he would get the sides customized at the V-Moda site but I'll explain that in a minute. The other part of his intrusion was to say HE would purchase the optional external mic that sits in front of your mouth. He said it is more comfortable for him to know where his voice is being sent??). I mention this only to make you aware there are accessories!

The thing the impresses me almost as much as the sound is the comfort of these after wearing them the entire time of writhing this review which is after nearly an hour of TV and Music. I am impressed that it will sync with two devices over bluetooth, like a phone or a laptop (meaning you don't have to unlink one to link to the other).

Sound quality didn't change from wired to wireless (which shocks me) but there was a noticeable drain on battery (nothing you wouldn't expect) so it's good to know that they can be wired without loosing your connection. title: Probably the best bluetooth headphones out there so far, but not perfect yet.
text:
To be completely honest here, I'm a pretty big V-Moda fan when it comes to their crossfade line. I've owned the LP, the LP2, the M-100, and now these. I've had the chance to see just what V-Moda can do with their sounds.

The crossfade wireless is advertised, more or less, an M-100 with bluetooth and re-tuned drivers. Unfortunately, the only thing it truly retains from the M-100 is the way it looks.

Looking at the outside of the headphones, they're the same beautiful V-Moda crossfades that we've seen throughout their line--with buttons. The buttons look nice. They aren't obtrusive and they don't make you stand out like a lighthouse should you walk around with these in the middle of the night. The only light on the headphone is a fairly dim power light on the power switch. With that being said, I dislike the buttons. On the bottom of the headphone, we have the switch. Nothing wrong here, very sturdy feel to it. But at the top, we have the three buttons we will be using the most--Multi-Function (Play/Pause/Command), Volume up, and volume down. These three buttons feel flimsy to me and for worse, they are kind of hard to press, for some reason presenting resistance particularly when I try to turn the volume down. Perhaps they made it this way to avoid accidental pressing, but these buttons are right underneath the metal clip that holds the band to the cans so I'd imagine it would be somewhat difficult to bump into something that would hit the buttons here.

On the inside, we have a whole new story. If you're coming from the M-100, these are supposed to sound the same. Even after burn-in, the sound felt almost hollow to me, compared to the M-100. The bass was lacking, both on bluetooth and wireless, which is what most seem to buy V-Modas for. The mids were recessed, but this is no change from the M-100. The highs were also present, so no change here. Somewhere along the line, V-Moda tweaked these headphones and dropped (upped?) the bass from the M-100s. These headphones also lack aptX lossless/low-latency codec which is a major disappointment in this price range. The Sony MDR10BT has it and costs less. What gives, V-Moda?

The other thing to note in regards to the bluetooth is that if you listen to softer music, you may notice a near-silent static playing along with your music. This seems to be the standard for bluetooth headphones.

Other notes:
- The micro USB charging port is on the LEFT cup, while the 3.5mm plug is on the RIGHT cup. I prefer my wire on the left side, so this is entirely up to user preference.
- These lose the cliquefold mechanism that was so popular with the M-100. Bluetooth is intended for mobility, so it's strange that this would get removed, but it may be a design limitation here. If you're coming from the M-100, expect the larger LP case.
- These can be paired and connected with more than one device at a time, but can only play one at a time. This is pretty interesting, since the M-100s had two ports so that you could either listen to two sources at once or daisy chain your headphones. Unfortunately you can not stream to the cans and use the 3.5mm port as an audio-out.
- If you have the M-100s, or really any headphones that have a removable audio-in cable and want wireless, I'd check out these: [[ASIN:B0134DTP9Q BTunes VXB-35 (3.5mm Model) To Make Wired Headphones Wireless for Beats, Monster, Sony, V-Moda, Marshalls and more]]. I'm ended up returning my Crossfade Wireless and buying this instead.

title: Love these!!
text:
I already had a couple of V-Moda headphones [[ASIN:B00GO4GMHQ V-MODA XS On-Ear Folding Design Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone (White Silver)]] and [[ASIN:B003BYRGKE V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-Ear Noise-Isolating Metal Headphone (Rouge)]] both of which I have been satisfied with, but honestly I haven't been using them that much lately because they were not wireless and when I go to the gym or listen to music before I go to sleep, the wire just got in the way. Luckily I also had the [[ASIN:B00KGGK71A Samsung Level Over-Ear Bluetooth Headphone - Retail Packaging - Black]] which are an excellent set of headphones that I used in the gym as well as occasionally before I go to sleep. The downside to these otherwise great headphones is that they are huge and tend to get hot with prolonged use. I attempted to use the Bluetooth adapter with my wired VModa headphones, but they were too tacky and too cumbersome to use.

Introducing the WIRELESS V-Moda Crossfade over the head headphones!!! In short these headphones are excellent in almost every way. They combine the great sound from my wired V-Moda headphones with the convenience of wireless capability of my Samsung level over set. Comparing these with the Samsungs which sound excellent I would say these sound slightly better with a little deeper bass and fuller sound. A big advantage of these over the Samsungs is that they are more comfortable to wear. They do not get hot and because they are so light weight I can wear them for an extended period of time without them being uncomfortable. They also look great and offer customizable choices of ear plates ranging from $20 to well over $400 for the precious metal options.

Connecting these to your Bluetooth enabled devices is a snap, just set follow the easy to read instructions included in the packaging and you'll be connected to your phone, tablet, or music device in seconds. Another great option (which are also on the Samsungs) is if your battery is low or don't want to use Bluetooth, then you can plug in a standard earphone wire (included) into the side and these immediately turn into a wired set of headphones. This is also convenient for gaming because while they are wireless, my PS4 does not recognize these headphones when trying to connect them to my console via Bluetooth. I wish I could use the wireless option for my PS4, but that is not the fault of these headphones.

These headphones have many of the same features as the Samsungs, but there is one thing the Samsungs do a little better. On the Level Overs, volume control and track skipping are controlled by a integrated touch pad embedded in the right earpiece. So simply running your finger up over the side of these headphones would instantly turn the volume up, and running your finger down, will turn the volume down. Track skipping/backtracking is controlled by forward and backwards motions with your finger. To pause you just simply tap your finger and to resume tap your finger again. While the V-Moda can do the same thing, these functions are controlled by physical buttons. There are two buttons for volume up and volume down, and a single button that controls track skipping as well as pausing/resuming. To pause just tap the button once, to skip to the next track tap the button twice, but your timing has to be just right or it will just pause the song. In addition there doesn't seem to be a way to go back to the previous track.

Other than the downside I mentioned these are excellent high quality comfortable headphones that should leave you satisfied for a long time.

title: Excellent!
text:
I will jump straight to the point. Please keep in mind that I am not an audiophile, but do pursue better quality audio products where it matters.

* Size, Weight, Packaging: These full size over-the-ear headphones have moderate weight, a bit on the heavy side comparing to regular headphones but not much different from the weight of noise-cancelling or wireless over-the-ear phones. They are not portable and come with a custom-molded very nice black hard case with a zipper. Two cables are included: male-male 3.5" audio cable and a flat micro-USB cable for charging, as well as an RCA Y-to-3.5" adapter and a small instruction booklet.

* Comfort: The headband is a bit tight, but this keeps the phones tightly and securely positioned on your head. Absolutely no wobbling! The leather (or leather-like -- I am not sure exactly) material of covering the headband and ear cushions is nice and soft. It feels a bit hot around the ears after wearing them for about 1 hour, but not too uncomfortable.

* Sound Quality: I am more than satisfied with the range and the quality of the highs and lows. The sound feels "just right" -- very comfortably soft, not too high or crackling and not too low to the point of being boomy.

* Operation: The headphones hold the charge very well. To turn the power on and off, you will need to slide a switch, which is easy to slide with one finger. The power button is inconspicuously located on the outer side (not along the perimeter, as in some headphones), so it takes getting used to finding it by touch. This multi-function button is the only control element: you use it for pairing with a Bluetooth receiver as well. Every function -- turning on, off, going into pairing mode or having paired is confirmed by a distinct and pleasant sound in the headphones.

Pairing is a breeze. To make these headphones work with my TV and receiver, I have purchased from Amazon.com a Bluetooth transmitter by TaoTronics. Both work very well together, although after a few days of non-operation they needed to be re-paired. Pairing does not require entering any codes: just put both devices in discovery mode and they will magically pair in a few seconds. Pairing with an Android phone and iPad (both up-to-date with their system software) was just as easy and required no codes. If codes are required, a small instruction booklet included with the headphones lists them.

The shields on both sides are metal and come covered with protective film. I have noticed a bit of glue residue one one side after removing this film, and this is the only negative comment that I can make. In other words, I am very satisfied with these headphones.

title: I've got no strings on me!
text:
I love running with over-ear headphones, and lately my Crossfade M-100s have been my go-to cans for that. The one thing that I've always hated while running with any headphones is dealing with the cords - pulling earbuds out of my ears, rubbing and getting in the way of arm movement with on-ear or over-ear, etc. I can tuck them in my shirt or whatever, but then they're annoying and pull when I turn my head. And let's be honest - most cordless headphones sound like garbage. Been there, done that, returned it. Yeah, first world problems but why not shoot for perfection? The only reason I even gave these a shot is because they're V-MODA and I'm not just surprised, I'm blown away.

V-MODA claims that these sound equivalent to wired headphones. I'm going to disagree for my most common use case - connected directly to my iPhone 6S. In this case, they sound a bit better. The integrated amplified delivers more and cleaner bass presence than my iPhone can. Not as good as with a standalone DAC/amp, but I'd say about 30% better than the iPhone alone - which is not a subtle improvement, and without the distortions introduced by the iPhone's electronic equalizer. You can practically see the strings on a bass guitar vibrating in your mind, and the bass drums have a beautiful kick. Highs and mids still feature V-MODA's trademark clarity and nice, even frequency response. So yes, the sound is wonderful, which is what everyone really cares about. I've seen some complaints in forums, but as far as I can tell these have been narrowed down to devices that just can't send good quality audio over Bluetooth. I haven't personally had any issues yet, but I've only tested with my iPhone and MacBook Pro. Charging is accomplished with a standard micro-USB cable, so most people won't have to worry about carrying extra cords or chargers to keep the Crossfade Wireless topped up while traveling. Battery life hasn't yet been an issue. They come with a typically excellent V-MODA travel case, the sort that puts every other brand to shame but V-MODA buyers have become pleasantly used to.

Minor quibbles:
* No cliq-fold hinges like the M-100s and XS. Sorry, V-MODA, you spoiled us and it's hard to go back.
* A single button for pause / resume / track-forward / track-back. I suck at pressing these fast enough, so I always wind up just pausing it.

I'm pretty nit-picky about things, so that's a pretty short list. I'm loving these so far!
