Overall great build quality, decent sound that probably needs an eq to be optimized, negligible ANC, and a lack of ability to fold up small and throw in my gym bag.

For my purpose of gym use I thought they were a hard pass, and I would suggest sticking with the cheaper so drop 2's

title: Just what I wanted, great customer support
text:
I originally bought the $99 Acoustic Sheep bluetooth setup, which worked fine, but having to disconnect and reconnect the battery every day was a pain. I talked to support about it, and they referred me to the Effortless, and I upgraded right away, no hassle and they refunded my original purchase gladly. I would have bought the Effortless originally, but despite doing a lot of product research on Amazon I didn't realize they existed.

Anyway, this product does exactly what I want.

First, the mechanical aspect. The speakers are flat, thin, and flexible. You can lie your head down directly on your side on a pillow and the speakers still work. You might notice that they are present, but they aren't uncomfortable.

Second, the sound. Well mostly I am using them for noise blocking, which means I usually have my white noise app playing. Sound quality doesn't matter too much. When I do play music it sounds fine. You're not going to get any bass out of a speaker this size, and that's not their fault, it's the laws of physics.

Third, the convenience. The charger is very easy to use, you just line it up on the charging base until the magnet grabs it and the light starts blinking, walk away and forget about it.

Fourth, the Bluetooth controls. I'm able to change the volume with relative ease while lying down, I don' t need to fumble around and find my phone. I do think this is on area for potential product improvement - it would be great to have external controls in a fixed position. As it is you have to find them through the fabric of the headband. No big deal.

All in all, this product is exactly what I wanted and it performs exactly as I hoped.

title: Extremely cheap components for large amounts of money
text:
I really really really wanted to love these headphones. I really did. I have been looking for the perfect pair of Sleeping headphones, and these are very far from the best.

Take note; I have tried every type of these, the wired ones, the wireless ones, and now these "effortless" ones.

The wired ones were probably the best, as there is no battery to worry about. The issue is that the cable broke within a few months. I'm not sure what they expect, as you move around when you sleep, that cable is going to get bent. Bulk up that cheap cable.

The wireless one was awful because taking out the component to charge it was an incredible hassle. Most cheap wireless headbands just have a cable that pokes out and you plug it in there, the sleephones you have to take the entire wireless unit out, unplug it from the headphones, and plug it in to a cable.

So after not wishing to deal with that, I decided to go with the "effortless" ones. And oh boy was that a mistake. They advertise these to last 12 hours on one charge. And they did! The first couple of nights, I didn't exactly sleep for that long, but one night I decided to sleep a bit early, and they lasted an entire 13 hour bed session. Awesome! Then, a few days later, I tried sleeping early again, and they died in the middle of my sleep, within about 8 hours. Now, the next night, as I'm writing this, they did not even last 6 hours. They don't even last a proper amount of sleep, and I think I know why.

Induction charging is notoriously bad. It wastes a ton of energy, and gets very hot. I decided to check the unit while it was charging, and it was incredibly hot. This thing is burning its poor battery to smithereens. Clearly they did not test this at all. I don't even know how anyone can give this a positive review. Sleep headphones should last AS LONG as a normal sleep schedule. This was an extreme waste of $150

The sound quality is fine. They are comfortable tho I do wish they covered your eyes, you can spin them around tho and you can put the larger part over your eyes. However battery life is an absolute joke. I bought these like 2 weeks ago and they already don't even last 6 hours. This is pretty much a scam.

Additionally, if I take one ear piece out to make sure i can hear my surroundings for whatever reason, the weight of the hanging ear piece falls down my chest and pulls on my neck and other ear uncomfortably. Overall, these are not bad ear phones, but they just don't quite fit me right.

title: Must-buy For Console Gamers
text:
I have been someone who's gamed for along time using over-ear headsets like Turtle Beach, Triton, Astros, etc. but I started using earbuds because I kept sweating too much. These headphones are perfect for someone who has to/likes to wear glasses when gaming, someone who doesn't like over-ear style, or someone looking for a high-quality headset for really cheap. -Great sound quality (bass, mids, and treble all come through)
-Can be used with the sound mixer (Xbox One)
-Choice of built-in or add-on mic
-A lot of accessories (rubber inserts for ear piece, foam inserts for ear piece, extensions that hold headphones to ear, leather case, external mic)
-Braided cable does not get tangled and is durable
-External mic is of really good quality
-They last (I've had them for months now)
-Price -> I spent 1/10 of what I would normally spend on headset and got something that works better for me

Cons:
-No mute switch (could be pro or con, I prefer simplicity)
-Sometimes the mic built into the headphones sounds odd to my friends. Likely and issue with the connection to the Xbox One Controller (easily fixed with external mic)

title: Sound Good, But Button Design is Frustrating!
text:
Bluetooth headphones are one of those items that have finally started to become less expensive for the unwashed masses. Sure, Bluetooth earpieces have been available for cell phone use for years, but a set of nice cordless headphones with a solid connection (earlier Bluetooth versions didn't always transmit sound reliably) that don't require breaking the bank are being released in droves.

So MEElectronics® provided me with a sample of their Rumble Bluetooth Headphone set, and after a couple of weeks of use, I can comment below:

Construction

The MEElectronics® Rumble headset (aka MRH) comes in at 5.3oz (146g), with thick, leather-wrapped, soft ear pads and a plastic frame. The headset allows each earpiece to fold up, enabling the entire set to become compact enough to fit inside of a felt drawstring bag (included). Unfortunately, while these metal hinges do "lock", there is still a tendency for the sides to fold inward when manipulating the headset. In one instance I pinched my finger, but I attribute that more to my own clumsiness than a design flaw. That being said, exercise caution if you are adjusting the fit so that you don't accidentally pinch your own skin.

There are three buttons on the left earpiece which control volume, play/pause, and track forward/back. There is no dedicated power button; you simply press the play/pause button to turn on the headset, as well as initiating the sync mode. The microphone and audio jack port are also on the left side, with the right side having the micro-USB port used for charging the unit.

Function

First and foremost, the headset packs good sound. The bass is pronounced while still keeping the vocals of each song clear. While all of the songs that I listened to, ranging from Mozart, classic rock, modern rock, punk, & reggae to the crooning of broken-hearted country ballads, sounded good, I couldn't shake the feeling that the quality was only a step or two better than a basic car stereo. While that within itself is not an especially bad thing, the MRH should sound much better than it does. All of this being said, 95% of the time the headset sounds great and plays songs with a drum and guitar track much more pronounced. The other 5%, however, especially if there is a really strong bass to a song, makes it sound like you are missing some of the music.

The only other issue that I have is in regard to the operation of the headset buttons. While it is not unusual for buttons on a smaller device to do double duty, the programming of the MRH is frustrating. Each button that controls the track selection is also used to adjust the volume. Where most headsets would require you to hold down a button to adjust the volume while allowing a quick press to change the song, the Rumble is the exact opposite. As such you are forced to hold down the buttons to change the tracks, making it next to impossible to 1) not adjust the volume, and 2) jump to the next song since the button is inexact. As a result, it was easier to use my iPod to change songs and only use the MRH for volume control.

My last issue concerns the buttons and general control of the headset. Whenever you manually advance a song and/or adjust the volume, the headset makes a beeping noise. While the beep is not too annoying when you are selecting a song, the volume control is downright aggravating when you use a slide bar (such as on an iPod). The MRH will beep continuously until you remove your finger from the volume control; using the buttons on the headset prevents the annoying sound from being nonstop, if nothing else.

Final Say

While the sound quality and aesthetic design of the MEElectronics® Rumble is pretty good, there are still several features of the headset that range from annoying to just a plain bad design. Most of the issues that I have with the MEElectronics® Rumble are easily rectified, however, so I am hoping that MEElectronics® will be able to incorporate some of the feedback into improving their next Bluetooth headset. Until then, I think that there are too many flaws for me to give this product a strong recommendation.

I have already requested a refund.

title: Even with some cons, they're 5 star worth
text:
I got them by luck, I was having a hard time picking a good Bluetooth Headphone, I was torn between the MEElectronics Air-Fi Venture and the Photive BTH3. All in all, I was looking for a Wireless + Wired Bluetooth Headphone in the 50$ish price range. Looking for reviews, both in and out of Amazon, including manufacturers page, I stumbled across the MEElectronics Air-Fi Rumble and the Enhanced-Bass got my attention right away. (I love a deep, strong, punchy bass) they were up by 20$ but luckily for me they went down to 59.99$ just a few bucks more than my two first choices, so I got them right away.

Now, after I got them and tested them, I have some pros and cons about them:
+Great sound, very high volume, both wired and wireless. Good bass. (Warning: they're really loud, and the sound isn't isolated, so beware while using in public space or office space, those at full volume could pass by a small speaker, lol)
+Comes with a neat carry bag and cables.
+Wired&Wireless function (you can also use the wired without battery or while charging)
+Looks like good battery life, but I'll have to use them more to see how that goes. Will update if necessary.
+Incredible range, with my Moto G I can walk around the house almost from an entire side to another and just aaalmost at the end they start to lose signal, still, I'm really impressed in a good way.
+- (again, a pro and a con), even though they're not entirely over-the-ear, more like on-ear, they are comfortable and because they're on-ear, they hang tight in there, you can use them at the top or hanging at the back, and they will stay in position.
-Only three buttons for basically almost everything you can imagine, while you have the other side totally free to add at least three more buttons, they decided to add a bunch of ways to press the buttons so you have every possible option in one side, bad choice imho.
-Foldable, not a fan of that (for me, the less things they have to potentially broke, the better)

Even though there are some cons, they're 5 star worth for me.

Edit: I recently had some issues related to the bluetooth drivers and I contacted MEElectronics for support, they were quick in responding and did a great job assisting me. Another good thing for them, since I value customer service a lot!

title: Amazing first impressions.
text:
I only had this product for about 12 hours and already love it! My opinion might change a little in future from small little issues but my first impression is highly positive.

First of all, it looks gorgeous. It's very shiny and the ear cuffs look nice as well. It looks like it's worth just as much as some higher end headphones. The headphones are also very light and comfortable. Adjusting for the size of your head is also very simple and it doesn't move out of place.

The sound is also very good considering I got this for $40 on sale. I've had listened to beats headphones before and it's quite not up there in terms of sound quality and volume but it's very close. On max volume, I'm highly satisfied with the sound and bass. I can bump to any song with the best experience.

The Bluetooth worked instantly with no connection problems. The product comes with easy instructions on how to connect and I figured it out in 2 minutes. Once it turns on it also connects to your phone instantly.

30 feet of range? Can't get any better. The fact that I can leave my phone charging, walk to the kitchen with my headphones on and comeback is very satisfying to me. The sound quality didn't seem to change to me either. Maybe once you get near to that 30 feet mark, but my house isn't that big for that to be a problem.

These headphones also come with some useful features as well. It has a built in mic that worked perfectly for me when I ordered pizza last night. The employee had no trouble hearing me and I had no trouble hearing him. Communication was perfect. It also has a pause button and a volume up/down buttons. The pause button also serves as the on/off button, as well as the Bluetooth connection button; and the volume buttons also serve as play next, play previous, and replay button.

So overall, you definitely get the "bang for your buck". If you're just trying to get some good quality headphones without burning a hole in your pocket, this is it. Like I said in the beginning, I only had this for less than a day so I'm not sure if it will have battery issues or charging problems but all I can say is that I'm satisfied enough to be giving a review in such little time. I would recommend this product to anyone.

title: Could use improvements
text:
Pros:
It's very lightweight. Great battery life. Amazing range (with my phone, not so much with my Bluetooth adapter on my computer). Easy to set-up, but instructions can be a little confusing. Sleek design and the ability to snap the arms closed is really nice, coupled with the small carry bag. The buttons are relatively stiff, so there's no worry about brushing the headphones against anything and depressing any of the buttons. This includes laying in bed.

Cons:
Not noise-canceling whatsoever. Wearing both headphones with music playing at a moderate level, could easily hear someone talking. For reference, I can clearly hear my computer's fans (which are really quiet). This actually can be either a pro or a con. For me, I like to be able to hear my surroundings while also having music wireless transmitted to my ears. The bass is acceptable, but it's not amazing. If you're an audiophile and you're willing to pay top dollar for good headphones, steer clear. The Bluetooth microphone does NOT work with my Windows 7/Kinivo Bluetooth adapter, which is very unfortunate. I have researched this issue for several hours, and ended up emailing support (support@meelec.com) on 12/16/15. EDIT: Response as of 12/21/15.

The three horizontal buttons are a pain in the ass to use. The top and bottom buttons both have a protruding dot so that you could feel the difference (In theory). But the buttons are all pretty long, and with the power button being in the center, it's almost impossible to tell when your finger is over the power/play button. Which is basically the most important button, so you'd want quick access. Combine that with having to hold the power button for two or so seconds to turn on/off, it becomes a pain in the ass. Some sort of sliding/toggle power button would have been greatly preferred.

The clear smooth plastic finish looks great when it's first unboxed, but it's the same type of material that shows fingerprints/dirt too well, not unlike the face-plate of the Xbox One. You'll find yourself wiping it frequently if it bothers you.

Overall, could use some improvements.

title: Great Value
text:
I bought these to replace some lost EarPods. While they definitely don't stack up to the EarPods for feature functionality, they are an amazing value and definitely worth a look.

What you give up compared to EarPods is a mic for placing phone calls and interacting with Siri. You also lose any ability to locate them using your phone. They also don't have the smart features that sense when they are/aren't in your ear, so you have to do all the on/off manually.

Sound quality is good. I felt like they didn't get as loud as my ear pods, but everything sounded good while I was running outside with them. I honestly don't have super high standards for sound quality, though, so if you're a real audiophile, you can probably discount/ignore that feedback.

They are very comfortable and light weight. On a 16 mile run, I never felt the need to adjust them- they stayed in place and felt comfortable the whole time. The upside of losing the smart on/off is that you can take one out without having to do anything to keep listening. This is great for times when you need a little more awareness of your surroundings, but also want to keep listening.

title: Stays in my ears when exercising, always good sound
text:
I bought these a second time after I stepped on my first pair. I am not knocking their durability. Don't charge your headphones on the floor and then step there, its that simple. Based on the price, and my experience with this model of headphone, it was no question I'd buy the same type as replacement.

These headphones are great as athletic headphones, but have enough sound quality to enjoy any music. They have an impressive built in bass boost. I have never had an ear bud fall out while I was running, and the connecting chord between the two buds, allows you to use one headphone at a time, if you are driving, biking, or working in the office (just make sure to switch your audio source to mono).

They are Bluetooth only and therefore do not have headphone jack option, but should be fine for most people. They do have a built in microphone and are surprisingly great for hands free phone calls and video conferencing. Battery lasts all day with decently consistent use. When it comes to value for an all-around pair of Bluetooth earbuds, there is no safer choice.

title: This is really worth it! Cost-Benefit is spot on and I have paid more for equal or less
text:
I needed a noise cancelling, decent sounding, quality Bluetooth device that I can hook up to my phone for when I am doing yard work or cleaning out the garage, or misc indoor housework. I have loud kids who are going bananas sometimes if they are home (like these days). This headphone fits comfortable, is snug (the expandable or adjustable band) has good padding for covering your ears, and doesn't flop around as I move up and down and about- it stays steady on my head. The noise cancelling works great - I can see my kids hollering at me or my wife trying to get my attention- but while their lips are moving, I cant hear a thing. Even mowing the lawn, it does the best I have experienced at reducing that sound.

The sounds are rich, deep, with a great mid range and treble. Its easy to work with the controls, and its distance from device range is superior. For example, I left my paired phone on the front porch while I went into my back yard and garage, about 30-45 feet distance, and only then when I was furthest away deep in the garage, did I get a spotty connection. Otherwise, I can leave my paired device on the back deck, work in the garage and yard, no problems.

Great rich sound, also. Snug and comfortable. Excellent for what I required - tune out the world and get stuff done without disturbing people with my music or even tv audio (I stay up late, and with syncing it to my TV, nobody has to pound on the floors to get me to "Turn it down!". I am an audiophile, and have had decent Bose, JBL's and SOny, and I have to say, at this price (currently $199) you definitely get what you pay for.

title: Very good for the price I got them for
text:
My wife got these for me for Father's Day. I've had a pair of Bose AE2 (wired only, no noise cancelling) since 2014, so that's what I'll be comparing these to.

The Sony headphones have a more satisfying, deeper bass, so unlike with the Bose, I can actually use the default graphic equalizer setting on my DAP. With the Bose I found myself having to reset the equalizer setting to maximize bass. The highs are not as bright as on the Bose. Besides that, my ears can't detect any other differences in sound quality.

I got the blue tooth to work, but the volume levels were super low compared to when they were wired. I actually listen to them wired most of the time, so not a big deal. However, the aux cable that came with these headphones was a foot too short for my liking.

The headphones themselves are bulkier on the ears than the Bose, and I can't sleep with them on, which is a bummer because I fall asleep faster with music playing.

As with the Bose, these headphones get very warm when worn outside at temperatures in the 70s or more, especially in direct sunlight.

The noise cancelling feature could be better. As has already been noted, it gets rid of low frequencies pretty well, but other frequencies not so well. The sound quality with noise cancelling off is just as good as when it's on, which I like a lot.

Overall, at $140, I'd say these are an upgrade

The Sony headphones have a more satisfying, deeper bass, so unlike with the Bose, I can actually use the default graphic equalizer setting on my DAP. With the Bose I found myself having to reset the equalizer setting to maximize bass. The highs are not as bright as on the Bose. Besides that, my ears can't detect any other differences in sound quality.

I got the blue tooth to work, but the volume levels were super low compared to when they were wired. I actually listen to them wired most of the time, so not a big deal. However, the aux cable that came with these headphones was a foot too short for my liking.

The headphones themselves are bulkier on the ears than the Bose, and I can't sleep with them on, which is a bummer because I fall asleep faster with music playing.

As with the Bose, these headphones get very warm when worn outside at temperatures in the 70s or more, especially in direct sunlight.

The noise cancelling feature could be better. As has already been noted, it gets rid of low frequencies pretty well, but other frequencies not so well. The sound quality with noise cancelling off is just as good as when it's on, which I like a lot.

Overall, at $140, I'd say these are an upgrade

title: Review from a non-tech guy
text:
I wanted to provide a review, without using technical jargon, for the average person to understand. This is my first pair of quality headphones. For years I have just been using the free earphones that come with my phones. After using these, I’ve realized what I’ve been missing all these years.

Unboxing:
There weren’t too many highlights with unboxing these headphones. It comes in very basic packaging. The headphones are wrapped in a thin layer of foam and come with a headphone cable and usb type c cable for charging. Also in the box was a quick setup guide and an instruction booklet. Keep in mind, these do not come with a case or carrying pouch, so you may want to invest in one if you play on traveling with these.

Set-up/Pairing/Navigation:
After charging the headphones, pairing them with my phone and laptop were simple via bluetooth. No issues here. It took less than 30 seconds.

The headphones have multiple navigation buttons to turn the volume up or down and to skip songs. This takes a day to get used to since you have to feel around for the buttons while they are on your head. Since I am always on my phone, I found it easier to just use my phone to control these settings.

Sound quality:
For years I just used the free earphones that came with my phones. I never really understood why someone would want bulky headphones. However, after using these, I was amazed by the sound quality. It was as if all the songs I’ve been listening to over the years suddenly became more vibrant and clear. I loved the experience of using the headphones to listen to my music. I was able to hear parts of songs I’ve listened to hundreds of times and never noticed before.

For voice calls, the headphones were crystal clear.

Noise Cancelling:
The smart noise cancelling feature seemed to be hit or miss for me. It did a great job with background noises like white noises (vacuum, dryer, street noise, bus, etc). However, I found that it didn’t cancel the conversations people around me were having. I was hoping to use these in the office, but I don’t think they would be ideal for a talkative office environment.

Overall:
Overall, I would definitely recommend these headphones. I have been wearing these non-stop since I got them, even when I’m alone in the house, because the audio quality is much better than any headphone or speakers I have used in the past.

title: Modern look, very good noise cancellation, good sound
text:
The WHCH710N headphones are one of the better Sony wireless over ear headphones I've used. The noise cancellation is very good and may be the standout feature on these. The fit is good but some users might not like the plastic feel of the headband. It was actually uncomfortable at first but after wearing them for a few hours, I got used to the feel and now I'm a fan of both the headband and ear cups.

Sonically, these are ok. The audio quality is crisp and clear but bass is lacking, partially due to the smallish 30mm drivers. There is bass, and it's more pronounced with ANC off, which is standard on all NC headphones I've used. These aren't designed as a "maximum bass" headphone so it probably won't be an issue for most users. I've listened to a lot of music genres on these including pop, rock, metal, electronic, jazz, and classical and I'm happy with the relatively balanced sound. For spoken word, audio is clear and easy to understand.

The Bluetooth connectivity on these is good. Standard stuff. Also has an NFC connection if your device supports that. I tested both and it connects right away. Not much to report there, I was expecting that to work well and it does.

Battery life is good and a wired cable is included if your battery runs out or if you need to work in zero latency mode for something like music creation. There's no case included but there are some available as a separate purchase if needed. I have an old Astro headphone case that these fit in that I use for storage and travel.

Overall, a nice set of Bluetooth ANC headphones. I like the over hear closed back design. I like the sound quality and comfort, and I'm a fan of the overall look. These aren't perfect but at this price point they are a reliable, good sounding pair of headphones that should last a long time.

title: Nice headphones but a lousy unboxing experience
text:
These Sony WHCH710N noise-cancelling over-the-ear headphones boast a 35-hour battery life with quick charging, 30mm drivers with active noise-cancellation and Bluetooth with NFC connectivity.

What I liked most about these Sony WHCH710N noise-cancelling over-the-ear headphones was:
- The sound. I admit to being initially skeptical of these cans because of the 30mm drivers as most of my favorite over-ear-headphones have 40mm+ drivers but the sound coming out of these is big and immersive. While not the richest or most nuanced sound you can find for 200 dollars this headset has a nice separation of mids and highs with deep, punchy bass. There's even a hint of soundstage, but this is much more muted with these cans than others in this product line.
- Battery life. Opting for 30mm drivers allows Sony to give users longer battery life. While 35 hours might be possible if you keep your headset at 50% volume without ANC activated, I was able to get 25-27 consistently with the cans cranked up to 75% most of the time. I used ANC roughly a third of the time I had my cans on.
- Active noise-cancelling and sound isolation. These cans have sufficient clamping force to drown out a good deal of background noise without activating noise-cancelling. Once you activate noise-cancelling you have the choice of allowing some sound in or toning it out at this headset's maximum capacity with Sony suggests is about 75%.
- Easy NFC pairing. Once you've paired a headset via NFC you'll never, ever want to do it the old fashioned way again. With NFC pairing, even if the headset is off, aligning your source device's NFC chip with the NFC insignia on these headphones will turn them on and automatically pair them.

What I liked least about these Sony WHCH710N noise-cancelling over-the-ear headphones was:
- The unboxing experience. These headphones were boxed in a brown cardboard box and wrapped in cheap plastic. They included cheap charging and audio cables, nothing else. I was quite underwhelmed at what Sony offers customers who 'only' spend $200.00 with them. I felt almost as if the company wanted me to thank them for letting me buy their tech for such a low price.
- No app support. A key way Sony intentionally detracts from this headset is by not supporting it within its app. This means there are no granular controls to access for ANC, acoustic settings, and the like.
- No carrying case. Amazon sells hundreds of headphones for less than 200 bucks with many of them having active noise-cancelling onboard and some have cases. No excuse for a 200 dollar headset to ship without one.

Overall, while I was pleased with the sound quality, noise-cancelling, and battery life of these Sony WHCH710N, I was somewhat disappointed by the pauper treatment you get in the unboxing experience. Combine that with glaring omissions to app support and a carrying case and I am left conflicted about these cans. If you want a jack-of-all-trades headset that is just good enough in every area to warrant regular usage, the Sony WHCH710N should make your list. However, I think you'll find offerings within this price range that exceed expectations in areas that might be most important to you and don't offer the compromises Sony seemingly built into this model to keep it from cannibalizing sales of their flagship cans. 3.5 out of 5.0 stars.

title: Not worth it, poor sound quality
text:
If I had nobody else to help me review these, I'd give them one star, but after giving them to a few friends and having them say "its not that bad," I've settled on 3 stars.

The key points: Subpar sound, cheap material feel, okay build quality, comfortable enough, acceptable noise cancelling

I've tried a lot of headphones, from $5-$500, and these sound a whole lot closer to the $20 headphones I've tried than anything else. The mids are extremely muffled, almost as if the drivers are blocked by something, or if wires somewhere are crossed. The highs are rolled off and the bass gets a bit boomy, which themselves aren't dealbreakers at all, but the mids definitely are for me. The friends that've also tried this said that they could see someone liking it, but that they didn't exactly prefer it. To me, however, they are almost painful. If I paid full price for this ($130-$200!?), I would return it, potentially the same day. I've tried Mpow H10s at $40 that sound much better and have noise cancelling just about as good.

Onto the build, its made of very rough/loud plastic, and plasticy/polyestery headband and earpads. It feels like its put together solid and will last a while, but it doesn't feel like $200. It's not the most comfortable pair in the world, but its not uncomfortable. If these were a bit cheaper and weren't severely lacking in the sound department, I wouldn't take a star away or anything for it.

The noise cancelling works, but it's not amazing. I'm not sure if its up to par for a $200 pair of headphones, but if you're listening to music with it on, most outside sounds will be muffled enough to no longer be distracting.

In the end, I would recommend against them. From what I've tried/seen, there isn't a large jump in quality from a good $50 noise cancelling headphone until you get to around $250, so these aren't really worth it. The price of these looks like its been jumping around from $130-$200, but everything I've said still stands, I don't think its worth $130. If you can't afford the jump up to a WH-1000XM3 or anything, get a Mpow H10 and save a good chunk of money.

Comes with a 6” USB-C cable. Also comes with a cable (3.5mm) to plug the headset in as an alternative to Bluetooth. The cable is a generous 4-feet long, but note it only works for audio, not phone calls. NC is good at blocking white noise. Great battery life.

The negative: Phone calls over Bluetooth are quiet, and call-voice quality is poor. I wish the headset boosted volume rather than just synchronized with the device volume. Does not come with a wall charger. Uses HD audio: AAC, but the sound quality is more middling than I’d have wished for at this price range. It’s good, but not great. Hopefully Sony eventually adds 710N to the app so I can adjust the EQ to get better bass and treble. NC isn’t good at blocking voices. This headset isn’t the best option if you wear eyeglasses and not good for outdoor or sports activities. Voice guidance is accented, English only, and cannot be disabled.

### Full Review ###

-- Sound Quality --

I test all my headsets by listening to Some Chords by Deadmau5. It provides a good sampling of the full spectrum—from the highs to the midrange to the bass. The overall quality is good assuming you have a good seal around your ears (see section below about wearing glasses). The bass sounds rich and midrange is clear. The treble isn’t the best, though. You may have heard the term “crisp” when referring to high notes. These lack that. The high notes are more muffled and muddied. But, they are not the worst, either. I’ve had other headsets with worse treble. To compare, I tossed in my pair of Jabra Elite 75t and swapped back to the Sony headset. The Jabra sounded way better IMO. Clearer high notes and richer bass. The sound quality on the Sony is good, but for the price, I personally feel it should be better.

Other reviews mention that you can improve bass and treble in the Sony Headphones Connect app, but as of this review (July 2020), the app would not register the 710N version. So I searched Sony’s “List of compatible devices” and WH-CH710N isn’t listed. The closest I could find was for the WH-CH700N, but that doesn’t work on these. So for now, I have to review the default sound settings that I’m stuck with.

If you listen to voice, such as audiobooks and podcasts, that is fine. Voices weren’t too boomy or too flat. Slightly muffled perhaps, but only slightly.

-- Volume --

Pressing the volume up and down on the headset synchronizes the volume with your connected device rather than adding its own boost. That means you are at the mercy of your device for the loudness factor. On my OnePlus 7 Pro smartphone, the music volume got plenty loud enough. However, there are times when voices (e.g. podcasts) may be too quiet. Such as when mowing your lawn or vacuuming (even with NC on). Also, it’s pretty low when on a phone call (more on that below).

-- Calling --

This was the most disappointing feature. Even with volume maxed, the person on the other end is quiet. In general, I find that volume for calls is best when the headset boosts beyond the phone’s max, but this one doesn’t. As mentioned above, it’s locked to the phone volume. On top of that, the voice quality is low. It sounded muffled/muddy. And that’s calling mobile to landline on a 4G-LTE network. Mobile to mobile or to VOIP would likely fare worse. If you make a lot of phone calls and rely on your headset, you may want to look elsewhere. That said, the person on the other end did say they could hear me clearly, so at least the mic seems good.

-- Wearing --

This headset is super lightweight. I weighed it in at 220.2 grams. Whereas a similar pair of headphones I have is 335.5 grams. Feels good even when worn over long periods of time. Padding on the band adds to the comfort. The earcups rotate and headband has a good range of adjustability—could even fit it over a baseball cap.

The sides grip my head well enough so that the headset stays on when rotating my head downward, or violently shaking from left to right. But it doesn’t grip so tightly that it causes discomfort.

That said, when putting them in a resting position around my neck (not on my ears), the headset did feel a little tight. Not painfully so or even uncomfortably, just annoyingly. It was best when the earcups were vertical rather than horizontal. I'm getting more used to the feeling over time.

-- Wearing with eyeglasses --

I tried the headset with both my computer glasses and sunglasses. While it wasn’t uncomfortable per se, the temples on the glasses push against the earcups and create a gap in the material. Thus breaking the seal and allowing more outside noises in, and fewer sounds to stay put. For example, sound leakage causes a big drop in the quality and richness of the bass. Was flatter and weaker. The gripping of the band with eyeglasses isn’t as effective, either. While the headset doesn’t fall off with glasses on and lowering my head, they do slip a bit depending on how quickly I do it.

I find this headset isn’t the best if you need to wear glasses with them, but not the worst, either (for instance, the temples don’t dig uncomfortably into your head or ears as some headsets do).

-- NC / AMB --

I tested the noise cancellation (NC) and Ambient Sound mode (AMB). With all modes turned off, and no music playing, I sat on my couch in the living room while my wife and daughter played a card game in the dining room. I could easily hear them. Turning NC on, the sound of my refrigerator faded, but I could still hear their voices. With NC off and AMB on, their voices sounded about the same, but the fridge was louder. Also, there was a whooshing / white noise coming from the headphones when AMB was on. Sort of like the sound you’d hear back in the day when playing cassette tapes. This can distract from the quality of music when on a lower volume (and can be annoying when listening to voice).

With music playing in the headset and NC turned on, I couldn’t hear their voices anymore. That said, I really couldn’t hear them with AMB on (or off). Since these are Over-Ear Headphones, music playing pretty much stays inside and masks outside noises depending on how loud your volume is.

-- Using Outdoors / Exercising --

This headset wasn’t made to be used outdoors or for sports. While AMB (Ambient Sound mode) is supposed to help you hear your surroundings better (such as nearby traffic), it’s not super useful when music is actively playing. Even the manual states, “Do not use the unit while walking, driving or cycling. Doing so may cause traffic accidents.” Also, I found that the sound of wind blowing gets amplified when using both NC and AMB. It’s particularly loud and annoying with AMB on. This is likely due to wind hitting the sensor since it’s less noticeable when turned off.

Another factor that hurts it’s outdoor and active usability is the lack of waterproofing. This headset has zero waterproofing, and the manual warns that rain and sweat could damage it. Even says damp hands are bad.

-- Voice Guidance --

Voice guidance is a feature (a voice) that tells you things like battery level, connection state, and sound mode. I’ve owned many different headsets and have experienced both male and female voices with varying degrees of quality. On this headset, the voice is feminine and has a slight foreign accent. While I can clearly understand what the voice is saying, the Chinese accent does knock the quality down slightly. If only because cheaper off-brand headsets I’ve owned had similar accents whereas higher-end ones like Jabra sound more native. It’s not about being picky, since I’m honestly fine with the voice, but for the price of this headset I’d have expected something higher quality . . . less knock-off sounding.

Even though the manual has instructions in Espanol and Francais, the voice guidance is only available in English. I also didn’t see a way to disable the voice guidance for those who find it irritating. While both these things don’t matter to me, it may be of concern for some.

title: Great if your willing to sacrifice a bit of quality
text: At this price the noise cancelation and sound quality this provides is amazing. I have tried plenty of headphones near double the price that are equal or even worse than these. The fit is very tight and comfortable so I can wear them for the entire day without any pain and while still having plenty of battery. The mic is not amazing but it works well enough to where its not a problem. I like the ambient sound mode because a lot of times when I am trying to get work done I need sound but listening to a song will distract me, it acts like white noise at the press of a button. One thing that you will be giving up with this model is the quality, The unit is very light which is nice because it makes it fells better when on, but that lost weight is due to using what fells like a very cheap textured plastic, I would fell uncomfortable traveling around with this in my bag especially since there is no included bag or case to hold them in. The buttons have a bit of a tactile click to them so you can fell when you have pressed them which is nice. The ear-cups and cushion on the top are thin, the light weight makes it so that the lack of much cushioning is fine but the shallow ear-cups make is so that my ears are always touching the inside of the headphones. However in the end I think that a headphone should be judged more by the quality of its sound than the quality of what its made out of, so while I am a bit disappointed in the quality of these headphones I am thoroughly impressed by the quality of the sound and would happily recommend these but would also recommend picking up some type of case along with it.

title: A Good Option at around $100
text:
Overall, these are quality headphones that provide ambient and noise cancellation. They are lightweight and comfortable. The music sound is good and the phone sound / mic works well and easily. I think these headphones need to be right at or below $100 based on everything. From the durability to the noise cancellation quality, I don't think they meet the standards of other top quality headphones I have used above the $100 range. These are good at below that price.

I like the comfort, as my head usually stretches headphones to their extent so they are not always comfortable or headphones of good quality can be heavy after a while. These fit well and are lightweight and comfortable, even though they seem cheaply made with plastic and minimal padding on the ears, but they work well as long as they hold up.

I also like the auto adjusting ambient noise or noise cancellation that senses outside noise and adjusts for it. You can switch between these by touching a button on the headphones. I don't think the noise cancellation is as robust as you might want on some noisy airplanes. It does create a subtle white noise to drown out other noises and reduces noise, too.

I think the sound quality for music is acceptable for average users like me. I have no problem with that and am pleased with it. I can see wearing these for music at my desk and using it for travel.

These do not come with any sort of carrying case or bag that indicates that these are not up to the level of top quality headphones that almost always come with a carrying bag or protective case.

title: They're acceptable - but not as good as the better ones.
text:
I have these, the Bose QC35, and another pair of higher end Sony headphones. These are relegated to using at my desk at work - where I don't care if they end up disappearing as much as the others, and the noise cancelling isn't quite as important (I have an office with a door).

The noise cancelling is the weakest part of these headphones. During work from home, I tried to use them to drown out the kids upstairs or in the other room. It didn't really work. It is a very subtle noise cancellation. On a plane, I'm sure they'd be adequate, but in other environments, not so much.

Setup was simple and easy. Charging is easy. I do really like that they use USB-C and not USB-mini or micro - that's a huge benefit and one less cable I need to carry. Hooking them up to my phone and laptop only took a couple minutes.

Overall - very good headphones, especially for the price. I don't listen to much music - only podcasts or audiobooks, and they're more than adequate for that.

title: Comfy, but Lackluster Sound
text:
I purchased these as a replacement for a pair of Sony MDR-XB9501n that cracked after a few years of pretty much living in them 24/7. Despite previously owning headphones whose primary feature was EXTRA BASS, I'm not a huge fan of bass - so naturally I was looking for something with less of it. Sadly, these are still too skewed toward lower frequencies for my liking. Not only that, but the mid-range is dull at best, and while the higher frequencies have their moments, I was immediately disappointed by how lackluster my overall listening experience was right off the bat. I will say that the quality improved significantly when using the provided cable, which is to be expected - but as that's not going to be my primary mode of listening, it's not enough to convince me to stick with these.

Before I even put them on, I was surprised by how cheap the construction seems to be compared to my previous Sony headphones. That being said, these are much lighter and significantly more comfortable. I could easily see myself wearing them for hours at a time without issue. The button controls are pretty standard, and everything is more or less in the same place as it had been on my other pair. To be honest, I'm weird and usually forget that I even have the option of using the controls, so they're more of a bonus than a priority for me. My only problem is the noise cancelling option. I prefer to do much of my listening with noise cancelling switched off, so on these, every time I turn the headset on and off, I have to cycle through two options just to listen without it. A minor gripe, but it makes the apparent lack of app support (or maybe I'm just unlucky?) that much more frustrating. After doing a little searching, I'm still unclear whether this particular model is supported by Sony's Headphones Connect app, as my MDR-9501n model was. If it is, then I had no luck getting my headphones to do what the app's name implies they should: connect. They connected to both my PC and my phone with a few minor issues; I just couldn't get them to show up in the app for some reason.

Speaking of noise cancelling, this feature seems markedly less effective than what my previous 'phones had to offer, and there's an obvious hiss that occurs when it's active. I definitely wouldn't be relying on these to perform well in an environment where noise is an issue. I haven't played around with the ambient sound option, so I can't really speak to its effectiveness either way.

They're certainly not bad headphones - although, in my opinion, you can get better sound for the price. Ultimately, between the merely mediocre noise cancelling and a sound profile which just isn't for me, I think I'll continue searching for a pair that better suits my needs.

title: This is a great pair of headphones for everyday use
text:
This is not the flagship Sony noise cancelling headphones for sure. When I first open the box and took the WH710N out, I thought it felt cheap, The plastic body is well made, but still felt cheap. But after using the headphones for three days straight, I really appreciate the light weight construction of the headphone. The clamping force is not high. I find that I reached for it more than I normally would (since I own the higher end 1000XM3 and the Bose 700 as well).

The sound signature of the 710N is reasonably flat — the base is not boosted like many of the other popular sony headphones. That is just fine with me. The driver is only 30mm in size but the sound is good. The noise cancelling is fair. This would not be my first choice of headphones for flying. But to cut out noise at a cafe? It does a fair job. I only tested it with a simulated sound source during these stay-at-home times.’

Bluetooth range is good. I walked 40 ft away from the source with walls and doors in between before the connection drops. However — the 710N does NOT support multi-point connections. I have to manually switch off the Bluetooth on my iPad to (re) connect the 710N to my laptop. I do not know why Sony do this in 2020.

I think Sony is pricing this headphones wrong. Either keep the price and throw in some goodies like a good carrying case, or price it lower and make this a per of great affordable headset. At the list price I think it is over priced, but at a discounted price, this is a great deal. Think of this as the affordable version of their flagship 1000XM3 if you can find this on a discount.

title: Great value entry in quality noise cancelling headphones
text:
These are some great headphones. Are they perfect audiophile quality "cans"? No, but they get so much right that I think they earn a 5 star rating for they offer. So what's that?

* Sound quality? Very nice sound signature that biases mids over highs and lows. This give music a "full" feeling without that very popular bass forward sound that's all the rage right now. Highs are good but again, these are hyper articulate cans, they provide a nice a full sound that is easy to approach with being tailored to bassheads. I can see some calling this signature "bloated" but in my opinion, the treble is just there enough to keep from earning that description. As I said, I think this is a very approachable sounding headphone.
* Affordable noise cancelling. It seems to get into quality noise cancelling headphones you're looking at high end 'phones that are easily over $200 - Sony's big brother to these come to mind. But these, with street prices that can be much lower than $200 offer some really good noise cancellation.
* 35 hours on a full charge. Add in quick-charge capacity and this should easily last start to finish on the most grueling day(s) of travel. And if you forget you should be able to get you to your next connection with a quick pit stop at a charging booth in the terminal.
* Comfortable. Earpads are vinyl but they are comfortable (that said these closed back headphones can get hot if you're prone to that)
* Bluetooth 5.0 support
* Wired option. Yes, these are Bluetooth headphones but they include a headphone jack in case you prefer of need that wired connection.
* Volume, play/pause, and NC controls. Easy to reach and use buttons on the headphones for these critical functions.
* Decently stylish. Obviously personal opinion but the navy version while not flashy looks pretty decent in my humble opinion. Uncluttered is how I'd describe them.
* USB C charging port. Cable included but something to note if you've got a bunch of USB micro cables (maybe of a longer length) lying around you were hoping to use with these.
* No carrying case or tote bag. This is my biggest gripe with these actually; would have been really nice to have at least a fabric carrying tote.
* Alexa compatibility. I know I'm behind the times but I have yet to jump on that bandwagon so I can't comment on how well they integrate into Amazon's voice recognition ecosystem.

In summary, I think this is a very nice package (minus the tote bag I'd have liked to see) especially if you can get them below the $200 MSRP. Highly recommended.

Note: 700 vs 710
* 710 is apparently a little lighter, looks to have a bit better build quality (less squeaky), and is upgraded to BT 5.0. Earpads seem to be a bit of a downgrade though I felt they were decent.

title: Build quality is a joke
text:
This review is for the Sony WHCH710N headphones.

I ordered the Philips PH805 headphones first, which were very comfortable, but I returned them because I didn't like the controls.

When I put these on, my first thought was that they must be counterfeit -- but the box had been sealed. The pleather is thin and itchy, similar to what you'd expect to be given out for free on an airplane. The cushioning makes a crinkling noise when you press against it, like cheap foam. I have small ears, but they don't fit inside the ear cups, so the tips of my ears get irritated as they scrape against the drivers. The only way I could tolerate wearing these for more than a few minutes was to fold my ears forward so that the drivers contact a less sensitive part of my skin.

Pros: good ANC, good audio quality, intuitive controls, USB-C port
Cons: uncomfortable, thin cushions, poor build quality, no case included

Sound quality was good, and noise cancelling was good. But so are other headphones in this price range, and those come with a case included! I guess you pay for the Sony brand name.

I could pay $15 to replace the ear cushions and another $15 for a case, but I think I'll order a different pair instead.

title: Hard to recommend
text:
I love these headphones; but there are some issues with them that make it hard for me to recommend them. Upon first receiving them, I immediately noticed how nice the noise cancellation was. Keep in mind, that when you turn ANC on, you can feel your ears under more pressure like you’re in an airplane. It’s mildly discomforting at first.

I would give these 4 stars, but I’ve been having issues with my unit. With ambient sound turned on, only audio comes in through the left ear. Maybe mine’s a defect or maybe it’s intended to work that way, I’m unsure. Also, I find these headphones disconnecting randomly on a rare occasion, plus sometimes the right earcup (and on rare occasions the left earcup) pop and crackle by themselves whether they’re playing music or not. I don’t know if there’s an issue with my unit or if this happens to pretty much every unit, but these issues are preventing me from recommending these to someone who just needs some wireless headphones with noise cancelling and is on a relatively tight budget.

title: The Worst Headphones At This Price
text:
These headphones really underwhelmed me. Were they really $200 at one point? If so that’s ridiculous. They are very light and the noise cancelling is very good for the price point and the design is good and they’re quite comfortable because of the light weight. But...

The sound quality is awful. Music sounds muffled - like the highs are pulled back so things tend to not be articulated well with vocals, cymbals, anything that pops really from an instrumental side. They don’t sound like garbage but the sound quality is more in line with what I expect from a $30-$40 over ear headphone set. The buttons aren’t the best for access and in low light knowing L from R when putting these on is a major chore.

I have a pair of Plantronics Backbeat Pro 2s that were $130 and sound quality is noticeably better across the spectrum and those have similar noise cancelling performance. Those are heavier but honestly they feel sturdier than these Sony 710s which feel like they’ll fall apart with one drop. If the sound quality was better and these had a touch more power I’d be really happy with them. But I’m just not there so I’m returning them and sticking with the BackBeat Pro 2 set.

Sony should dump these and get better amplification and better equalization and offer app support. If they could do that I’d pay $20 more for that and be extremely happy. But this is unacceptable for the price. I don’t know if there’s a worse pair of headphones in this price range to be honest.

title: This are a budget set of wireless bluetooth headphones that give good performance.
text:
I like these headphones and am planning to keep them. They can also work as a phone communication device with the mic built into the headset. They are comfortable, If you're used to getting ear aches with press against the ear small headphones these are much more comfortable as they go around the ear instead of right on top of it.

The biggest issue with these that I noticed right away was the noticeable difference in sound quality between the bluetooth wireless connection and the normal 3.5mm headphone jack cable. The wired connection was head and shoulders fuller, clearer more robust sound in my opinion. I was able to tweek the equalizer on the playback device to improve the sound to some degree, but I can't get over the sound difference between the headphone cable and the bluetooth interface.

The second issue is range. For a blue tooth device about 25-30 feet is about all the range you are likely to get. If you have a large workarea that you roam, these will start cutting out and dropping conversation when you get out to about 20 feet. It's wireless but reliably, I was only able to get about 15 feet away from the bluetooth device and not have to wory about it cutting out.

This technology is still fairly pricey so if you don't need wireless right now. I'd wait.

I would NOT recommend wearing these or any headphones while driving. The noise cancelling / ambient noise cancelling technology makes traffic very faint while you are wearing them. NOT SAFE for driving should be a prominent disclaimer.

title: False advertising and poor audio.
text:
For anyone's information I'm using a sony xz2 Premium. The features range from aptx hd to LDAC and many other upscaling options. It also plays natively 24-bit hi res quality audio. Other than a Slow camera, it's a great device especially for listening to music.

That said I'll move to my review.

Had it for 2 hrs and can easily say the audio stinks. I accidentally picked up an en fire e60 with these (vs the e90 newer ones) but it's clear as day that these are pretty bad. I have an older pair of enflcfire as well that still sound clearer and cleaner. I'm only looking for an upgrade because the new phones average at 8 hours vs my old boys at 4.

The bass, while a small portion louder, isn't good. The audio is noisy and sounds bad. There is no aptx hd as it promotes. I even went to my settings under developer settings forcing apt x HD to no avail.

It's bad enough that the quality stinks, but to say HD and mislead people? Nahh terrible company in my eyes.

title: Great Sound
text:
I've only had these for a day but I have nothing bad to say about these headphones. They connected to my laptop and phone via Bluetooth easily.
Amazing sound. Clear, full range. Deep bass. Natural sounding bass. Not booming bass. Clean, clear mid range, and nice crispy clear highs. I cranked up the volume, and there was plenty of sound. No scratchy mids or highs and the deep clean bass I mentioned earlier. No ear fatigue.
Very comfortable. They seal up around my ears and I hardly feel them. Soft and snug and a comfortable headband.
The controls are on the right side and they did a nice job of keeping them simple. And the outside of the right earcup is setup for volume and tracking. Also, if you hold you hand over the right earcup it stops the music so you can briefly talk to someone or listen to something, and then when you take your hand off it starts where it left off. If you tap the power button it tells you the remaining battery percentage. And ANC and Ambient Sound are simple to turn on and off while wearing them.
As for the Noise Cancelling, it seems to work very well. I haven't been on train or plane with them yet, so I haven't put them to a serious test. I also haven't tested the mic yet.
My biggest concern was sound quality and I am very happy. I have yet to find anything I don't like about them. I'm old school and I'm not used to buying sound equipment without listening first. I am very particular about sound but not wealthy so finding something I like without spending a ridiculous amount is difficult. But the Treblab Z7 pros did it.

While I appreciate the follow up and offer, the headphones have been regifted and are being used in an environment where moisture is not an issue, as is the off ear detection (my other major issue). 4 stars for the after sale support audio quality and other features (except for the off ear detection).

title: They Are Now Sweat Resistant!
text:
[[VIDEOID:4a481846ce6582e770f2f3c90c96ed87]] I bought these headphones specifically for using at the gym, as they are the only ANC BT Over-Ear headphones that I could find with an IPX rating of any sort (even if it's only a 4). The first day, they worked fantastic for the whole 2.5 hours I was at the gym. The noise canceling kills all but the sound of people slamming weight stacks or dropping weights. When I first turned them on, with no music playing, it's as if someone hit "Mute" on the world. The sound quality was great... for the price. Think, better than my $100 earbuds, but not as good as my $250 over-ear cans.
The second day I used them, the right side started crackling and popping after about an hour or so. I thought that it was an issue with sweat and the ANC microphones, because turning the ANC off would stop the noise. I used them a few more times to see if it would persist, and it did. Last night I used them for the first time outside of the gym; dry, if you will. After about an hour it started crackling and popping again. I'm sending this set back to get a replacement from Amazon and if they have any issues after a week or two, I'll return them and get back to my search for some Over-Ear ANC BT headphones that are gym-safe.
A couple of side notes:
- I've used them for about 11hrs, altogether, in the 2 weeks I've had them and they still say "Battery High" when prompted.
- The touch controls are sporadic, at best. Sometimes they will pause with a tap. SOMETIMES, they will volume up or down with a vertical swipe. SOMETIMES, they will skip songs. If you aren't prepared to use your phone for controls, steer clear.

I'll update this review in a couple weeks, as to whether or not the replacements worked properly. I hope so, because I genuinely like these... when they work right.

Update - 5/3/2022:
So the second set worked fine for the 2 hours I worked out yesterday... until I was standing at the entrance of the gym to leave. The right side started crackling and popping again. :(
Today, they started doing it again after about 25 minutes. As, with the first pair, turning off the ANC stops the noises. I remembered to record a quick clip of them popping this time, and that they stop, when the ANC is turned off.
This sucks; I really like these headphones, but for $150 I can get something better without the ANC that I can't even use.

Update - 12/20/2022
I randomly got an email from the Treblab customer support yesterday telling me that they found and fixed the issue that was causing my problems with these headphones. They are sending me another pair to try and I will post up later whether they WORK OUT (😂sorry, I had to) or not. Always a nice rarity to see good customer service. 👍🏻

Update:
I spent 2 hours in the gym Tuesday and 2 hours tonight, sweating like a pig in the Hormel parking lot. They are fixed! The hole that the CS rep mentioned being fixed, by the ANC mics, apparently was the problem after all. The new set I have hasn't had any issues yet. That's with 5-6 hours around the house and 4 hours sweating like crazy. Actually It was also pouring down rain when I went in and out of the Gym Tuesday, with them around my neck. I gave back the 2 stars. Good stuff! 👍🏻

[[VIDEOID:4a481846ce6582e770f2f3c90c96ed87]] I bought these headphones specifically for using at the gym, as they are the only ANC BT Over-Ear headphones that I could find with an IPX rating of any sort (even if it's only a 4). The first day, they worked fantastic for the whole 2.5 hours I was at the gym. The noise canceling kills all but the sound of people slamming weight stacks or dropping weights. When I first turned them on, with no music playing, it's as if someone hit "Mute" on the world. The sound quality was great.. for the price. Think, better than my $100 earbuds, but not as good as my $250 over-ear cans.
The second day I used them, the right side started crackling and popping after about an hour or so. I thought that it was an issue with sweat and the ANC microphones, because turning the ANC off would stop the noise. I used them a few more times to see if it would persist, and it did. Last night I used them for the first time outside of the gym; dry, if you will. After about an hour it started crackling and popping again. I'm sending this set back to get a replacement from Amazon and if they have any issues after a week or two, I'll return them and get back to my search for some Over-Ear ANC BT headphones that are gym-safe.
A couple of side notes:
- I've used them for about 11hrs, altogether, in the 2 weeks I've had them and they still say "Battery High" when prompted.
- The touch controls are sporadic, at best. Sometimes they will pause with a tap. SOMETIMES, they will volume up or down with a vertical swipe. SOMETIMES, they will skip songs. If you aren't prepared to use your phone for controls, steer clear.

I'll update this review in a couple weeks, as to whether or not the replacements worked properly. I hope so, because I genuinely like these.. when they work right.

Update - 5/3/2022:
So the second set worked fine for the 2 hours I worked out yesterday.. until I was standing at the entrance of the gym to leave. The right side started crackling and popping again. :(
Today, they started doing it again after about 25 minutes. As, with the first pair, turning off the ANC stops the noises. I remembered to record a quick clip of them popping this time, and that they stop, when the ANC is turned off.
This sucks; I really like these headphones, but for $150 I can get something better without the ANC that I can't even use.

Update - 12/20/2022
I randomly got an email from the Treblab customer support yesterday telling me that they found and fixed the issue that was causing my problems with these headphones. They are sending me another pair to try and I will post up later whether they WORK OUT (😂sorry, I had to) or not. Always a nice rarity to see good customer service. 👍🏻

Update:
I spent 2 hours in the gym Tuesday and 2 hours tonight, sweating like a pig in the Hormel parking lot. They are fixed! The hole that the CS rep mentioned being fixed, by the ANC mics, apparently was the problem after all. The new set I have hasn't had any issues yet. That's with 5-6 hours around the house and 4 hours sweating like crazy. Actually It was also pouring down rain when I went in and out of the Gym Tuesday, with them around my neck. I gave back the 2 stars. Good stuff! 👍🏻

title: Good but not great
text:
Comparing to my Bose comfortquiet 2 ii that I've had for years. I used these for a month or two, here's my critique.

Price was great for Active (microphones and software) and passive (cup material and fit)
Noise canceling was equal or better.

Phone call quality was lesser than bose.

Not a good integration with phone software, bose app is superior.

The smart feature for transparency mode is neat in theory but if you want to wear one ear on and one off it can't tell and fails to perform.

The smart touch side is only the right side.

THe smart touch side isn't sensitive enough for intuitive gestures for volume.

The smart touch gestures are not intuitive, and often doesn't feel the taps for pause skip and such.

The smart touch side is too sensitive to sleep in as it constantly stops if your shoulder or head presses on it from the pillow too hard.

Sound quality isn't bose quality but for the price you're getting enough. Bass not so much.

Battery life about as good as Bose if not same.

Materials feel good.

Charging is type c so im happy about that.

All in all. You get what you pay for. It's a discount version of Bose in price and quality. Only Beats or equates bose in noise canceling. I'd be happy with just buying a new pair of Bose bonestly. Will check in 6 and 12 months.

Another month and half later from this review. Having just one intelligent side is awful. It's smart senor of pausing media whenever the head band thinks it's not on your head has gone now to beyond annoying. The right side speaker quality seems to have changed. Whatever youtuber got paid to rank these higher than bose was a scammer. Such quality shouldn't be allowed to be sold. A shame its past time for its refund window.

text:
not sure if this has happened to anyone else, but at first the ANC feature worked just fine. after about a couple of weeks, there was one morning where i came home from the gym with the headphones on and ANC feature on when all of a sudden there was a loud static noise.

i thought it had something to do with the connection but it seemed like an internal problem with the headphones and it honestly messed with my eardrum a bit. i let that one pass until it kept happening, and i noticed it was because the ANC feature was ON.

once i turned it off i never heard the fuzzy, static noise again.

overall the headphones are great, i would recommend if you're just looking for simple headphones to listen to music casually or at the gym, etc. my favorite feature is the touch panel of the right ear (swipe left/right to change song, up/down to change the volume, double tap to pause/play). super cool!

title: Perfect for me needs!
text: I was wanting a pair of over the ear wireless headphones for the gym so I did some research about which ones are best and saw everyone recommending the Sony XM4 or XM5. I ended up getting the XM4s since they fold up and they're a bit cheaper. To my surprise, they did not live up to the hype for me but I liked how they looked and enjoyed the touch features on the ear cup. Somehow I stumbled upon these Treblab headphones which look very similar and have the same touch features so I decided to give them a try in hopes they would replace my Sonys and I could return them and save some money. After just a few minutes of using these, that is exactly what I ended up doing! The differences are so subtle that it just wasn't worth the price difference for me. They also fit my head better and they're extremely comfortable! I really just plan on using them for air travel and the gym for the noise canceling since I am perfectly happy using airpods for day to day uses so I am thrilled to save the money and still get the things I liked about the Sony XM4s. These are definitely worth a try if you want them for casual use or you're on a budget. I also like that the noise canceling isn't quite as severe as the XM4s, that was a bit much for me and made me a bit claustrophobic.

text:

(3) I discovered the noise cancelling feature is too “strong” for me. It is FANTASTIC at cancelling noise, but it made my ears hurt after an hour of use. I’m used to my Bose noise cancelling headphones, and they don’t have this issue.

All in all, I think they’re great headphones… for someone else.

They just don’t work for me, and that’s too bad.

text: First the seller. I received a new, unopened pair of AirPods Max! Wow. The sound on these are fantastic for the price, even more so since I paid so much less for a refurbished pair. Co-workers often ask me to be quieter. In transparency mode, these headphones solve that problem given the microphones on the outside of the cups. My ears don't get hot at all. The mesh in the headband somehow redistributes weight. I was able to comfortably wear these for a 6 hour workshop and didn't even have to plug them in. 100% worth it, especially when purchased as a refurbished unit.

title: Paired to some else’s Apple ID. :::UPDATED:::
text:
I pulled the AirPod Max out of their oddly shaped cover and they automatically tried to connect to my phone, but I was immediately greeted with this message “The owner of this item will be able to see its location.
You are connecting to an item that's
paired to someone else's Apple ID.”
The headphones are in excellent shape and I don’t see a single blemish. The noise cancellation and spatial audio work amazingly well, but I’m definitely not going to connect them to my phone with them being traceable and no way of removing it without contacting whoever owned them previously. I feel like this should be one of the very first things they check for when receiving a return product for refurbishment. 1 star for now, will update review when I get a pair that doesn’t belong to someone else.

:::UPDATE:::
I left a message with customer service and was called back the next day. They told me how to factory reset the headphones [hold the Digital Crown and the spatial audio button down simultaneously for 15 seconds until the LED flashes amber then white] and it paired to my Apple ID and was no longer associated with someone else’s. Wow, that was easy. Great product and great customer service experience. Would have been nice to not have to deal with that scary experience, but it all worked out well!

title: Amazing quality, outstanding noise cancellation, basically brand new
text:
These 'renewed' AirPods Max are basically new. As you can see in the pictures, the headphones are shipped in generic packaging with a generic lightning charging cable. There is zero evidence of wear on the headphones. I have zero regrets getting these 'renewed' at a significant discount to the original price. It also comes with the original AirPods Max Case, but it's absolute garbage, so I would opt for a 3rd party case.

The sound quality is fantastic for wireless headphones. Exceptionally clear for music, TV, or podcasts (almost no distortion). Great balance for sound for most of the sound frequency range. If you don't find the profile perfect, you can use an equalizer. These headphones are heavy, but that's due to the exceptional build quality. I have worn these for 6-8 hours without any discomfort--the headband helps with minimizing the impact of the weight. The Apple features are great--transparency mode feels like there's no headphones on, I can hear everything. Noise cancelling is amazing--almost completely blocks out a crying baby, fan, or conversations. Easy to switch between modes with button on the right can. The crown is great for sound controls and volume.

I highly recommend getting these renewed.

title: Really Nice!
text:
I will say, I only just got these a few hours ago. But I've been through countless headsets trying to find something decent to be on the phone all day with. I've tried every kind out there--the one-sided style with a boom mic, traditional over the ear, tiny ear buds, ear buds that wrapped around the ear, even bone conduction. And I hated all of them. They were uncomfortable within an hour and my ear felt like it was going to fall off. These? I've had them on for 5 hours now and not only has the battery not dropped even a little bit, but I could seriously forget they're in my ear!

So far all the buttons have worked flawlessly, and the neck piece is nice and lightweight, doesn't feel like a collar around my neck. It's really easy to forget the whole thing is there. I love the retractable earbuds too--the last pair I had like this just dangled, and because I only ever use one side (so I can hear myself during phone calls, and my son running around) it was so annoying to have the other side just dangling around getting hung up on things.

The sound quality is okay. I don't know that they'd be the best thing ever for heavy music listening, though that's just personal discretion. It's honestly fine for phone calls, which is what I'll use them for 95% of the time anyways. So far, my girlfriend says the mic quality is fine. It does pick up a lot of background noise, but so did all the other options I tried. She said for some reason they process my toddler crying and being loud weirdly, but that it wasn't necessarily bad, just weird. She's been able to hear my voice super clearly, and in 5 hours they haven't tried to disconnect or do anything weird at all. I struggled with that issue with a lot of the other headphones I tried, and when privacy is important you can't have your headphones disconnecting every 2 seconds. Oh, and the volume is pretty damn good. They get louder than any of the previous pairs I've tried, so I can very clearly hear my phone calls with no issue.

Overall, so far I feel like they're a solid pair of headphones. I have no complaints, really. Pairing was simple, quality is solid. They came with a nice case, they fold down well without feeling like they'll snap apart. They're good headphones, and with the insane battery life I feel like I'll use the heck out of them.

I'll update if anything goes south as I use them more, but so far so good!

title: A decent pair of headphones at a reasonable price
text:
My first thought with these headphones was, "you get what you pay for". The price point of these ear buds is very attractive at sub $40, but don't expect the same level of sound quality or functionality that you'll get with more premium models from other well known brands. Recommended for those who want the comfort of wireless, but don't need a high end product.

title: Easy to Use, Good Sound Quality, Decent Battery Life, Great Value
text:
These ear buds are wonderful! First off, they feel very nicely made and don't feel cheap. They come with a nice compact hard case that provides more then enough protection while travelling or in your pocket. This case also charges them as well. The charging uses a USB-Type C connection and they do include a cable in the box.

The sound quality is really good and they have a good bit of bass to them, too. I was really impressed and they allowed for a great experience gaming, listening to music, watching movies and TV shows, and making phone calls. Charging is simple and once charged, I averaged quite a few days of use with them being recharged in the case (keep in mind I didn't use them all day). Once fully charged they are very easy to setup and pair. No worrying about them unpairing each other and then doing some complicated hold this and that button to pair. Put them in the case and pull them back out, it's that simple.

They are very comfortable in the ear and easy to wear for an extended period of time. They come with extra tips as well. They stayed in my ear while running and working out. The touch controls were very easy to learn and worked exactly as they should.

All things considered, I really love these ear buds and to me, they sound just as good, if not somewhat better, than more expensive ear buds out there.
