title: I was hoping for so much more...
text:
I started out comparing these headphones to my favorite Bose set, and that’s just a little unfair as there is just no comparison. I was hoping to write a review saying that I just discovered a set of reasonably priced headphones that were just as good - but no way...Jose. Throw that comparison out immediately!

I do have a set of noise cancelling MPow’s (MPow who?) valued at around $60.00 though. They lack bass, but are very comparable and quite good.

These are fairly comfortable, and they’re easy to fit and nicely padded. I’m surprised though that the controls are located on the left ear. There’s a helpful stick-on guide on the left ear showing all of the controls, and they charged up fast and were instantly paired. If you need to extend the headset to fit your head, there’s very thin metal band that becomes exposed, and doesn’t scream quality to me. Noise cancellation works well, but the range is a bit limited at about 30ft.

As far as sound goes - sound is good, but lacks Bass and sometimes can be a touch on the tinny side.I can’t comment on the battery life as I haven’t worn them long enough. They do come in a very attractive carrying case that keeps all the accessories together, and the included operation manual is informative.

I hate to tell you though, when I sit switching back and forth listening to my favorite tunes, between my $60.00 MPows and these $130.00 Altec Lansing’s (at time of review, as the price fluctuates), the $60.00 set wins!

title: Nice bluetooth but noise cancelling causes noise
text:
These are a nice set of headphones, look-wise. They don't look cheap, fold up well and are fairly comfortable once you get them fitted right. I was getting some ear pain at first, but extended the top a bit and they now fit comfortably.

The bluetooth connected easily and easily allows me to go into the next room and still listen to my iPad that is more centrally located to pick up the wifi. Great for when I'm cleaning and want to listen to podcasts or YouTube. It charged fairly quickly and has lasted about a week of non-continual use. When the charge ran out, I was still able to hear by plugging in the phones into the audio until I had time to recharge.

Now the noise cancelling. It works. Our A/C unit sits outside the family room and is very noisy when running. I put on the NC and it was gone. Only problem was a static sound that popped up periodically. It wasn't continuous but loud enough to be annoying when it did. It may not be an issue for someone else, but it caused me to ding it a star. I haven't yet tried these on an airplane, which is where I normally use noise cancelling. But base on how it worked with the A/C, I expect these will do a great job. Just don't expect it to wipe out outside noise. I could still hear the TV going and my husband talking. Just no A/C loud rumbling noise. Now if only I could sleep in these to kill the sound of my husband's fan.

I did get these free in exchange for my honest opinion. What is funny is a just bought a new pair of noise cancelling headphones because my old ones just died and I like these better so far....

title: Great bass for headphones. Microphone is nice for phone calls. Fairly comfortable.
text:
These Altec Lansing Comfort Q+ headphones came with a nice large, round clamshell case that has a zipper. Inside is a bag that is attached to the case to store the 3.5mm cable, the charging cable, and a splitter. (use the splitter to connect it to a PC that doesn't have Bluetooth) The case is decent and holds the headphones when they are folded up. They do not fold up very tight so the case is a little larger than I would have expected.

The sound quality is pretty good. The bass is actually very good. I always play a bass test song that has very low tones and most of the time headphones cannot even reproduce those sounds. These actually did a pretty good job of reproducing even the lowest of lows. Doing this for a long time will probably hurt your ears though so I only did it on low volume.

The highs and mids sounded pretty good as well. For a minute, I thought they might sound as good as my studio-quality Audio Technica ATH-40 headphones. I did a comparison and the studio cans sound better. (The studio headphones cost more, are wired only and are not very portable though)

So as far as Bluetooth headphones go, they sound pretty darn good. I also used these with Skype for a few meetings. Everyone said I sounded fine. The only thing that is a bit strange about using them for Skype is that they do block out background sounds even when the noise canceling is off. I can't hear my own voice which may take a bit of getting used to.

The passive noise cancellation is great. (the earcups keep outside sound out) The active noise cancellation doesn't seem to improve the noise cancellation done by the ear cups much. In fact, I couldn't really tell the difference between having the active noise cancellation on or off. If there is a difference, it is not much of a difference. I have just been leaving it off.

The headphones do talk to you when you turn them on and off which is nice. The ear cups are soft and nice. The headband feels good and has a soft cushion at the top. They do put some pressure on the ears but not too much.

Left and right are not marked but it is pretty obvious which way they go. (the way they fit ears) They feel funny if you put them on backward.

Most of the materials feel like they are of good quality. If anything is going to break, I would guess it would be the headband.

Overall, I really like them. I keep them paired with my computer for Skype meetings and they can go with me when I travel. The case is a bonus.

When using these on active noise canceling (ANC) they are nice Bluetooth headphones. They have very nice sound quality in both music and audiobooks. I didn’t experience any bleed through from appliances or fans during ANC. I like the ease of use one button to pause and for on and off. So no fiddling with a bunch of buttons. These headphones sit back on the head. The controls are on the left hand side, which is great for leaftys, and a little odd since most of the world’s population is right handed. They have killer battery life! I listened to two audiobooks on one charge. I seriously hate giving these headphones such a low rating as when watching streaming videos on YouTube or NetFlix, there is NO LAG between sound and lip movement.
Why then do they get two stars despite them being made by Altec Lansing, having great sound quality and no video lag?. When not in ANC mode, they have a lot of static to the point of being extremely annoying. I experienced the most on the right ear cup. It wasn’t an appliance in my home causing the static, as I turned EVERYTHING OFF. It happened even outside so it was electronic interference. I expect more from Altec Lansing, as they are a leader in the production of sound equipment.
Please Altec Lansing fix the static condition as having no lag headphones is a WIN!

title: Nice Headphones with Good Sound.
text: I liked these. Easy enough to charge, pair to my phone (or TV) and use. I've used them several times now for listening to my TV, and to music on my phone, and they sound great. No outside noise can be heard, and extremely comfortable to wear. I'm not an expert at what makes headphones better or worse than one another, I'm just looking at if I can set them up easily and use, and how good they sound, that's it. I've had other headphones that after months I'm still trying to pair them to something, these I had paired to my phone on the first try. Different colored lights on the bottom of one of the ear pieces tell you when pairing is complete. The parts that fit over your ears are padded nicely, and extremely comfortable to wear. All you need is located on these including the charging port, on/off pairing button, noise cancelling button, and a 3.5mm jack for plugging into listening devices not equipped with Bluetooth. The only thing that took me a little getting used to was the on/off button being so close to the volume up/down button. They are right next to each other, and although they are shaped differently so your touch can tell them apart, my old fingers still kept turning the headphones on/off by mistake when i tried adjusting the volume with the headphones still on. Young people will most likely have no problem with this, for old(er) people like me, having on/off on one ear and volume on the other side would have worked better, but this is hardly a deal breaker on these because they sound great once adjusted right. I can't say if the treble or bass could be this or that, but I've been to over a 100 rock concerts back in the 70's, and have heard all the great rock bands live that you still hear today in movies and commercials, and know what good music sounds like. Without being nerdy technical, this sound good enough to me. Very happy with how easy they are to use and how good they sound. Well worth the money.

title: VERY POOR Battery Life
text:
Honestly, idk if other customers get the actual Altec Lansing product itself or not. But if so, I have the same exact kind which is the MZX770. And my 1st pair lasted a long time until it got messed up. I got a new pair probably about 1 maybe 1 1/2 years later. The noise cancellation button isn't the issue for me at all. It's the battery issue where it used to Hold up REALLY Well, but now it's starting to Annoy me.

So my question is: When I use the Wired Cord it comes with and I have my noise-cancelling Feature ON, WHY Do I have to CHARGE it when they're plugged into my computer with the wired cord itself? I thought the Point of that particular cord was so you DIDN'T HAVE to Charge it on what seems like a near-consistent basis. I 100% understand it dying and running out of battery when consistetnly using Bluetooth which is something I Rarely ever do...But in terms of it being plugged into my computer with the cord it comes, why do these Headphones Die with it plugged into my computer? This has been ANNOYING the Crap out of me. I'll plug it into my computer & it doesn't matter which end it is on, I Attempt to play a video while the noise-cancelling feature is lit up green and guess what, NO Sound comes out because my Headphones are DEAD for some unknown reason. When headphones are Both Noise-Cancelling and plugged in w/the 3.5mm cord to a cell phone or computer, it should NOT need to be charged. I literally do NOT understand why my headphones die like this. I should be able to plug them in w/o them dying on me while being plugged in. Or is the noise-cancelling button a partial reason as to why they die when plugged in w/the headphone cord itself?

title: Short Cable, Microphone on right side
text:
This is what my work got me so I didn't get a choice. I am not sound quality person, unless it is really bad everything sounds fine. It muffles environmental sounds so either it is from noise cancelling or just having my ears covered up.
What I like:
Headphone automatic mute when the microphone is flipped up.

What I don't like:
1. Cable too short. It is only 4ft long, way too short for me to plug into computers that's even a couple feet from me. And it is too short for me to get the cable out of the way. This shortness is workable if not for #2
2. Microphone is on the RIGHT side. Why? All other headsets I have used have the microphone on the left side, even a different Jabra one. My laptop dock is to my left. So when I wear this I have the cable coming across from my left to the right ear cover, across my keyboard and work area. Since it is so short, I can't even push the cable behind the monitor to keep it out of my way.
3. A bit tight between ears. Headset felt comfortable for a while, then I wish the pressure would lessen. Not so much it cause pain, just mild discomfort.

1 and 2 are pretty much a deal breaker if I bought this myself. If the microphone is on the left, the short cable wouldn't be a problem, but combining both makes it really hard to work with. I can't re-design my entire work station just to accommodate a headset.

After 2 days of use:
I dislike this headset even more as time goes on. The headset feels very heavy on my head and makes my ears very hot. And I noticed the microphone is actually picking up the mouse and keyboard clicks so I hear that through the headset. Really annoying.
The cable is also too stiff. 4 days later it is still kinky from the initial packaging foldings, which makes the short cable worse.
I'd have return this if this is mine. Downgrade from 3 to 2 stars.

A few months later:
There's a setting that stop picking environmental noise in the microphone that requires the Jabra software. So that is resolved.

title: Poor reliability for the price
text:
First, the good: The mic quality and isolation of background noise is great! This is the reason I bought this product. The headset is modern and stylish. The indicator lights are a nice and the UC buttons are a handy feature and work best with Zoom in my experience. I had less success with GoTo and Teams.

My biggest issue: When using Evolve2 40 with Windows and UC soft codecs, audio does not remain reliable throughout the day. When jumping between multiple conferencing platforms and local computer audio (music and computer notifications), audio becomes modulated and distorted requiring disconnection and reconnection of the headset multiple times a day, even during a conference. UC buttons also stop working after a while, especially when hopping between conference platforms. Additionally, there appears to be interference with cellular devices indicating shielding is not sufficient as static and audio artifacts are introduced to the audio signal.

Other issues: The passive noise canceling feature primarily relies on the earpads squeezing your head to create a tight fit to your ears, keeping room noise out. Over time, this becomes uncomfortable. If you want proper isolation, go with in-ears or full muff headphones.

Overall, when it works it works beautifully and sounds great - but I'm displeased with the quality and reliability for the price paid.

It is USB-C, which is WONDERFUL! So much easier to use. The features are fantastic -- it integrates seamlessly with Skype, Zoom, WebEx and all the others. All the controls are on your right ear and very intuitive to use.

I absolutely love it and wish I had bought one much sooner!

title: Better sound quality than the Jabra Evolve 75 Bluetooth
text: Our offices use several Jabra Evolve 75 Bluetooth headphones (both with BT desksets and with mobile phones), so I expected good sound quality, but I was surprised at how much better the Jabra Evolve 2 40 sounded than the 75. The difference is probably the avoidance of BT compression, but even factoring that in, the sound quality is surprisingly better than the more expensive 75s. If you need BT, you need BT. But if you application supports a wired headset (computer telephony, or mobile phone with USB-C), the 40 blows the 75 out of the water. Instantly recognized in Win10 and Android 11. 2 hour calls with no fatigue, and much clearer and more immersive than using a speakerphone in a car.

title: Good Overall
text:
I use these for work, 8 hours a day in a work from home call center. I have a large head and am a big guy. The sound is fantastic for voice communication, I would never use these for gaming, music or multimedia. The audio range is not good enough for those applications, it is great for voice. The microphone works beautifully and others can hear me clearly and crisply.

To say that these are "passive" noise cancelling is laughable. There is really no such thing as passive noise cancelling, it's just how much noise is blocked out by wearing the headphone. Do not take that into consideration when buying headphones, unless they totally cover the ear. You can hear everything going on around you.

The ear pads are pretty comfortable, much more than a foam ear pad on standard headphones. I do need to pull these away from my ears every now and then to restore circulation and reduce soreness. Durability of the pad itself is in question, but I have not had these long enough to figure that out. First impression is the pad might last 6-12 months using 5 days a week for work. To me the pads seem to be a weak spot durability speaking.

Overall a great headphone for work. If these had active noise cancelling and a more comfortable/durable ear pad, they would be perfect. I have no experience with microphone filtering yet.

text:
I bought two of these so I can have one at my home office and one at my other office. The only way I can get either of them to work on my brand-new Windows 10 machine is by: unplugging the headset, uninstalling all the device drivers entirely, restarting my computer, and then plugging the phone back in.

Then, it works great! Great sound, all features working wonderfully, lightweight and comfortable. Then, if my computer goes to sleep or is restarting or shut down and started again, it stops working. Even if I haven't changed to a different headset!

Needless to say, restarting my entire machine every time I have a Zoom meeting is impractical. I would suggest pursuing a device from a more reliable manufacturer.

title: Just what I was looking for...
text:

It is so nice when you have a million windows open to just look over and see the red light that I'm muted. No more checking back in the meeting widow to double check. The light even captures when you mute from the meeting (Zoom/Google Meet).

title: Sound is good, comfort is meh, and has other issues.
text:
Received this as a headset provided to me by my work.
It has decent sound and others can hear me well in conference calls. Being noise-cancelling I do hear the typical white-noise-like sound during silence that I feel like all noise cancelling headsets do, which can be annoying/uncomfortable to some. Additionally the fit is pretty snug on your ears and I feel like that would eventually cause discomfort if continually wearing them for long, but that it likely helps with the noise cancelling part.

Jumping right to what is a huge disappointment for me:
The usb cable is really short. Going from my laptop to my head is stretched nearly full length on my desk, especially when standing. That is lame, but not as lame as the fact that the microphone wand is expected to be worn on the right side of your face (only pulls down on that side) which is coupled by the usb cable is also on that side - this conflicts with having my laptop setup on the left side corner of my desk because to be plugged into the laptop, the cable now has to cross over my keyboard to reach the right side of my head. I'll need to change where all my monitors are clamped to my standing desk to make room on the right side of my desk for the laptop now, just so the headset cables can reach me without overlapping my keyboard. Some people may have this sort of a setup positioning already, but the headset could have been made with the wand being able to be pulled down to either left or right side. Big design flaw.

I also wish that the sound controls weren't positioned at the top of earpiece and I wish they were instead located mid-usb cable. During a conference call I have to rely on touch/memory to mute or adjust sound and that doesn't make things work very smoothly.

Finally, the only included instructions for these are printed on the back of the box, which of course someone plastered a big barcode label on top of. There aren't instructions inside the box, only a many language warning and declarations booklet. I figured out it's saying go to jabra.com/manuals for the manual. You'll need to install the free software from Jabra.com/direct to really get the features on this headset working, the software does have a neat concept it enables for auto-answer by lowering the mic arm and muting when raising the mic arm. Things like skipping track that is says it supports does not work with Amazon Music app in Windows.

I would say this is not worth the price and do not recommend purchasing.

title: They’re okay…but not great.
text:
I’m personally not a huge fan of these headphones. Now I realize they are currently priced at $25 and at that price, you have to curb your expectations a little (which I did), but they are advertising that these are typically $60 headphones - which they are absolutely not worth. There are better headphones out there for even $30 (ie Skullcandy).

First off, these earbuds default to what is presumably Chinese, which I haven’t been able to figure out how to change and don’t care enough to try to research…so I suppose on the plus side, I am improving my Chinese vocabulary every time I turn these on. It doesn’t bother me THAT bad, but it definitely gives a slightly “cheap” feeling to the headphones.

The sound quality isn’t bad, but it isn’t great either. Honestly, the aforementioned Skull Candy headphones for almost the same price have a higher quality sound. I think what bothers me the most about these headphones is their overall design. Yeah the touch feature sounds cool on paper, but any time you adjust the position of these headphones in your ear or bump them, the touch feature is so sensitive it’s inevitably going to pause, skip, or do something else funky. I run with these a lot and the overall fit isn’t great (even with different size ear buds), so my music is constantly getting interrupted every time I adjust their position.

Finally, whenever I take a phone call on these headphones, the person on the other line tells me they can barely hear me and, worse, the phone call randomly gets dropped most of the time.

In conclusion…I would say you get what you pay for, but the problem is there are far superior headphones out there for almost the same price. These aren’t HORRIBLE, but they ain’t great. Cheers.

title: Very good value-priced true-wireless earbuds.
text:
To get this out of the way first, I did receive this as a promotional item, and am exchanging an unbiased review.

I "needed" a new set of earbuds, and figured that this would be a good time to go with a true-wireless set. These came up on my Amazon recommendations, so I figured that I'd give `em a shot. I had previously owned a set of the older T6s, which had held up pretty well and had overall good quality.

These are pretty nice, and paired with my iPhone almost immediately. From there, I put the earbuds through the paces. I listen to a lot of audiobooks, and my music tastes are fairly varied. There's the Tozo app that is suggested. I found the basic sound to be pretty good, but did like the variety provided by the app, which gives 16 different sound modes aligned mostly by music styles. I pinged between them, but ultimately settled on the "Rock" preset, which seemed to me to be the best "all around" preset for my taste.

Audiobooks (currently listening to "Three Body Problem") are crisp and clear.
Music - I'm actually listening to these as I'm writing the review, and I'm listening to Amon Amarth's "Great Heathen Army," and am very pleased with the robustness of the sound. Again, the sound is crisp and clear and of very high quality. I've also listened to other music, such as classical, various classic rock (mainly Queen Led Zeppelin, and Pink Floyd), and Sarah McLachlan - all of which sounded great.

Call quality wasn't the best. It sounded like the call would go from being on both earbuds, then it shifts about a half second to one ear, then to the other, then back to both earbuds. This happened several times in a 20 minute span, and the other person that I was talking with would complain about the quality the call. But that's OK!

Overall, a solid performer. 4.5 of 5 stars!

title: They are a good option for the price
text:
Recently I have been testing out different Bluetooth options for use with my phone. Up until recently I was happy with my cheap, wired headphones, but they tend to get caught on things when exercising which all I need them for.
I gave the Tozo T10S just three stars across the board simply because in every measurement they were average. However, compared to the other's at this price point I have tested this set compared quite well.
Starting with the case they come in it was the easiest to hold and open to get the 'phones out. The other's were too rounded, or small, making them difficult to grip when trying to access the contents. the latch was also easy to use while others required a either a great deal more effort or force to open them.
The design of the 'phones are not much different than the others in that they are relatively easy to grasp and have a familiar shape. The shape is the oval type with a flat control face that sits in the ear comfortably. I was I was able to use these for almost two hours without feeling pain in my average sized ears. If you have large ears they might feel loose, which is a big issue, and if you have smaller ears than it's likely these will be uncomfortably tight, perhaps painful.
The control face for pairing, music controls, etc. is too sensitive. Any time I brushed across them accidently, or while adjusting their fit, they would pause or change the music, or book I was listening to. Since the entire face is a control panel it's difficult to grasp these without touching that control area.
One thing that surprised me was the audio quality. Definitely not high quality, but it was decent. I tested them against my cheap and expensive wired headphones as well as the other inexpensive Bluetooth sets I have. While they don't reach the same level as the wired 'phones they sounded better than the other three wireless sets I've been testing which all seem to have a dull, muffled quality to them.
The thing I didn't like about the Tozo T10S is stability in the ear. After only a day of cycling these almost fell out of my ear three times. The fourth time they did and I lost one of them. It's a shame since I had started to use them around the house to listen to my music and books when doing chores or cooking.
I would have like to have spent more time with these, but since one part is lost I can only give my impression based on a couple of days use. In that short time I did grow to like them and wish the design fit better and didn't fall out of my ear so easily.

Update:
Forgot these were in the pocket of my safety vest I wear when cycling and put them in the wash.
They still work. :| Washed, dried and still work. That's impressive.

title: Another Great TOZO Product - T10S
text: I like this case included a lanyard--that's a nice little bonus. I'm a big fan of TOZO products--I bought my first pair 4 years ago. I own several pairs that I have paid $30 - $60 for and I have never been disappointed with the build quality, sound and features. This model allows for some customization via the app, which I did not use with these yet--but good to know. TOZOs are know for great battery life and high-capacity battery cases that offer additional, fast charges to the earbuds. The packaging is always excellent and these came with the standard array of buds to fit your ear perfect. Our family of four (2 teenagers included) started with all AirPods and between 3 family members we either lost or had stolen 4 units. In hindsight, I would give my kids these--less of a target for theft and frankly, IMHO, these are better than Airpods for the money. They connect very quickly to my iPhone and stay connected; they have a louder sound but to be fair, they are buds and you get a better fit. The call quality is just as good and these have call noise cancellation that improves call quality. Tremendous value from a company that stands behind its products.

title: All Good Except One Thing
text:
[[VIDEOID:19213d6fddf7c389e0fcdc2ab8b608b0]] I had high expectations for this newer TOZO product and was not disappointed. Right out of the box it connects via Bluetooth. Out of all the earphones I have had in the past, these earphones have touch actions that make the MOST sense. Double tapping for the next/previous track and long presses for volume. As expected, the Bluetooth connection does not cut out nor does the music while connected.

The case is a bit larger than other earbud cases but I LOVE the loop for attaching! Many times, I come across a great set of earbuds and they refuse to add a loop. These do not disappoint.

The only gripe I have about this product is the app they advertise that works with earphones. The moment I connected my earbuds to the app, the app crashed and refuses to stay open. That is why I docked a star off for the value of money and sound quality because in this case, I did not COMPLETELY get what I paid for.

As with many new things (especially software) they never really work like their supposed to even after testing the first time, so I'm positive in the future the app will get a rework and start working again. If I'm correct this is TOZO's first attempt at implementing an EQ so I understand.

TLDR: Overall, the sound quality is amazing. Can hear individual instruments clearly. A great amount of bass. Fit comfortably. Touch controls are intuitive. The case is a little big (pictures for reference). App does not work but is not needed (for me anyways)!

title: Can The T10S Take Out The TOZO NC2?
text:
[[VIDEOID:cc75227daed0095b2ab609f43bee89f3]] I am very new to the world of wireless earbuds, and I needed something for a plane trip. After a brief bit of research, I decided on the TOZO NC2 earbuds, which I purchased on August 17. I absolutely fell in love with the NC2 and their snug fit, crisp and clear sound, deep bass, and amazing ANC that completely blocked all the ambient noises in the plane cabin. So, two weeks later I saw the T10S available as a Vine product and immediately jumped on them. But, in my haste, I didn’t catch the fact that the T10S utilizes ENC (Environmental Noise Canceling) technology, not ANC (Active Noise Canceling). A simplistic way of explaining the differences in these two technologies is that ENC removes ambient noises from signals being transmitted by the microphone (outgoing), and ANC removes ambient noises from signals being heard through the speakers (incoming).

Even without ANC, the T10S still does an admirable job of blocking ambient noises due to the tight seal of the comfortable and soft silicone earpieces, and they performed very well in my “leaf blower” test. My “test” is to simply fire up my cordless leaf blower while listening to some music, preferably while my ground AC unit is also running. The music was plenty loud and very clear without the need to max out the volume, and they were a lot closer to the NC2 in keeping all this racket out of my ears than I expected. Unlike the bass-heavy sound of the NC2, the T10S puts more emphasis on the high and mid ranges. For those that want more bass (like me), the sound can be easily tweaked through the 10-channel equalizer in the simple and user-friendly TOZO app. There are 16 presets to chose from, and, of course, any of them can be customized to the listener’s personal preferences. Unfortunately, I found that no amount of tweaking can get the T10S to output anywhere near the levels of highly gratifying deep bass that the NC2 does. A feature that is missing from the T10S that I really like in the NC2 is the pause feature when one of the earbuds is removed. I know that a single tap will pause the T10S, but “pull out to pause” is just so convenient.

The T10S is tough to recommend when they are currently $3 more than the NC2. They have a nice style, great and comfortable fit, solid and high-quality case, and a great equalizer app. But, price, low bass levels, and no ANC make it a no-brainer to get the NC2. If someone just wanted basic, but good quality earbuds, and the T10S was $20 or less, then that’s a pretty good buy. But, as it currently stands, it’s NC2 all the way. Be impressed, or for $3 less, be REALLY impressed.

title: Good value, good sound, good battery life
text: We have several sets of Tozo ear buds in our household. We use them for listening to podcasts and audio books, primarily, and they are great for that purpose. They come with several sets of inserts, so will fit just about anyone. We tend to use just one ear bud at a time, keeping the other in the carrying case that is also the charger - so battery life is not an issue for us. If you use both, you can expect to get 6 or 7 hours out of a full charge. I am rating them high for sound quality and noise cancellation but that is a relative rating. They do not deliver the same quality of audio or noise cancellation as my over-the-ear head phones, but that is to be expected. The range is about 60 - 70 feet, through walls. That's can be an issue when I am out and about in the garden and my phone is on a charger. Also, they don't work well - for me - with hands free phone calls - listeners often complain of distortion on their end and I usually end up switching to speaker phone. All that said, these are the go-to ear buds for our household. We find them very well suited to spoken voice content. If were music lovers, we'd probably spend more to get more.

title: Great quality like the original T10 set, but now can tweak the EQ in the app!
text:
I've used several different pairs of Tozo earbuds over the last few years and have always been very pleased, but I've always wished for the ability to tweak the EQ settings. After seeing this updated 2022 version - the T10S, I can now do that and had to give it a try!

I have an original pair of T10 earbuds and the sound quality has been great and the touch controls have been responsive. The T10S pair is no different, but have been updated to work with Tozo's new app which finally lets me tweak the EQ to my liking, so now I can push lows or highs a little when needed depending on my environment. I've only had these for a couple days now, so can't speak to battery life, but I suspect they'll be just as good as the original T10 pair.

My single minor complaint is the size of the charging case. It is about twice the size as one of my other favorite tozo earbuds - the NC2. That's not enough to take off a star as I suspect battery life of the charging case will be an advantage with the size. So, when I want a pair that will live in my pocket all day when I'm on the go, the NC2 will probably still be my go to set, but the T10S will take over for my normal T10 and will be my go to for wearing around the house now and my old T10 pair will be passed on to my daughter.

They also come with a wide assortment of silicone ear pieces so you can be sure to get a proper fit which is necessary to get the best sound quality and isolation from external sounds. Another nice feature is the cover of the charging case is a semi transparent so you can easily see the charging status as well. Overall, very pleased and highly recommend!

title: Good earbuds for side-sleepers
text: I've been looking for earbuds that would lay flat enough to be comfortable when sleeping on my side. The Jesebang IT100 work so well that I'm going to order another pair. Sound is good. Comfortable and stayed in my ear. I would describe as smooth without too much treble. Happily these stay connected to the bluetooth on my Dish Joey. Others would cut out if I layed down on my side. I tested by walking to another area of they house. 45 feet with no dropped connection. Only two slight negatives: because of their small size and position of the stems facing inward in the case they are a little finicky to take out and turn around to put in each ear. The other is when I tried to connect to my phone after first pairing to the TV in the bedroom with the Dish Joey, the phone would not connect. I had to go back to the bedroom TV, go into the Dish bluetooth device list and disconnect the IT100. Then the phone and these earbuds were good to go. Other earbuds support more than one device. That said, these are excellent for the price. I highly recommend.

title: Surprisingly great sound!
text:
The 13mm drivers in these tiny buds are incredible! I've tested approximately 30 Bluetooth earbuds from high end to low end and these surprisingly provide similar sound quality compared to many of the higher end models like Jabra 75t/ 85t, Liberty Pro 3, Soundpeats H1. Also, the small form factor is amazing and the surprisingly fit well in my large ears. They of course come with a variety of ear tips and it’s crucial you find the right size so you have a snug fit. If you don’t have the proper fit even the highest end earbuds will sound awful. The touch controls also work like a charm.

With the proper ear tips these earbuds do offer good noise isolation. However, I wish they had ANC (Active Noise Cancellation). I’d pay at least $20 more to have ANC/ transparency mode on these. I’ve searched everywhere and can’t seem to find a similar size/ form earbuds with these features. Despite not having ANC I highly recommend them. If you're a bass head like me you'll be in love!

One thing I don’t necessarily care for it the glossy finish on the charge base. It seems like it would be very easy to scratch. This is a very minor thing so take that con with a grain of salt.

title: For the price, not bad
text:
I got these during a good sale when they were $30. They appear to be that price now anyway. For the price, they aren't bad. They are comfortable and I don't feel like they will fall out. It's hard to find them with the ear clip which is what I wanted. The sound quality is fine to me, but I use them mostly to listen to audiobooks while doing hands-on chores so I'm not sure how much music would be affected.

Another user said the case wouldn't charge. I also found that to be an issue at first. I was using my own cord in a rapid charge adapter and they wouldn't charge at all. I plugged the tiny 12 inch cord it came with into my desktop port and the case is finally charging. The case is nice, I like the look of it and how easy it is to see the case's remaining charge. My only complaint that took this from 5 to 4 stars is that occasionally the sound will cut out in one or both. It's only a split second, and it isn't very common, maybe 5 or 6 times in an hour. For my purposes, and for $30, I'm okay with it. I will be less so if it gets worse. They don't have too much "noise cancelling" to them but I was able to hear them over the lawn mower so they get loud enough. There is also no way to turn them off. If they are out of the case, they are on, and only putting them back will turn them off. Its a minor inconvenience, more of just something to be aware of for preserving battery life.

title: Good sound quality and volume control, super cute too!
text:
My kids LOVE these cute rainbow unicorn headphones! I have one pair that I use in the classroom for our only computer and they always fight to get to the computer first to use them. They are adjustable and fit my 4 year old as well as my 7 year old just fine. I have also used them and they are snug on my adult head but usable.
The child volume control is good - you adjust the volume like normal but they just don’t turn up after a certain threshold. They do get loud enough to a point where the kid can comfortably listen without it being so low that background noise distracts them.

Sound quality is pretty decent, nothing less than any standard headphones would be. Also would like to point out that there is a microphone on the wire that works great.

Overall I am extremely happy with this product. Oh and it also comes in the cuuuuutest unicorn gift box in case you’re planning to give them away as a gift. These are perfect!! Highly recommend.

You can turn them off by touching them simultaneously for five seconds until you hear them power off. I’m not sure why this function would be used because even though they have been powered off as soon as you remove one of them from the case they automatically start your music anyway. One last thing is that I am unable to figure out how to adjust the volume from the earbuds rather than the phone. There is nothing that mentions this in the instructions so I am going to assume this is not an option.

title: Surprisingly decent
text:
This is my first set of wireless ear buds. I was nervous to try inexpensive ones and couldn’t spend the money on fancy name brand ones. But so far these work very well! I can’t really attest to the sound quality, they sound the same as every pair of wired ear buds I’ve owned over the years and I’m not really picky as long as the sound is clear.

They seem to hold a charge for quite a while. I only use them to listen to music or videos for 1-2 hours a day and I’ve only had to charge them a couple of times over the last month. And i only charged them because I thought it was time, not that they ran out of power. There are 3 little lights on the front of the case that I think indicate the level of charge, though I haven’t noticed them changing at all yet. When you pair these with your device there is no indicator to tell you their charge level. I use apple products, so I’m not sure if that has anything to do with that.

While they have been simple to pair with my devices, it seems that they will only pair to one device at a time, whether that device is being used or not. For instance, if I pair them to my computer, then log off the computer, they will not pair to my phone. I have to remember to unpair them before I log off and leave the office. I’m not sure if this is typical? It’s kind of annoying that they won’t connect to other devices even if they aren’t currently connected to the paired device. And there is no way to disconnect them from the device when you don’t have the device on hand. Like I said, I don’t know if this is just how these things work since this is my first time using wireless ear buds. I suppose I will get used to it.

Their range seems okay, I was able to walk to the bathroom which is maybe 40-50ft from my computer where they began to cut in and out. So, not too bad but I certainly couldn’t walk around the house listening to a podcast or something.

So overall, not bad for inexpensive wireless ear buds!

title: Good light weight neckband-style Bluetooth ear buds - comfortable and rest where they should
text:
I've been needing a new pair of bluetooth earbuds for a while, but I break all earphones eventually so I stick to buying inexpensive ones - I've had decent luck with cheap ones in the past so I wanted to give these a try.

Pairing was simple, once my Android phone got around to scanning the nearby devices, which took a while. The N18s showed up immediately on my Samsung tablet.

These TONEMAC N18 Bluetooth Neckband Earbuds were listed at $29 with a 20% off coupon at the time of the review, which is a fair price for what they are. The last pair of bluetooth earbuds I had were a slightly different style, lighter and more flexible and I could just stick in my pocket. This pair has a stiffer neck band that stays in place better, but they will be a bit harder to pocket. They'll fit in an inside coat pocket, but may be a bit more awkward in my windbreaker hand warmer pockets.

Charging is USB-C, but the instruction manual is old and stills says micro-USB. The magnets on the earbuds to hold them together while you are not using them are pretty strong, which means it will be hard to accidentally loose these, unlike Apple Airpods and other similar earbuds that have no wires connecting them, or even regular wired earbuds which I some times drape around my neck when I'm not wearing them, and have wound up loosing them because they aren't made for that the way these are.

Sound is decent for my needs. Outgoing audio from the microphone is a little bit distorted and output is low, though not any lower than the NoxGear I compared the audio to using the Android audio Recorder app.

Overall, I'm happy with the earbuds. But it will take some time to get feedback from people about the outgoing call quality.

The neckband portion of these is smooth and flexible, but the portion where the microphone and buttons are housed has this texture.
For me, it is unbearable to touch.

I paid for this with my own money and I haven’t been encouraged by anyone to give this review in any way.

title: Review Depends on Intended Use
text:
I typically wear just one earbud during the day while I listen to podcasts, and at night while I fall asleep. These earbuds are not a good choice for these purposes for two reasons.
1) There is no way to stabilize the other earbud or affix it to my clothes, so it dangles from my neck, and if I bend over, it attaches to anything metal it comes into contact with. 2) The volume change with each click on the device (including the slider on your device) is in huge increments, so there is no low volume to fall asleep to. When you reach the lowest volume, it is way too loud, even if you pull the earbud out from your ear. And if you click one notch lower, it is silent.
So I can use these to work out, with both in my ears at the same time, but I will revert to my prior brand when it comes to my day-to-day activities and falling asleep.

title: These are bad in every way
text:
There isn't much to like about these headphones. (a few good things at the bottom)

The sound quality, even compared to other cheap examples, is tinny. I use them for audiobooks, so it's bearable, but they butcher music.

The microphone is awful. To others I sound like I am underwater. Again, this is even worse than other cheap headphones. I bought these in hopes of improving this very thing. Basically I cannot conduct a phone call with these headphones.

The buds themselves are uncomfortable. I've lived with earbuds in my ears for a decade. These are the least comfortable I've owned.

These do not stay in place around the neck well. They tend to rotate.

I hate the "dangle in front" earbud thing. I cannot always have them in my ears and so i have to take them out and let them dangle. I hope manufacturers go back to making over the neck sets that include a magnet on each side for holding the earbuds. (I looked and looked before giving up and buying these. I'm too tough on electronics to use the skinny little wires in the retractable kind) These get tangled up in my clothes, or stuck inside my coat, etc. And when you dig them out, the little rubber bud cover comes off 20 percent of the time, stuck inside my coat or collar.

The battery life is fine. The range is just ok. The buttons work well. I like that they charge using USBC. I haven't tested their water resistance.

Believe it or not, this review is for reimbursement, but I'm not gonna lie. Look elsewhere.

title: Good for the price
text:
So I got these headphones to have a spare pair for the gym or sometimes for use at work.
At only $25, I didn't expect much at all but was surprised at what these brought to the table.
Now, you can't go and compare a cheap pair of headphones to anything out of its ballpark price range so don't expect to be blown away.

The headphones included a USB-C charging cable and a 3.5mm TRS aux cable. The headband on these were fairly comfortable. I have what I would believe to be an average sized head for a male adult and they felt snug. Pressure on the sides was minimal but enough to keep them in place during some light jogging and sweating. The ear padding felt great but also feels cheap.

Sound quality is decent but definitely lacks bass and a good sound stage. Mids are ok, Highs are good.
Battery life seems a bit short though. When I got the headphones I gave them a full charge before first use. During my workouts, I usually do 2 hour sessions. By the fourth day I had to recharge the headphones so that was only 8 hours before they got low. I was listening to Rock style music probably at mid volume during each use.
Another full charge and battery life improved greatly but still fell short of the claimed 55 hours.
Maybe the 8 hour issue was a 1 time fluke? I don't know. But with continued use I only average about 30 to 35 hours of playtime before needing a charge.

Bluetooth connectivity was spotty at first when trying to pair with my Galaxy S9. I would have a random disconnect and it would immediately reconnect. It only happens every now and then.

During a phone call, the person on the other end said they can hear my voice clearly but that it sounded like I was at a distance. Kind of like when you have aftermarket bluetooth in a car.

Overall for a budget set of wireless headphones, they are great for what you're paying.

title: Great reference headphones with a great form factor, comfort could be made better.
text:
The sound is great for people who know the audio profile theyve selected. Its a non-bass heavy reference sorted sound geared towards comfort and soft layered clarity.

The audio has a great layering, but if youre a normal human that just wants a quick immediate solution to your audio needs then this probably isnt the product for you.

The construction leaves a little to be desired and the cups could use slightly more foam and a less thick liner.

Those caveats having been said you wont get the soft layering produced from these drivers elsewhere.
I recommend having good enough headphones that youre more happy with before purchasing these as theyre non punchy but great cloudy subtle layering of sound in which youll find new clarity in your music.

The pads could also be built better. But the rest of the plastic parts, the cups have a fantastic soft smooth finish. Also steelor aluminum around the headband. Maybe it could be cheaper? As an audio lover this still passes as a 5/5 product just not for those who want a thump or thumping in the sound.

title: Looks good but not for serious runners.
text:
I really, really, really wanted to like these headphones I really did. They look really sleek and for the price sound really good! But unfortunately if you're thinking of getting these for long distance runs beware. They would always work fine for a short 3 mile run but any longer and one headphone would always stop working for a few seconds or minutes and then would start working again. And then on my latest long run I got to mile 9 and they just disconnected all together and would not repair. Such a bummer and buzz kill for my run. I brought them back home and tried troubleshooting them as instructed in the product manual. After a hard reset they reconnected but then they just started having a mine of their own literally and started pressing their own commands (pause, play, skip, voice assistant) without me even touching them. I attempted 3 more hard resets and still no luck as it continued to press commands on it's own. Could I have gotten a lemon? Possibly. But with so many others out on the marketplace I would look elsewhere. If you're looking for something for podcasts or audio books these could work but if you're thinking of getting these for running or working out I would pass.

**Update**
The customer service I received exceeded my expectations! The seller reached out to me and agreed that I may have purchased a defective product and sent me a replacement ASAP! So far so good. No disconnections or issues when running long distances with the replacement.

title: Great Value with comfortable ear piece
text:
I've been looking for noise canceling earbud with the power beats pro shape because regular earbuds fall out of my ears when I'm working.

The original connection took a little bit to figure out... One would work then the other and there was three devices as an option to be paired... But with a few restarts they work fine.

There doesn't seem to be an option to turn off the noise canceling anywhere so it's always on... which is not typical from other noise canceling headphones I've had in the past, and I'm not sure the active noise canceling is the greatest, but I'm just trying to dim down printing presses at work so these to the trick.

Has an app and it's ok... I don't really need an app for headphones but the app, but it has programable touch buttons for single tap, 1 second hold, 3 second hold, double tap. A useful feature is to see how much battery is left in each earbud, and you don't get that in every budget earbud.

I do like the physical buttons for volume which is nice feature to have.

Recommended good value for the price point.

title: I wanted to like these earbuds
text:
Initially, I thought these were "keepers" but ultimately decided to return them because they are ultra-sensitive to an unintentional touch, which in effect disconnects them from my "smart speaker". That may or may not be a problem when paired with a cell phone, but it's extremely frustrating when paired to a "smart speaker".

Because I have a mild hearing loss, I pair these with my “smart speaker” to listen to podcasts, as I’m heading for bed.

Sound LEVEL is good and sound QUALITY can be tweaked with the free app equalizer.

I don’t detect any noise-cancelling whatsoever, but that’s not a problem for me under the circumstances.

They have an excellent range (30-35 feet/10m from the BT source), pair easily, and use a USB-C charging cable.

I’m eagerly awaiting FDA approval of Over-The-Counter BT hearing aids; but until then, I'm trying to find a viable alternative.

title: Amazing for the price.
text:
First off, I always find it promising when I see a product is packaged well; it says something about the manufacturer to me, but a good cover doesn't always mean a good book; I know that. After I opened the box, and then the hard shell charging-case the earbuds were in, I was taken aback how beautiful these things are; nothing like the half dozen other ones like this that I've had in the past. They obviously care about their product. Pairing was a snap. Paired my computer, phone and TV seamlessly. No issues there.

Figured out how to turn the volume up and down w/o the directions, but didn't realize at first that I had the choice of adjusting the sound from either the left or right earbud; a great feature for me. I did have to look at the directions to figure out where to press, to pause/play, answer/end calls, and to reach my voice assistant. It was easier on this site to see that illustration then in their booklet.

Was out blowing snow this morning with them on. My phone was in the house about 30' away at the furthest, but I stayed connected for the entire forty five minutes, and the sound was loud enough that I could clearly hear my music over the snowblower. Made blowing snow so much more pleasant..lol.

The sound is what I'd call upper average...its maybe a hair better than the others like this I've owned, but for the price I wasn't expecting Bose sound. I will say this, if you spend the time and try the different ear tips sizes/shapes, you'll find the sound quality changes quite a bit, so spend the time and find the one that fits your ears, and sound preferences the best..
The sound on calls is perfect on my end, and on who ever I was talking to's end, b/c no one, out of the few dozens calls I've used it for, mentioned to me that I sounded like I was on a speaker phone, or similar.

These also come with a real nice supply of the rubber replacement earbud-thingie ends. One set is already installed, and four other replacement pairs that are of different shapes and sizes are in a little baggie. You can find one pair that work to cancel the noise out better than other tips, if thats what you're after.

I really like these, and just hope I dont lose them. I need to make a habit of putting them back in their case after each use. I guess nice things sometimes take a little more paying attention to....and these are really nice.
..now that I'm thinking about it...they'd make good presents...hmmmm.

title: Good for staying in ears.
text:
These are very good at staying in my ear when I'm doing all sorts of activities. I also found I can wander further from my phone than most every other BT device I've used. The various control features work nicely. Sound is adequate for audiobooks and phone calls.

On the down side, play time is limited to 3 to 4 hrs. Noise canceling is pretty ineffective. Perhaps changing bud sizes can help there? I've got a pair of over the year noise canceling over the ear headphones that make it so I can easily run my riding mower without making volume adjustments or turning volume up high. Same for over the ear headphones working well to cut down noise on long airplane flights.

I was hoping these would last long enough and be effective at noise canceling for air travel. They fail on both of these issues. They don't even last long enough for a modest half day of working in the yard, or a simple round trip hike or bike trip. I generally expect earphones to last at least 12 hours, or more between charges. Several I've used last for 24 or more hours between charges.

title: Optimal Compact Charging Unit For Multiple Devices
text:
The vast majority of people today are dependent upon rechargeable devices such as cell phones, tablets, and e-readers. Naturally, along with this comes the mayhem with a multitude of wall plug-in chargers and cables. This can be very unsightly in any kitchen or office, and people can also end up using a charger that was not designed for a specific device. Thus, it follows that a compact multi port charger can help alleviate this problem.
This new Anker five port charger that I received a couple of days ago replaces my four port charger that I generously gave to my grandson. Both units have what Anker calls "PowerIQ Technology" which means that the charger actually identifies the device that is plugged into it and then optimally charges it at full speed safely. It can simultaneously charge at all five ports. While I have no way of objectively measuring charging speed, it is appears that my Samsung Galaxy S5 cell phone charges at the same rate as its supplied charger.
The charger kit includes five cables of varying lengths though they all have the same micro-USB connector. All Anker products that I am familiar with come with a generous 18 month warranty and excellent technical support.

text:
In a few hundred years when historians look back at our time and museums proudly display the pinnacle of USB chargers, they will talk about this charger, or one similar to it. A year or two ago I bought the previous generation white charger which had ports specific to each device. In a few days I am to leave town on business and asked my wife if she had a charger for her phone while I was away. I bought the newest one with PowerIQ and a complete set of cables. It nicely complements the Anker 10,000 mAh external battery I also purchased to keep all of my devices charged during a 13 hour pair of flights each way.

* Quiet and out of the way
* Comes with appropriate cables

title: A true powerhouse for your house!
text:
First, I would like to state that I was supplied a sample from Anker for testing and evaluation, and I promised them detailed, fair, and honest feedback on the product listed. This is my eighth review for Anker and these are my honest impressions of this product, for which I used to type this entire review.

Packaging
I would like to start with the first impression, the packaging. Anker is constantly striving to become very green and they are maintaining this to the fullest as I have outlined in prior reviews. The packaging is still a recycled brown box with a white sleeve that has a picture of the charger on the top along with the Anker logo and a prominent PowerIQ Specification badge. The front also includes badging that there are also 5 cables included in the package. The bottom of the sleeve has a QR code to direct you to ianker.com and their offerings. One side of the sleeve has contact information for Anker and the other side has a label with the serial number of the device. The box itself is rather simple, after sliding off the sleeve you are met with a plain recycled box and just the Anker logo on the top. My box did not have a security seal and it opens from the side. Once opened, you are greeted with the PowerIQ pull-out leaflet and under it is the 40W 8.0A Desktop charger in its plastic bag. Next to that is a pull-out section with the supplied power cord. Under the charger is another pull-out section which contains the 5 different Micro-USB Cables and they are bundled by size: 2 cables 1 foot long end-to-end, 1 cable just under 3 feet end-to-end, and 1 cable just under 6 feet end-to-end. Also, a Welcome Guide and a Happy/Not Happy card that has Anker’s contact information. Those cards seem to be the standard with all Anker products lately.

Impressions
There is little that can be said in relation to this product as Anker has completely nailed it in regards to the PowerIQ technology. It is simple, you plug in your device and the charger will charge it in the fastest means possible. There are 5 ports that does this so you can charge 5 different devices simultaneously at their maximum speed. The device measures in at 3 ½” L by 2 ¼” W by 1” H roughly the size of a deck of cards albeit a little thick and weighs in at 5.2 oz. Other than the fact that you have a separate power cord, this is one powerful little charger and the power cord is actually a benefit as you can place this anywhere on your desk or night stand and have easy access to your USB ports. The exterior of the device has a soft-touch coating that really gives it a striking feel to it and the face of the device where the USB Ports are located does have a shiny plastic surface that is prone to fingerprints and really makes the device stand out when placed atop a desk. The cables are of really high quality for aftermarket cables with a plastic over mold and rubber stress relievers that are very stiff. Only time will tell how well these cables stand up to wear but at this point they seem like they will take some abuse. The beauty of it all is that Anker backs these with an 18-month warranty. My only gripe is the advertised lengths, the 1 footers do seem to be 1’ exactly from end to end but the 3 and 6 footers are both a couple inches shy of their advertised lengths so keep that in mind when you are trying to map out their reach, personally I like the lengths to match the advertisements as I am an exact kind of guy but these will be fine for most users.

Charging Performance
This charger is UL certified safe and at 40W 8.0A output power, rest assured that there is enough juice to go around for all your devices. My desk normally charges an iPad 2, iPad Mini, an iPhone 5S, HTC One, and even a Pebble Steel Smartwatch all with relative ease. I also charge many Anker products on my desk including the Portable Bluetooth Speaker (MP141), 2nd Generation Astro 3, and an Astro Mini all without a hitch so this product definitely delivers. The performance from PowerIQ technology is definitely much faster than its stock counterparts, all of my Apple devices charge much faster on this than the supplied chargers by almost 50%, the same applies to the Android devices that are being charged with even faster charge times.

Summary
Overall, I personally love this device and has been my daily driver quite some time as I purchased one when they first came out. The quality of the product is second to none and the fact that it is $49.99 MSRP is a steal for this much power from something no bigger than a pack of cigarettes. Trust me on this one, you cannot go wrong with this combo and I would rate this product as 5 stars out of 5.

title: Great sound and pairs instantly!
text:
As you can see in the pictures, the packaging of these is quite nice and professional. The earbud charging case is nice and shiny and feels great to hold. The earbuds are also nice to hold and feel just smoother and more solid than Airpods. A USB-C charging cable and a set of silicon covers was also inside the box along with the warranty card and detailed instructions.
Upon placing the earbuds into the case to charge for a few minutes, I really liked the digital power readout on the outside of the case. The case charged wirelessly with my Qi charging pad in my car and also by USB-C. When I took them out of the case, they powered on, and I selected "K6" on my iPhone, and they paired immediately. The sound was rich and deep when I listened to music at home and also in the shower since these are waterproof. The earbuds also help drown out background noise. Definitely a great pair of wireless earbuds!

title: Good sound and comfort at a great price
text:
These came with the case about 25% charged.
It didn't take long for me to charge them up to 80% and then take them out on a disc golf outing.
The outing went well. They sound fine, and I like that I'm able to hear my surroundings while listening to music.
The silicone add-ons that were included do make them a little more comfortable, but the buds won’t fit into the case with those on. They’re very easy to put on and remove (maybe too easy), but they’re also just fine without the silicone bits. So, it’s nice that they’re included, but they are 100% optional.
For the price, I think they sound just fine, I like that the case tells you how much charge it has, and they stay in my ears better than I expected them to while I’m out and about being active.

Last month I nearly jumped for a pair of Apple EarPods when this very site had them on special, but many review sites consistently mentioned Earpod’s mediocre sound (even for earbuds). So I found myself taking a chance on this set, which lets be honest, could pass for the Apple product based on appearance, and I am glad that I did.

The earbuds arrived wrapped well and in a sturdy, attractive box that should hold up to reasonable bumps and bangs. The box contained the earbuds, silicone covers x 1 pair, a charger/storage case, instructions, and a USB-A to USB-C charger cord. I was impressed that the earbuds case/charger used an USB-C plug, as most newer rechargeable devices now utilize this connection to allow for faster charging, and Android has had Apple on the ropes for years with their chargers.

The earbuds arrived partially charged, and when I placed them in the charger, they were at full capacity within half an hour. The case can be recharged without the earbuds inside, and based on my first couple of recharges, it seems to hold enough power for 3-4 recharges.

The headphones were lightweight and comfortable but here’s the kicker - they stayed in place. I put on some metal and did as much head banging as my 47 year old neck would allow, which wasn’t much, but these things stayed put.

The sound. (!) I know next to nothing about earbud speaker technology, but I know when music sounds clear and crisp. They handled the continuum of sound from base on up really well, and vocals weren’t drowned out by instruments. Now, these are not over the head earphones that completely cup the ears, but they deliver as good a sound as any earbuds I’ve tried, and some headphone sets. Operation was intuitive and commands are given by gentle touches to the earbud itself (no buttons). Well worth the price. 10/10. Would head bang with these again.

title: I like these!
text:
I purchased these earbuds in an attempt to look like the cool kids. Ha. Seriously though, these caught my eye for a number of reasons. I normally wear over the ear buds because the dang things fall out of my ear. These stay in! Woohoo! The price is more than reasonable, compared to some other sets available.

The ear buds slipped into their appropriate slots with ease, and started charging immediately. I really LOVE that these charge with a C-charger. One less cord to hassle with, since my phone uses the same charger. You can also wirelessly charge these on a charging pad, according to the directions. I’ve not personally tried to charge them that way.
In no time at all they were completely charged (they came out of the box at 52% and within 30 minutes were at 100%). I like that you can see the percentage charged on the outside of the carrying case. They paired with ease. Thank goodness. It’s been my experience that pairing is sometimes Just.Not.Easy.
The sound quality is very good. I can listen to music or watch YouTube or Netflix without any loss of sound quality or distortion.
